paragraphs.text: The fourth doctrine: That the effector in the occurrence of the act is the servant's power by way of independence. And this is the doctrine of the Muʿtazilah. Then these differed in several places:

والقول الرابع : إن المؤثر في حصول الفعل هو قدرة العبد على سبيل الاستقلال. وهذا هو قول المعتزلة (1) ثم هؤلاء اختلفوا في مواضع : فالأول : إن تأثير القدرة في حصول الفعل. هل هو موقوف على حصول الداعي؟ أما «أبو الحسين» فقد اضطرب قوله فيه. فكلما تكلم مع الفلاسفة في قولهم : لم خصص الله إحداث العالم بالوقت المعين ، دون ما قبله أو ما بعده؟ قال :
paragraphs.arabic: والقول الرابع : إن المؤثر في حصول الفعل هو قدرة العبد على سبيل الاستقلال. وهذا هو قول المعتزلة (1) ثم هؤلاء اختلفوا في مواضع : فالأول : إن تأثير القدرة في حصول الفعل. هل هو موقوف على حصول الداعي؟ أما «أبو الحسين» فقد اضطرب قوله فيه. فكلما تكلم مع الفلاسفة في قولهم : لم خصص الله إحداث العالم بالوقت المعين ، دون ما قبله أو ما بعده؟ قال :

paragraphs.text: The first: Whether the effect of power in the occurrence of the act is dependent upon the occurrence of the motive? As for Abū al-Ḥusayn, his statement is confused on this. Whenever he spoke with the philosophers regarding their saying: "Why did God specify the creation of the world for the particular time, rather than before it or after it?" he said: "The act is not dependent upon the motive." And whenever he spoke in the other questions with his companions, he said: "The act is dependent upon the motive, and that preponderance without a preponderator is null in the first principles of intellects."

«الفعل لا يتوقف على الداعي» وكلما تكلم في سائر المسائل مع أصحابه. قال : «الفعل يتوقف على الداعي ، وأن الرجحان من غير المرجح : باطل في بدائه العقول». وأما مشايخ المعتزلة فأكثرهم [لا يوقفون (2) ] حصول الفعل على الداعي. ثم إذا قلنا : إن الفعل يتوقف على الداعي. فهل يصير الفعل واجب الوقوع عند

Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ق-د-ر** | Word: القدرة | Definition: القوة التي بها يقع الفعل، وهي من صفات الله تعالى ومن صفات العبد على سبيل المجاز عند أهل السنة. "The power by which an act occurs; it is an attribute of God and of the servant metaphorically according to Ahl al-Sunnah."

2. **Root: ك-س-ب** | Word: الكسب | Definition: ما يقع بقدرة العبد من صفة الفعل لا ذاته، وهو اصطلاح للقاضي أبي بكر. "That which occurs by the servant's power from the attribute of the act, not its essence; a technical term of al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr."
3. **Root: أ-ث-ر** | Word: التأثير | Definition: إحداث الأثر في الغير، وهو إيجاد الشيء عن غيره. "Producing an effect in another; bringing something into existence from another."
4. **Root: ط-و-ع** | Word: الطاعة | Definition: موافقة الأمر، وهي صفة للفعل باعتبار مطابقته للشرع. "Conformity to command; an attribute of the act by virtue of its agreement with the Law."
5. **Root: ع-ص-ي** | Word: المعصية | Definition: مخالفة الأمر، وهي صفة للفعل باعتبار مخالفته للشرع. "Opposition to command; an attribute of the act by virtue of its contravention of the Law."

6. **Root: د-ع-و** | Word: الداعي | Definition: الباعث على الفعل، وهو ما يرجح جانب الوجود على العدم عند حصول القدرة. "That which impels toward the act; that which preponderates the side of existence over non-existence when power is present."

7. **Root: ر-ج-ح** | Word: الرجحان | Definition: زيادة أحد الطرفين على الآخر في الوجود، وهو شرط ترجيح الفعل على الترك. "The preponderance of one side over the other in existence; a condition for preferring the act over its omission."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: باب الفاعل والمفعول** | The construction "لم تؤثر في وجود الفعل" employs the verb with فاعل مستتر and جار ومجرور as متعلق بالفعل، following Sībawayh's principle that verbs of effect take their object via prepositional phrases when the effect is abstract rather than concrete.

2. **Rule: باب العطف والتقسيم** | The phrase "ثم هاهنا احتمالان" uses ثم for sequential enumeration and هاهنا as ظرف مكان مجازي for presentational deixis, following Sībawayh's rule that ثم indicates arrangement with interval, and that الإشارة المكانية may be used metaphorically for conceptual presence.

paragraphs.text: Know that the existent is either that which is spatially extended (mutaḥayyiz), or that which inheres in the spatially extended (ḥāl fī al-mutaḥayyiz), or that which is neither spatially extended nor inheres in the spatially extended. As for the spatially extended: it is either divisible, and that is the body; or it is not divisible, and that is the indivisible part (al-juzʾ alladhī lā yatajazzaʾ), according to those who affirm its existence. As for that which inheres in the spatially extended, it is the accidents (aʿrāḍ) subsisting in bodies and substances. You have already known that accidents, according to the philosophers, are nine genera:
وأسرار الدهر والأزل». القسم الاول
paragraphs.arabic: وأسرار الدهر والأزل». القسم الاول

paragraphs.text: One of them is the category of quality (al-kayf). We say: it is of two types:
من الجزء الرابع في مباحث القائلين بالقدم
paragraphs.arabic: من الجزء الرابع في مباحث القائلين بالقدم

paragraphs.text: One of them: the accidents whose inherence is valid in non-living things.

في تفسير العالم

paragraphs.text: As for the first division, it is of five kinds:
أحدها : الكيف : ونقول : انه نوعان : أحدهما : الأعراض التي يصح (4) حلولها في غير الأحياء.

paragraphs.text: The first: what is perceived by the power of sight, namely colors and lights.
والثاني : الأعراض التي لا يصح حلولها إلا في الأحياء. أما القسم الأول : فنوعان : أحدهما : الأعراض المحسوسة بإحدى الحواس الخمس إحساسا أوليا.

paragraphs.text: One of them is life. As for the attributes that yield perception, they are of two divisions: the first: beliefs (iʿtiqādāt). They are either conceptualizations (taṣawwurāt) or affirmations (taṣdīqāt). The affirmations are either certain (jāzima) or not certain. As for the certain: they are either conforming to reality (muṭābiqa) or non-conforming. Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation
1. **Root: و ج د** | Word: الموجود | Definition: "That which is found/established in existence; the existent." — Lisān al-ʿArab: الوجود هو الكون الحاصل، يقال وجدت الشيء وجوداً إذا أدركته ووجدته.
2. **Root: ح ي ز** | Word: الحيز | Definition: "The place/region in which a thing is contained; the spatial locus." — Lisān al-ʿArab: الحيز الموضع المتسع، وكل شيء انضم إليه الشيء فهو حيزه.
3. **Root: ج س م** | Word: الجسم | Definition: "The body; that which is extended and divisible in three dimensions." — Lisān al-ʿArab: الجسم هو الطول والعرض والعمق، والجسمانة المقدار.
4. **Root: ق س م** | Word: القسمة | Definition: "Division; the act of separating a whole into parts." — Lisān al-ʿArab: القسمة تفريق الشيء، وانقسم الشيء صار أقساماً.
5. **Root: ج و ه ر** | Word: الجوهر | Definition: "The substance; the self-subsistent entity that occupies space." — Lisān al-ʿArab: الجوهر هو الذي لا يقبل القسمة ولا العرض، وهو قوام الشيء.
6. **Root: ح ر ك** | Word: الحركة | Definition: "Motion; the first occurrence of a substance in a second locus." — Lisān al-ʿArab: الحركة انتقال الجسم من مكان إلى مكان، والتحرك التغير.
7. **Root: س ك ن** | Word: السكون | Definition: "Rest; the second occurrence of a substance in its first locus." — Lisān al-ʿArab: السكون ضد الحركة، وسكن الشيء إذا ثبت وقرّ.
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The Conditional Construction (الشّرط والجزاء)** | In the phrase "الموجود إما أن يكون متحيزا، وإما أن يكون حالا" — Sībawayh treats "إمّا" as a disjunctive particle governing a nominal predicate, where each clause stands as an independent alternative, requiring the predicate to be in the accusative via the implicit copula (كان الناقصة). The repetition of "إمّا" establishes mutual exclusivity, a structure Sībawayh analyzes in Kitāb al-Kitāb under bāb al-ʿaṭf.

2. **Rule: The Genitive Construction (الإضافة)** | In phrases like "أعراض القائمة بالأجسام" and "حصول الجوهر في الحيز" — Sībawayh's rule on the construct state (al-iḍāfa) requires the first noun (al-muḍāf) to be stripped of tanwīn and the definite article, while the second noun (al-muḍāf ilayh) determines its definiteness. The prepositional phrase "في الحيز" functions as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) or predicate (khabar), governed by the rules of taʿalluq.

paragraphs.text: As for the third division of the divisions of existents—namely, the existent that is neither spatially extended nor inhering in what is spatially extended—it has been established by certain proofs that God, glorified be He, is such. But has there occurred among possible beings an existent of this description, or not? The philosophers affirmed it, and the theologians denied it. Yet the theologians have no proof demonstrating the corruption of this division. Their proof for the temporal origination of the world only addresses spatially extended things and the accidents subsisting in them, and does not address this third division. Thus, their claim that everything other than God is temporally originated is only completed either by refuting this third division, or by adducing a proof demonstrating the temporal origination of this third division, assuming its existence. Since they did not mention anything in these two positions, their discourse remains incomplete regarding the intended conclusion.

يثبت بالدليل أن المحدث يمتنع أن يحدث إلا لمحدث وموجود ، فإنه لا يثبت أن المحدث لا بد وأن يكون مسبوقا بوجود غيره. أما سواء قلنا : إن المحدث يحدث لنفسه أو لغيره ، أولا لنفسه ولا لغيره ، فإنه يجب أن يكون مسبوقا بالعدم. فيثبت : أن التفسير المحدث بأنه الذي يجب أن يكون مسبوقا بالعدم أولى من تفسيره بأنه الذي يجب أن يكون مسبوقا بغيره ، وإذا عرفت هذا فنقول : قد

paragraphs.text: We say: There is no doubt that the temporally originated cannot be interpreted except as that which another thing preceded. Then either that predecessor is non-existence or existence. If it is non-existence, then it is said: The temporally originated is that whose existence is preceded by non-existence. And if that predecessor is existence, then it is said: The temporally originated is that which the existence of another thing preceded. The first interpretation is more appropriate, because the temporally originated, insofar as it is temporally originated, must have its existence preceded by its own non-existence, and it is not necessary, insofar as it is temporally originated, that its existence be preceded by the existence of another. For unless it is established by proof that the temporally originated cannot originate except from an originator and an existent, it is not established that the temporally originated must necessarily be preceded by the existence of another. But whether we say that the temporally originated originates from itself or from another, or neither from itself nor from another, it must necessarily be preceded by non-existence. Thus it is established that interpreting the temporally originated as that which must be preceded by non-existence is more appropriate than interpreting it as that which must be preceded by another. And once you have understood this, we say: You have already understood in the book "The Judgments of Existents" that precedence and priority are of five divisions: The first: precedence by causality. The second: by essence. The third: by honor. The fourth: by place. The fifth: by time.

وإن كان المراد به التقدم بالذات ، فهذا مسلم. لأن العالم عندنا ممكن ، والممكن ليس له من ذاته إلا عدم الاستحقاق ، وله من غيره ثبوت الاستحقاق. وما له من ذاته ، سابق على ما له من غيره ، سبقا بالذات ، وأما التقدم : بالشرف والمكان ، فظاهر الامتناع. بقي التقدم بالزمان [فنقول : التقدم بالزمان (2) ] لا يحصل إلا مع حصول الزمان ، فإذا كان تقدم عدم العالم على

paragraphs.text: And once this is established, we say: If what is meant by non-existence preceding existence is precedence by causality, then this is impossible, because non-existence cannot be a cause of existence.

وجوده ، تقدما لا أول له ، وثبت أن هذا التقدم ليس إلا بالزمان ، وثبت أن التقدم بالزمان لا يحصل إلا مع حصول الزمان ، فهذا يقتضي قدم الزمان. ثم ثبت في الطبيعيات : أن الزمان من لواحق الحركة ، التي هي من لواحق الحسم ، فيلزم من قدم الزمان قدم الجسم. فيثبت : أن تفسير حدوث الأجسام بما ذكرتموه يوجب القول بقدم الأجسام ، فكان ما ذكرتموه من التفسير باطلا. هذا إذا فسرتم أن المحدث بأنه الذي يكون مسبوقا بالعدم. أما إذا فسرتموه بأنه الذي

paragraphs.text: And if what is meant is precedence by essence, then this is conceded. For the world, according to us, is possible, and the possible has from its own essence only the lack of deservingness, and from another it has the establishment of deservingness. What it has from its own essence is prior to what it has from another, with a priority by essence. As for precedence by honor and by place, their impossibility is manifest. There remains precedence by time. We say: Precedence by time does not occur except with the occurrence of time. So if the precedence of the world's non-existence over its existence is a precedence with no beginning, and it is established that this precedence is only by time, and it is established that precedence by time does not occur except with the occurrence of time, then this necessitates the eternity of time. Then it is established in the natural sciences that time is among the concomitants of motion, which is among the concomitants of body. Thus, from the eternity of time follows the eternity of body. So it is established that interpreting the temporal origination of bodies by what you have mentioned necessitates affirming the eternity of bodies. Thus, what you have mentioned of the interpretation is false. This is if you interpret the temporally originated as that which is preceded by non-existence. But if you interpret it as that which...
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ح د ث** | Word: الحُدُوث | Definition: كونُ الشيءِ بعدَ أن لم يكنْ، ضدُّ القِدَمِ؛ وهو وجودُ الشيءِ مسبوقًا بالعدمِ. (The being of a thing after it was not; the opposite of eternity; it is the existence of a thing preceded by non-existence.)

2. **Root: س ب ق** | Word: السَّبْقُ | Definition: التقدُّمُ والكونُ قبلَ غيرِه؛ يُقالُ سبقَه يسبقُه سبقًا إذا تقدَّمَه. (Precedence and being before another; one says sabaqahu yasbuquhu sabqan when he precedes him.)
3. **Root: ع د م** | Word: العَدَمُ | Definition: نقيضُ الوجودِ؛ وهو عدمُ الشيءِ في نفسِ الأمرِ. (The opposite of existence; it is the non-existence of a thing in actual fact.)
4. **Root: و ج د** | Word: الوُجُودُ | Definition: كونُ الشيءِ ثابتًا في الأعيانِ؛ نقيضُ العدمِ. (The being of a thing established in external entities; the opposite of non-existence.)

5. **Root: ع ل ل** | Word: العِلِّيَّةُ | Definition: كونُ الشيءِ مبدأً لوجودِ غيرهِ؛ والتقدُّمُ بالعلِّيةِ هو تقدُّمُ المؤثِّرِ على الأثرِ. (A thing being the principle of another's existence; precedence by causality is the precedence of the efficient cause over the effect.)

6. **Root: ذ ا ت** | Word: الذَّاتُ | Definition: حقيقةُ الشيءِ ونفسُه؛ والتقدُّمُ بالذاتِ هو كونُ الشيءِ سابقًا لغيرهِ لذاتِه لا لعلَّةٍ خارجيةٍ. (The reality of a thing and its very self; precedence by essence is a thing being prior to another by its own essence, not by an external cause.)

7. **Root: ز م ن** | Word: الزَّمَانُ | Definition: مقدارُ الحركةِ؛ وهو الذي يُقدَّرُ به تقدُّمُ الحوادثِ وتأخُّرُها. (The measure of motion; it is that by which the precedence and posteriority of events are measured.)
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The Conditional Construction (الشَّرْطُ وَالجَوَابُ)** | In the phrase "إن كان المراد بكون العدم سابقا على وجود التقدم بالعلية" (If what is meant by non-existence preceding existence is precedence by causality), Sībawayh establishes that the conditional particle "إن" governs a protasis (شرط) and apodosis (جواب), where the apodosis is the necessary consequent of the condition, and the verb of the protasis is past tense (ماضٍ) as a marker of supposition, not temporal past.

2. **Rule: The Distinction Between "أما" and "إما" (أَمَّا وَإِمَّا)** | In the text's use of "أما إذا فسرتموه" (But if you interpret it) versus "إما أن يكون ذلك السابق عدما أو وجودا" (Either that predecessor is non-existence or existence), Sībawayh distinguishes "أما" as the particle of disjunctive elaboration (حرف التفصيل) introducing a following clause, while "إما" is the particle of alternation (حرف التخيير) repeated for alternatives, each governing its own clause.

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say—and my success is only through God, upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn in repentance—the Imam, the Unique One, Fakhr al-Din Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn ʿUmar al-Khatib al-Razi, may God sanctify his soul, said:

Praise belongs to God (*al-ḥamd li-Llāh*), whose thoughts are bewildered at the origins of the lights of His Majesty (*kibriyāʾ*) and His Self-Sufficiency (*ṣamadiyya*); and whose sights are lost in the rising-places of the secrets of His Might (*ʿizza*) and His Uniqueness (*fardāniyya*). The very essences of created things bear witness to the perfection of His Power (*qudra*) and His Divinity (*ulūhiyya*), and the parts of the heavens and the earths indicate the utmost of His Knowledge (*ʿilm*) and the grandeur of His Wisdom (*ḥikma*). And blessings upon the Prophet of Mercy, Muhammad, and upon his family, companions, and progeny.

To proceed: When God Most High blessed me with access to the presence of the Sultan, the Magnificent, the Learned, the Just, Bahāʾ al-Dīn, the Sun of Islam and the Muslims (*Shams al-Islām wa al-Muslimīn*), the most noble of kings and the most just of sultans, Abu al-Muʾayyad Sām ibn Muḥammad ibn Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥusayn—may God adorn the foundations of his kingdom with all kinds of good things, and single him out in both abodes with the divisions of felicities—and made me among those who excel in love for him and loyalty to him, who seek shade under the shadow of his banner, and who are guided by his good oversight toward the furthest spiritual goals (*al-maṭālib al-rūḥāniyya*) and the ultimate psychic aims (*al-maqāṣid al-nafsāniyya*). And among the burdens of those great blessings and exalted ranks was that God Most High granted me success in refining the discourse on the explanation of the names of God Most High and His attributes (*ṣifāt*), and in verifying the statement concerning the interpretation of His descriptions and marks. So I composed this book, and I named it *The Radiant Proofs on the Names and Attributes* (*Lawāmiʿ al-Bayyināt fī al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt*), and I arranged it into three divisions: the first on the principles and preliminaries (*al-mabādiʾ wa al-muqaddimāt*); the second on the aims and goals (*al-maqāṣid wa al-ghāyāt*); and the third on the appendices and completions (*al-lawāḥiq wa al-mutammimāt*).

#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: س-م-و (s-m-w)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: "الِاسْمُ: مَا يُعْرَفُ بِهِ الشَّيْءُ وَيُدَلُّ عَلَيْهِ" (al-ismu: mā yuʿrafu bihi al-shayʾu wa yudallu ʿalayhi) — "The name is that by which a thing is known and indicated."

#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: The Distinction Between the Utterance and Its Referent (al-farq bayna al-lafẓ wa al-madlūl)**
*Al-Kitāb*: "وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّفْظَ لَيْسَ هُوَ الْمُسَمَّى، وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ دَلِيلٌ عَلَيْهِ" (wa-ʿlam anna al-lafẓa laysa huwa al-musammā, wa-innamā huwa dalīlun ʿalayhi) — "Know that the utterance is not the named thing itself, but rather an indicator of it."
ماهية المحكوم عليه والمحكوم به فنقول ان كان الاسم عبارة عن اللفظ الدال على
paragraphs.arabic: ماهية المحكوم عليه والمحكوم به فنقول ان كان الاسم عبارة عن اللفظ الدال على

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say: Know that the well-known position of our companions—may God Most High have mercy on them—is that the name (*al-ism*) is identical to the named thing (*al-musammā*), and distinct from the act of naming (*al-tasmiyya*). The Muʿtazila, however, held that it is distinct from both the act of naming and the named thing. The choice of Shaykh al-Ghazālī—may God be pleased with him—is that the name, the named, and the naming are three distinct matters (*umūr thalātha mutabāyina*), and this is the truth in my view.
الشيء بالوضع وكان المسمي عبارة عن نفس ذلك الشىء قالعلم الضروري حاصل بآن
paragraphs.arabic: الشيء بالوضع وكان المسمي عبارة عن نفس ذلك الشىء قالعلم الضروري حاصل بآن

paragraphs.text: Know that any assertion that the name is identical to the named or distinct from it must necessarily be preceded by an elucidation of what the name is, what the named is, and what the naming is. For every act of assent (*taṣdīq*) cannot but be preceded by a conceptualization (*taṣawwur*) of the essence of the subject and predicate. We therefore say: if the name is taken to mean the utterance (*al-lafẓ*) that indicates a thing by convention (*al-waḍʿ*), and the named is taken to mean that very thing itself, then necessary knowledge (*al-ʿilm al-ḍarūrī*) is attained regarding this [distinction]—namely, that the utterance is other than the thing it denotes, for the utterance is a sound composed of letters, while the named thing is the external reality (*al-ḥaqīqa al-khārijiyya*) that is indicated. This is a matter whose truth is self-evident to any sound intellect, and no one of sound reason can conflate the word "fire" with the burning substance itself, nor the word "water" with the quenching liquid itself. Thus, when the name is understood in this sense, it is unequivocally other than the named.

paragraphs.text: Chapter One: On the Demonstration that this Science is the Most Noble of the Sciences Absolutely.
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ش-ر-ف** | Word: أشرف | Definition: الأعلى مرتبةً والأفضل؛ يقال: شَرُفَ الرجلُ شَرَفًا إذا علا قدرُه وارتفع منزلتُه. (The highest in rank and the most excellent; it is said: a man is noble (sharufa) when his worth rises and his station is elevated.)
2. **Root: ع-ل-م** | Word: العلم | Definition: إدراك الشيء على ما هو به؛ والجمع علوم. (Apprehension of a thing as it truly is; its plural is ʿulūm.)

3. **Root: إ-ل-ه** | Word: الإلهي | Definition: المنسوب إلى الإله، وهو المعبود؛ وأصله من أَلَهَ يَأْلَهُ إذا عَبَدَ. (Pertaining to the Divine, the object of worship; its root is from aliha yaʾlahu, meaning to worship.)
4. **Root: ك-ت-ب** | Word: كتاب | Definition: الجمعُ المكتوبُ من الكلام؛ والكتابُ اسمٌ لما يُكتَب فيه. (The collected written discourse; kitāb is a name for that in which one writes.)
5. **Root: م-ق-د-م** | Word: مقدمة | Definition: ما يُقدَّم بين يدي الشيء؛ وهي الفاتحة والتمهيد للأمر. (That which is placed before a thing; it is the opening and preamble to an affair.)

6. **Root: ف-ص-ل** | Word: فصل | Definition: الفصلُ: الحاجزُ بين الشيئين؛ والجمع فصول. ومنه فصلُ الخطاب. (The divider between two things; its plural is fuṣūl. From it derives faṣl al-khiṭāb, decisive speech.)

7. **Root: ر-ت-ب** | Word: مرتب | Definition: من الترتيب، وهو تنزيل الأشياء في مراتبها ومنازلها على نظامٍ معلوم. (From tartīb, which is the arrangement of things in their ranks and stations according to a known order.)
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: Al-Basmala as an Elliptical Nominal Sentence** | The basmala «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» is a nominal sentence with an omitted predicate (khabar maḥdhūf), estimated as "my recitation begins" or "this book is written." Sibawayh treats such constructions as governed by an implicit verb or noun, following the principle of taqdīr (estimation) in Arabic syntax.

2. **Rule: The Conditional Clause with "wa-huwa" (The Wāw of Ḥāl)** | In the phrase «وهو المسمى في لسان اليونانيين», the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (the circumstantial clause), introducing a state (ḥāl) of the subject "kitābunā." Sibawayh rules that the ḥāl must be indefinite in meaning and governed by the preceding sentence, here functioning as an explanatory parenthetical.

Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation
1. **Root: ج-ز-م** | Word: الجزم | Definition: القطع بالشيء والحكم به حكمًا لا تردد فيه — "Decisive certainty in a matter, a judgment admitting no hesitation."
2. **Root: ي-ق-ن** | Word: اليقين | Definition: سكون القلب إلى الشيء مع زوال الشك والريب — "The heart's repose upon a thing with the elimination of doubt and suspicion."
3. **Root: س-ب-ل** | Word: سبيل | Definition: الطريق والمسلك، وجمعه سبل — "The path and route; its plural is subul."

4. **Root: ع-ق-ل** | Word: العقول | Definition: الحجر والنهي عن الشيء، وهو ما يميز به الإنسان ويدرك به الأمور — "Restraint and prohibition from a thing; that by which man discriminates and perceives matters."
5. **Root: ح-ص-ل** | Word: تحصيل | Definition: إدراك الشيء وإحرازه والوصول إليه — "Apprehending a thing, securing it, and arriving at it."
6. **Root: أ-خ-ذ** | Word: الأخذ | Definition: تناول الشيء وقبضه، ويستعمل بمعنى الاعتماد والاقتباس — "Taking hold of a thing and grasping it; used in the sense of reliance and derivation."
7. **Root: خ-ل-ق** | Word: الأخلق | Definition: الأحق والأولى والأجدر بالشيء — "The most worthy, most fitting, and most deserving of a thing."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The Interrogative Particle هل** | In Sibawayh's analysis, هل is a particle of inquiry (ḥarf al-istifhām) that seeks confirmation or denial of a positive proposition, and it governs the following verbal sentence without altering its syntactic structure, functioning as an operator on the entire clause.

2. **Rule: The Construction of أَمْ for Disjunction** | Sibawayh treats أَمْ as the disjunctive conjunction for exclusive alternatives (taqsim), where the second option is contrasted against the first, and the governing verb or particle extends its scope over both disjuncts equally.

paragraphs.text: The best of what has been said concerning it is: that he is the one from whom it is valid that he act at one time, and not act at another, according to the differing motives. The interpretation of motives is: that when a human being knows, or conjectures, or believes that he has in a certain act a preponderant benefit — then upon the occurrence of any one of these three, there occurs in his heart a firm inclination toward the act. For if his limbs are sound, then upon the occurrence of that inclination in his heart, that act issues from him. But if he knows, or conjectures, or believes that he has in a certain act a preponderant harm — then upon the occurrence of this knowledge, or belief, or conjecture, there occurs in his heart a firm aversion from that act. For if his limbs are sound, there follows upon the occurrence of that aversion, along with the soundness of the limbs: the abstention. And this is what is meant by the motive (al-dāʿī).

paragraphs.text: The First: On the explanation of the reason for which these three things are named "the motive" (al-dāʿī).
الأربعة لا بد من بيانها : ونقول : الأقرب أن يقال : المؤثر في الفعل هو مجموع القدرة مع الداعي. والدليل عليه : أن القدرة وحدها غير صالحة للتأثير على ما سيجيء بيانه ،

paragraphs.text: So we say: "Calling" (al-duʿāʾ) is a name for the specific utterance. However, when a human being knows, or conjectures, or believes that he has in a specific act a preponderant good, then that knowledge, or belief, or conjecture becomes a carrier for him upon the act. Thus that knowledge, or belief, or conjecture resembles being a caller (dāʿī) for him to that act. So this knowledge, or belief, or conjecture is named "the motive" (al-dāʿī) by virtue of this correspondence. And the motive may also be called "the purpose" (al-gharaḍ). The difference is: that the purpose is a name for that known or conjectured benefit. As for the motive, it is that knowledge or conjecture. And the philosophers call it "the final cause" (al-ʿilla al-ghāʾiyyah). And they also call it "the complete cause" (al-ʿilla al-tāmmah).

عند تقرير أنه عند عدم الداعي يمتنع الفعل ومعلوم أيضا : أن الداعي وحده غير صالح للتأثير. وأما عند اجتماعهما ، فإنه يحصل الأثر. فعلمنا أن المؤثر هو المجموع. فإن قالوا : قولكم القدرة وحدها غير صالحة للتأثير ، قول (باطل

paragraphs.text: The Second Investigation: That when the motive calls him to the act, the act occurs necessarily. Then here there are possibilities. The first of them: that the efficient cause in the occurrence of the act is the totality of power along with the motive. The second of them: that the efficient cause in it is the power conditioned by the motive. The third of them: that the motive is a complete cause, which makes the power of the capable one a complete cause for the occurrence of the act. And for this reason it is said: the final cause is a complete cause for the cause of the efficient cause. The fourth of them: that the occurrence of power and the motive is a cause for the occurrence of the complete preparedness for the emergence of that act from non-existence into existence. As for that very occurrence and origination itself, it is from the higher causes. So these four possibilities must be explained:

لأن القدرة عبارة عما يكون له صلاحية التأثير ، فقولكم : القدرة وحدها غير صالحة للتأثير قول) (2) بأن القدرة ليست مؤثرة. وهذا متناقض والجواب : إنا نعني بالقدرة كون الأعضاء بحالة متى انضم الداعي إليها حصل الفعل. وإذا كان المراد بالقدرة ذلك. فقد زال السؤال. فإن قيل : لم لا يجوز أن يقال :

paragraphs.text: And we say: The closest is to say: the efficient cause in the act is the totality of power along with the motive. The proof of it is: that power alone is not fit for efficacy, as will be explained later, when establishing that upon the absence of the motive the act is impossible. And it is also known that the motive alone is not fit for efficacy. But when they are combined, the effect occurs. So we know that the efficient cause is the totality. If they say: Your statement "power alone is not fit for efficacy" is a false statement, because power is an expression for that which has the fitness for efficacy — so your statement "power alone is not fit for efficacy" is a statement that power is not an efficient cause. And this is contradictory. The answer: We mean by power the state of the limbs such that when the motive is joined to them, the act occurs. And when what is meant by power is that, then the objection is removed. For if it is said: Why is it not permissible to say:
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ق-د-ر** | Word: القادر | Definition: "هو الذي يصح منه الفعل وعدمه بحسب الدواعي" — The one from whom an act is possible or not possible according to motives. (Lisān al-ʿArab: al-qadr is the measure and power by which one acts or refrains)

2. **Root: د-ع-و** | Word: الداعي | Definition: "ما يحمل على الفعل من علم أو ظن أو اعتقاد بمصلحة راجحة" — That which impels to action, whether knowledge, conjecture, or belief of a preponderant benefit. (Lisān al-ʿArab: duʿāʾ is calling; al-dāʿī is that which summons)

3. **Root: ص-ر-ف** | Word: الصارف | Definition: "ما يحمل على الترك من علم أو ظن أو اعتقاد بمفسدة راجحة" — That which impels to abstention, whether knowledge, conjecture, or belief of a preponderant harm. (Lisān al-ʿArab: ṣarafa means to turn away or divert)
4. **Root: م-ي-ل** | Word: الميل | Definition: "انعطاف النفس نحو الشيء" — The inclination of the soul toward something. (Kitāb al-ʿAyn: mayl is the bending or inclining of a thing)
5. **Root: ن-ف-ر** | Word: النفرة | Definition: "انزعاج النفس عن الشيء وإعراضها عنه" — The aversion and turning away of the soul from something. (Kitāb al-ʿAyn: nafara means to flee or shrink from)

6. **Root: غ-ر-ض** | Word: الغرض | Definition: "المنفعة المعلومة أو المظنونة التي لأجلها يفعل الفعل" — The known or conjectured benefit for the sake of which an act is done. (Lisān al-ʿArab: gharad is the aim or object of desire)

7. **Root: ع-ل-ل** | Word: العلة الغائية | Definition: "العلة التي لأجلها يوجد الفعل وهي الغرض" — The cause for the sake of which the act exists, namely the purpose. (Lisān al-ʿArab: ʿilla is the cause; ghāʾī relates to the end or final cause)
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The predicate of kāna and its sisters (kāna wa-akhawātuhā)** | In the phrase "أنه الذي يصح منه أن يفعل تارة" — the pronoun "هو" is the noun of kāna (in "كونه") and "الذي" is its predicate, both in the accusative position (ism kāna marfūʿ, khabar kāna manṣūb). Sībawayh establishes that kāna raises the subject and lowers the predicate, as in "كان زيدٌ قائماً" (Al-Kitāb, Bāb al-ism alladhī yufrad).

2. **Rule: The conditional construction with "إذا" (idhā) as a particle of time (ẓarf) requiring the apodosis (jawāb)** | In "إذا علم أو ظن أو اعتقد... فعند حصول أحد هذه الثلاثة يحصل في قلبه ميل جازم" — the protasis (sharṭ) is introduced by idhā, and the apodosis is introduced by fa- (the fāʾ of the answer), which Sībawayh mandates when the jawāb is a nominal sentence or a verb preceded by a particle, as in "إذا جاء زيدٌ فله كرامة" (Al-Kitāb, Bāb al-jazāʾ).

paragraphs.text: And branches derive from what we have mentioned:

القدرة والداعي يصدر الأثر عن سبب منفصل ، كما يقول الفلاسفة : من أن مجموع القدرة والداعي يوجب الاستعداد التام لحدوث ذلك الأثر ، وعند حصول هذا الاستعداد التام يفيض الأثر عن العقل الفعال؟ ويجب أن يتأمل في هذا الاحتمال ليعلم أنه حق أو باطل. البحث الرابع : إن قول القائل : القادر هو الذي يصح منه أن يفعل ، وأن لا يفعل بحسب الدواعي المختلفة كلام مشكل. وذلك لأن قولنا : إنه لم يفعل : إشارة إلى أنه نفي للعدم الأصلي ، كما كان. والعدم يمتنع وقوعه بالفاعل. لأن القدرة صفة مؤثرة ، والعدم نفي محض ، وسلب صرف. فالقول بأن العدم وقع

paragraphs.text: The effective agent is power (except that the joining of the motive to it is a condition for the issuance of that effect from power?) And the difference between the parts of the cause and that which is a condition for the cause's effect upon the effect is known. The answer: We do not mean by "source" and "effective agent" except the totality of things whose attainment is necessary so that it becomes a source for that effect. On this estimation, there is no difference for us regarding existential constraints between saying they are parts of the cause and saying they are conditions for the issuance of the effect from the cause. And know that with this amount which we have mentioned, it does not become apparent which of those four possibilities is the truth: what is it?

بالفاعل والقادر محال. (وأيضا : الشيء حال بقائه يمتنع إسناده إلى الفاعل. لما ثبت أن تكون الكائن محال) (2) وإذا كان الأمر كذلك فالعدم الباقي يمتنع إسناده إلى القادر. لوجهين : الأول : إن كونه عدميا يمنع من إسناده إلى الفاعل. والثاني : إن كونه باقيا يمنع أيضا من إسناده إلى الفاعل. فيثبت أن العدم الباقي يمتنع استناده إلى القادر من هذين الوجهين. ولما ثبت أن الترك لا معنى له. إلا البقاء على العدم الأصلي ، وثبت أن البقاء على العدم الأصلي يمتنع إسناده إلى الفاعل يثبت حينئذ : أن القادر لا قدرة له على الترك البتة. وإذا كان كذلك كان قوله : القادر هو الذي يصح منه الفعل والترك قولا مشكلا. ولهذا الكلام مزيد غور.

paragraphs.text: The Third Investigation: A speaker may say: Why is it not permissible to say that when the totality of power and motive is attained, the effect issues from a separate cause, just as the philosophers say: that the totality of power and motive necessitates complete readiness for the occurrence of that effect, and when this complete readiness is attained, the effect flows from the Active Intellect? And one must reflect upon this possibility to know whether it is true or false.

وحاول بعضهم أن يجيب عما يقرب من هذا الكلام. فقال : إن العاجز لا يجد من نفسه أنه إن لم يشأ الفعل فإنه لا يمكنه أن لا يفعل (وأما القادر على الفعل فإنه يجد من نفسه أنه إن شاء أن لا يفعل فإنه يمكنه أن لا يفعل) (1) وهذا الفرق معلوم بالضرورة. ولما كان العلم بهذا الفرق ضروريا. فحينئذ لا حاجة بنا إلى بيان أنه كيف حصل هذا الفرق؟ ولقائل أن يقول : هذا الجواب ضعيف. وذلك لأن ترك الفعل إما أن يكون أمرا زائدا على البقاء على العدم الأصلي المستمر ، وإما أن لا يكون كذلك. بل هو عبارة عن نفس ذلك العدم المستمر. والأول باطل لوجوه : الأول : إن على هذا التقدير يكون القادر قادرا على فعل

paragraphs.text: The Fourth Investigation: The statement of the speaker: "The capable agent is he from whom it is valid to act and not to act according to different motives" is problematic speech. That is because our saying "he did not act" is an indication that it is a negation of the original non-existence, as it was. And non-existence is impossible to occur by the agent. Because power is an effective attribute, and non-existence is pure negation and absolute privation. So the statement that non-existence occurred by the agent and the capable one is impossible. (And also: a thing in the state of its continuance is impossible to attribute to the agent, since it is established that becoming is impossible.) And if the matter is so, then continuing non-existence is impossible to attribute to the capable agent, for two reasons: First, its being non-existential prevents its attribution to the agent. Second, its being continuing also prevents its attribution to the agent. So it is established that continuing non-existence is impossible to attribute to the capable agent from these two aspects. And since it is established that abandonment has no meaning except continuance upon original non-existence, and it is established that continuance upon original non-existence is impossible to attribute to the agent, then it is established that the capable agent has no power over abandonment at all. And if it is so, then his statement "the capable agent is he from whom both act and abandonment are valid" is a problematic statement. And for this speech there is deeper profundity.

الشيء وعلى فعل ضده. ولا يكون البتة قادرا على الفعل وعلى ترك الفعل لأن فعل الضد فعل خاص. والفعل الخاص لا يكون تركا لمسمى الفعل ، وإلا لزم أن يكون أحد النقيضين عين الثاني ، وهو محال. فثبت أن على هذا التقدير لا يكون القادر قادرا البتة على الترك. والثاني : إن الله تعالى كان قادرا على خلق العالم وعلى تركه ، فإذا صار تركه مفسرا بفعل ضده ، فحين كان الله تاركا للعالم ، وجب أن يكون فاعلا لضده. فلما كان في الأزل تاركا لفعل العالم ، وجب أن يقال : إنه كان في الأزل فاعلا لضد العالم ، لكن الفعل الأزلي عند القوم محال. وأيضا : فعلى هذا التقدير كان ضد العالم أزليا ، والأزل لا يزول فوجب أن لا يزول ضد العالم. وإذا امتنع زوال ضده وجب أن يمتنع دخول

paragraphs.text: And some attempted to answer something close to this speech. He said: The incapable one does not find from himself that if he does not will the act, he cannot not act. (And as for the capable of the act, he finds from himself that if he wills not to act, he can not act.) And this difference is known necessarily. And since knowledge of this difference is necessary, then we have no need to explain how this difference occurred. And a speaker may say: This answer is weak. That is because the abandonment of the act is either something additional to the continuance upon the original continuous non-existence, or it is not so. Rather, it is an expression of that same continuous non-existence. And the first is false for reasons: First, on this estimation the capable agent would be capable of the act of a thing and of the act of its opposite, and would not be capable at all of the act and of the abandonment of the act, because the act of the opposite is a specific act. And the specific act is not an abandonment of what is named "the act," otherwise it would necessitate that one of the two contradictories be identical to the second, which is impossible. So it is established that on this estimation the capable agent is not capable at all of abandonment. Second: God Almighty was capable of creating the world and of abandoning it. So if His abandonment is interpreted as the act of its opposite, then when God was abandoning the world, it would be necessary that He be the doer of its opposite. So since He was in eternity abandoning the act of the world, it would be necessary to say that He was in eternity the doer of the opposite of the world. But eternal act according to the people is impossible. Also: on this estimation, the opposite of the world would be eternal, and eternity does not cease, so it would be necessary that the opposite of the world not cease. (The cause: that by which the state of a thing changes; in philosophy, that whose existence entails the existence of another thing.)

5. **Root: ش-ر-ط** | Word: الشرط | Definition: الشرط: علامة الشيء، وما يتوقف عليه وجود الشيء ولا يكون جزءا منه. قال ابن منظور: الشرط: العلامة، وجمعه شروط. (The condition: a sign of a thing, that upon which the existence of a thing depends without being a part of it.)

6. **Root: ع-ج-ز** | Word: العجز | Definition: العجز: ضد القدرة، وهو عدم التمكن من الفعل. قال الخليل: العجز: أن لا يبلغ الرجل الأمر. (Incapacity: the opposite of power, the lack of ability to act; failure to attain a matter.)

7. **Root: ع-د-م** | Word: العدم | Definition: العدم: ضد الوجود، وهو نفي محض وسلب صرف. قال ابن منظور: العدم: فقدان الشيء وذهابه. (Non-existence: the opposite of existence, pure negation and absolute privation; the loss and absence of a thing.)
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: باب الفاعل والمفعول** | Sībawayh states in Al-Kitāb that the agent (الفاعل) is that which performs the action, and the object (المفعول) is that upon which the action falls. In the phrase "المؤثر هو القدرة" (the effective agent is power), the predicate is made definite (معرفة) to assert identity, following the rule that when both subject and predicate are definite, it indicates complete identification (هذا باب الفاعل الذي يتعدى إلى مفعول به).

2. **Rule: باب الاستفهام بـ"هل" و"ما"** | Sībawayh discusses the interrogative particles, noting that "هل" is used for asking about the existence of a thing (طلب التصديق), while "ما" is used for asking about the essence or nature of a thing (طلب التصور). In the text's question "لم لا يجوز أن يقال" (why is it not permissible to say), the use of "لم" (why) follows the rule of asking for the cause or reason, which Sībawayh treats under the chapter of interrogation seeking justification.

paragraphs.text: We say (1): We find bodies differing in forms, yet similar in matter, such as the knife, the sword, the axe, and the saw. For all of them are made of iron, yet despite their sharing in this meaning, each one of them differs from the other in form and shape. So we say: These things have iron as their prime matter, and their forms are different. Likewise, the door, the bed, the chair, and the ship share in being made of wood, and differ in shapes and forms. When you have understood this, we say: Prime matter (2) is of four ranks: the prime matter of craft, the prime matter of nature, the prime matter of the whole, and the first prime matter.

أما [المرتبة الأولى : وهي (4) ] هيولى الصناعة. فهي كل جسم يعمل منه ، وفيه للصانع صنعة. كالخشب للنجارين ، والحديد للحدادين ، والتراب والماء للبنائين ، والغزل للحاكة ، والدقيق للخبازين. وعلى هذا القياس فكل صانع لا

paragraphs.text: As for the first rank, which is (4) the prime matter of craft: it is every body from which something is made, and in which the artisan has a craft. Like wood for carpenters, iron for blacksmiths, earth and water for builders, thread for weavers, and flour for bakers. And by this analogy, every artisan must have a body from which and in which his craft is exercised. So that body is the prime matter for that thing. And as for the shapes and engravings (1) which the artisan makes in that body, they are the forms.
بد له من جسم يعمل منه وفيه : صنعته. [فذلك الجسم هو الهيولى لذلك الشيء. وأما الأشكال والنقوش (1) ] التي يعملها الصانع في ذلك الجسم فهي الصور.

paragraphs.text: As for the second rank: it is the prime matter of nature. It is fire, air, water, and earth. That is because everything under the sphere (2) of the moon among generated things—namely minerals, plants, and animals—is only generated from these four, and to them it is transformed upon corruption.

وأما المرتبة الثانية : وهي هيولى الطبيعة. فهي النار والهواء والماء والأرض. وذلك لأن كل ما تحت [فلك (2) ] القمر من الكائنات أعني المعادن والنبات والحيوان فإنما يتكون من هذه الأربعة ، وإليها يستحيل عند الفساد.
paragraphs.arabic: وأما المرتبة الثانية : وهي هيولى الطبيعة. فهي النار والهواء والماء والأرض. وذلك لأن كل ما تحت [فلك (2) ] القمر من الكائنات أعني المعادن والنبات والحيوان فإنما يتكون من هذه الأربعة ، وإليها يستحيل عند الفساد.

paragraphs.text: As for the third rank: it is the prime matter of the whole. It is the absolute body from which the entirety of the corporeal world is obtained, namely the celestial spheres, the stars, the four elements, and the three generated beings.
وأما المرتبة الثالثة : وهي هيولى الكل. فهو الجسم المطلق الذي منه يحصل جملة العالم الجسماني أعني الأفلاك والكواكب والأركان الأربعة والمواليد الثلاثة.
paragraphs.arabic: وأما المرتبة الثالثة : وهي هيولى الكل. فهو الجسم المطلق الذي منه يحصل جملة العالم الجسماني أعني الأفلاك والكواكب والأركان الأربعة والمواليد الثلاثة.

paragraphs.text: As for the fourth rank: it is the first prime matter. According to some, it is the indivisible parts; according to others, it is a self-subsistent essence in which corporeality inheres, so from that self-subsistent (3) and that receptivity is generated the essence of the body. When you have understood this (4), we say: Our purpose in this book is to explain the states of the body insofar as it is a body, and to explain the first prime matter from which the body is generated. And God knows best (5).

وأما المرتبة الرابعة : وهي الهيولى الأولى. فعند بعضهم : هي الأجزاء التي لا تتجزى ، وعند آخرين : ذات قائمة بنفسها تحل فيه الجسمية [فيتولد من ذلك القائم (3) وذلك القبول : ذات الجسم. إذا عرفت هذا (4) ] فنقول :

paragraphs.text: The Muʿtazilites said: The body is that which is long, wide, and deep.

paragraphs.text: Know that the investigation into these two definitions (2) is branched upon whether the body is composed of indivisible parts. As for those who said that it is composed of indivisible parts, they said: It is that which is long, wide, and deep. Because when two composed substances occur in that body, length has occurred in it. And when two other composed substances occur and are joined to the first two, breadth has occurred in it. And when another surface composed of four parts in the described manner occurs and is joined to the first surface, then length, breadth, and depth have occurred in it. So it is established that every body is long, wide, and deep. As for those who said that the body is not composed of indivisible parts, they said: This statement is false. Because the simple body is in itself one thing, and is not at all composed of any parts. And if that is so, then length, breadth, and depth are not actualized in it in actuality, but rather causes are possible such that when they occur, length, breadth, and depth come to exist in the body. Then they branched upon this principle and said: The body may exist in concrete reality devoid of the line, such as the solid sphere devoid of motion. For in this body none of the lines exist at all. As for the surface, the body is not devoid of it in concrete reality, because every body is finite, and every...
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ه-ي-ل (H-Y-L)** | Word: الهيولى (al-hayūlā) | Definition: المادة الأولى التي منها يكون الشيء، وهي لفظ يوناني معرب، وتطلق على الأصل والجوهر الذي تقبل الصور — "The prime matter from which a thing is constituted; a Hellenized term denoting the substratum that receives forms."
2. **Root: ج-س-م (J-S-M)** | Word: الجسم (al-jism) | Definition: ما له طول وعرض وعمق، أو الجوهر المركب — "That which possesses length, breadth, and depth; or the composite substance."

3. **Root: ص-و-ر (S-W-R)** | Word: الصورة (al-ṣūrah) | Definition: الهيئة التي بها يتميز الشيء عن غيره، وهي الفعل المقابل للمادة — "The configuration by which a thing is distinguished from another; the actuality opposed to matter."
4. **Root: ص-ن-ع (S-N-ʿ)** | Word: الصناعة (al-ṣināʿah) | Definition: عمل الصانع في المادة لإحداث شكل مقصود — "The artisan's operation upon matter to produce an intended form."
5. **Root: ط-و-ل (T-W-L)** | Word: الطول (al-ṭūl) | Definition: امتداد الجسم في جهة واحدة من أبعاده الثلاثة — "The extension of a body in one of its three dimensions."
6. **Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-R-Ḍ)** | Word: العرض (al-ʿarḍ) | Definition: امتداد الجسم في الجهة الثانية من أبعاده — "The extension of a body in the second of its dimensions."

7. **Root: ع-م-ق (ʿ-M-Q)** | Word: العمق (al-ʿumq) | Definition: امتداد الجسم في الجهة الثالثة المقاطعة للطول والعرض — "The extension of a body in the third dimension intersecting length and breadth."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: Al-Ḥāl wa al-Maʿmūl** | The construction "إنا نجد أجساما مختلفة في الصور" employs the particle "إنّ" with its noun in the accusative (أجساما) and its predicate as a verbal clause (نجد), following Sībawayh's rule that the predicate of inna may be a jumlah fiʿliyyah, where the verb governs its object without requiring an explicit pronoun return when the meaning is clear.

2. **Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Maʿnā** | In "كالسكين والسيف والفأس والمنشار" the prepositional phrase (kāf al-tashbīh) governs a series of nouns in the genitive, and Sībawayh notes that when multiple items are coordinated after a single preposition, the governing force of the preposition extends to all, maintaining grammatical uniformity without repetition.

paragraphs.text: ...finite, so it must be encompassed by one surface or by surfaces in actuality. This indicates that the body is not disjoined in external existence from the existence of the surface, except that it may be disjoined from it in mental existence. For we are able to conceive of a body that is non-finite, until the proof establishes its impossibility. And if the surface were a part of the quiddity of the body, it would be impossible to conceive of the body as a body unless we apprehend it as finite — because conceiving the quiddity as disjoined from its parts is impossible. As for quantity and volume, although the essence of the body is not disjoined from them — neither in external existence nor in mental existence — yet it has been established by proof that they are other than bodyness. This is demonstrated by several aspects:

paragraphs.text: The second: Bodies are equal in bodyness and differ in quantities. That by which there is sharing is not that by which there is differing. Thus bodyness is other than quantities.

التخلخل والتكاثف. فههنا ذات الجسم الواحد باقية بعينها ، مع أن المقادير المختلفة متواردة عليها ، فوجب أن يكون المقدار مغايرا لذات الجسم. قالوا : فثبت بما ذكرنا : أن كون الجسم جسما ، أمر مغاير لكونه طويلا عريضا عميقا ، فامتنع تعريف الجسم بهذا الحد ، واعلم أنا بينا : أن بتقدير أن يكون الجسم مركبا من الأجزاء التي لا تتجزأ ، فإن قولنا : الجسم هو الطويل العريض

paragraphs.text: The third: It has been established by proof that the single body, while its essence remains, admits of rarefaction and condensation. Here the single essence of the body remains identical, while different quantities successively come upon it. Therefore it is necessary that quantity be other than the essence of the body. They said: Thus it is established by what we have mentioned that the body's being a body is something other than its being long, wide, and deep. Therefore it is impossible to define the body by this definition. Know that we have explained that on the supposition that the body is composed of indivisible parts, our statement "the body is the long, wide, deep" would be a sound definition. And these objections that the philosophers have mentioned are entirely invalid on that supposition.

paragraphs.text: As for his statement: "The body may exist devoid of the line, such as the sphere" — we say: This is false. For on the supposition that the body is composed of parts, the sphere must necessarily contain parts that are supposed to meet along a single direction, and that is the line. As for his second statement: "The surface is not necessary to the quiddity of the body in the mind, so it must not be constitutive of its quiddity" — we say: This poses a difficulty for your own view that the body is composed of matter and form, while people apprehend the body as being a body while being heedless of its being composed of matter and form.

ثانيا : «إن السطح غير لازم [لماهية (2) ] الجسم في الذهن ، فوجب أن لا يكون (3) مقوما لماهيته» فنقول : هذا يشكل على قولكم : بكون الجسم مركبا من الهيولى والصورة ، مع أن الناس يعقلون كون الجسم جسما ، مع الذهول عن كونه مركبا من الهيولى والصورة. وأما قوله ثالثا : «إن الفرق بين الجسمية وبين المقدار ، حاصل من الوجوه
paragraphs.arabic: ثانيا : «إن السطح غير لازم [لماهية (2) ] الجسم في الذهن ، فوجب أن لا يكون (3) مقوما لماهيته» فنقول : هذا يشكل على قولكم : بكون الجسم مركبا من الهيولى والصورة ، مع أن الناس يعقلون كون الجسم جسما ، مع الذهول عن كونه مركبا من الهيولى والصورة. وأما قوله ثالثا : «إن الفرق بين الجسمية وبين المقدار ، حاصل من الوجوه

paragraphs.text: As for his third statement: "The distinction between bodyness and quantity is obtained from the three aspects" — we say: Those aspects are all weak. As for the first: When we take a single piece of wax and shape it into various different forms — here, just as the single bodyness remains identical, so too the single volume and the single quantity remain identical. What changes and differs is the shape. For sometimes it becomes a sphere, sometimes a cube, sometimes in another shape. Thus the quantity is one in all moments, while what changes is the shapes and the transference of the parts of that body from one direction to another direction.

الثلاثة» فنقول : تلك الوجوه بأسرها ضعيفة. أما الأول : فلأنا إذا أخذنا الشمعة الواحدة ، وشكلناها بالأشكال المختلفة. فههنا [كما أن (4) ] الجسمية الواحدة باقية بعينها ، فكذلك الحجمية الواحدة ، والمقدار الواحد باقي بعينه. وأما المتبدل المختلف وهو الشكل. فإنه تارة يصير كرة ، وتارة (5) مكعبا ، وتارة (6) على شكل [آخر (7) ] فالمقدار في كل الأوقات واحد ، وأما

paragraphs.text: As for the second aspect — his statement: "Bodies are equal in bodyness and differ in quantities" — we say: Quantities too are equal in their being quantities in origin, and differ in bigness and smallness. Thus it would follow that quantity has another quantity.

المتبدل فهو الأشكال ، وانتقال أجزاء ذلك الجسم من سمت إلى سمت آخر. وأما الوجه الثاني : وهو قوله : «الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية ، ومختلفة في المقادير» فنقول : والمقادير أيضا متساوية في أصل كونها مقادير ، ومختلفة في الكبر والصغر. فيلزم أن يكون للمقدار : مقدار آخر. وأما الوجه الثالث : فهو بناء على أن الذات الواحدة ، قد يختلف مقدارها
paragraphs.arabic: المتبدل فهو الأشكال ، وانتقال أجزاء ذلك الجسم من سمت إلى سمت آخر. وأما الوجه الثاني : وهو قوله : «الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية ، ومختلفة في المقادير» فنقول : والمقادير أيضا متساوية في أصل كونها مقادير ، ومختلفة في الكبر والصغر. فيلزم أن يكون للمقدار : مقدار آخر. وأما الوجه الثالث : فهو بناء على أن الذات الواحدة ، قد يختلف مقدارها

paragraphs.text: As for the third aspect: It is built upon the claim that a single essence may have its quantity vary in smallness and bigness while that essence remains identical. But we have demonstrated by conclusive proofs in the chapter on motion that this is impossible. Thus it is established by these clarifications that the aspects upon which they relied in refuting the statement of those who say "the body is the long, wide, deep" are invalid statements — and God knows best.

بالصغر والكبر ، مع بقاء تلك الذات بعينها. وقد دللنا بالبراهين القاطعة في باب الحركة : على أن ذلك محال. فثبت : بهذه البيانات أن الوجوه التي عولوا عليها في إبطال قول من قال : [الجسم (1) ] هو الطويل العريض العميق : أقوال باطلة [والله أعلم (2) ]. ثم احتج القائلون بصحة هذا الحد : فقالوا : إنكم لما حددتم الجسم بأنه

paragraphs.text: Then those who affirm the soundness of this definition argued, saying: When you defined the body as...
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation
1. **Root: ح د د** | Word: الحد | Definition: "النهاية والمنتهى، والحد الفاصل بين الشيئين" — The extremity, boundary, or defining limit that separates one thing from another.
2. **Root: ج س م** | Word: الجسم | Definition: "القالب والخلقة، والجسد، وكل شيء له طول وعرض وعمق" — The mold, form, or corporeal substance; anything possessing length, breadth, and depth.
3. **Root: س ط ح** | Word: السطح | Definition: "الوجه الأعلى من الشيء والبساط، وهو النهاية السطحية للجسم" — The upper face or surface of a thing; the superficial extremity of a body.
4. **Root: خ ل ق** | Word: التخلخل | Definition: "تباعد الأجزاء وتفرقها بعد اجتماع" — The dispersion and separation of parts after being joined together.
5. **Root: ك ث ف** | Word: التكاثف | Definition: "اجتماع الأجزاء والتزاقها بعد تفرق" — The gathering and adhesion of parts after being dispersed.
6. **Root: ق د ر** | Word: المقدار | Definition: "مبلغ الشيء ومساحته، وهو الكمية المتصلة العارضة للجسم" — The measure or extent of a thing; the continuous quantity accidental to the body.
7. **Root: ع ر ض** | Word: العرض | Definition: "ما يقوم بالشيء ولا يقوم بنفسه، خلاف الجوهر" — That which inheres in a thing and does not subsist by itself, as opposed to substance.
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: باب النعت والحال** | The distinction between essential attributes (ṣifāt dhātiyyah) and accidental states (aḥwāl) governs how predicates attach to subjects — here, "the body is long, wide, deep" functions as an essential predication (ḥaml dhātī) versus accidental qualification.

2. **Rule: باب الاشتقاق والفرق بين المصدر والاسم** | Sībawayh's rule on derived nouns (mushtaqqāt) versus primary nouns clarifies that "bodyness" (jismiyyah) is a primary essence-term, while "long, wide, deep" are derived attributive forms — a grammatical distinction mirroring the ontological one al-Rāzī draws.

#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: ق د س (Q-D-S)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: القدس: الطهارة، والتقديس: التنزيه والتطهير، يقال: قدّسته تقديساً أي طهّرته ونزّهته (al-quds: purity; al-taqdīs: sanctification and purification; one says "qaddastuhu taqdīsan," i.e., I purified and exalted him)

#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Ṣifāt (العطف على الصفات)**
*Al-Kitāb*: هذا باب العطف على الصفات، تقول: مررت برجلٍ كريمٍ طويلٍ، فتنصب على الموضع أو ترفع على الابتداء (This is the chapter on coordinating adjectives; you say: "I passed by a man, generous and tall," and you may put it in the accusative by position or nominative by resumption)
ونصرة الصراط المستقيم فأرت أن أتحفه بتحفة سنية وهدية مرضية
paragraphs.arabic: ونصرة الصراط المستقيم فأرت أن أتحفه بتحفة سنية وهدية مرضية

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say — the Shaykh, the Imām, Fakhr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Rāzī, may God envelop him in His forgiveness: Praise be to God, whose existence and permanence are necessary, whose change and annihilation are impossible, whose majesty is immense and whose exaltation is supreme, whose blessings and favors are all-encompassing — His earth and His heaven testify to His absolute oneness (tawḥīd). His attributes and names are exalted above any admixture of anthropomorphism (tashbīh) or nullification (taʿṭīl). Thus, His "istiwāʾ" (establishing Himself over the Throne) is His omnipotent subjugation; His "nuzūl" (descending) is His benevolence and giving; His "majīʾ" (coming) is His judgment and decree; His "wajh" (face) is His generosity — or His bounty — and His gracious giving; His "ʿayn" (eye) is His preservation, aid, and selection; His "ḍaḥik" (laughter) is His pardon — or His permission — and His good pleasure; His "yad" (hand) is His beneficence, honor, and choice. Nothing proceeds in the two abodes from His acts except what He wills and desires. Grandeur is His garment (izār) and majesty is His cloak (ridāʾ).
فأتحفته بهذا الكتاب الذي سميته ب أساس التقديس على بعد الدار وتباين
paragraphs.arabic: فأتحفته بهذا الكتاب الذي سميته ب أساس التقديس على بعد الدار وتباين

paragraphs.text: I praise Him for His abundant favors and beautiful generosity. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner to Him. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and messenger, whom He sent with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists detest it. May God bless him and grant him peace.
الأقطار وسألت الله الكريم أن ينفعه به في الدارين بفضله وكرمه ورتبته على
paragraphs.arabic: الأقطار وسألت الله الكريم أن ينفعه به في الدارين بفضله وكرمه ورتبته على

paragraphs.text: To proceed: Although I dwell in the farthest reaches of the Eastern lands, I have heard the people of the East and the West in unanimous agreement that the magnificent Sultan, the learned, the just, the holy warrior — the sword of this world and the faith, the Sultan of Islam and the Muslims, the most excellent of the Sultans of truth and certainty — Abū Bakr ibn Ayyūb — may his banners never cease ascending to the heavens' heights in strengthening the truth and the sincere doctrine, and may the traces of the lights of his power and authority remain through the succession of morning and evening — is the most virtuous of kings and the most perfect of Sultans in the signs of excellence, the evidences of sincerity, the strengthening of the upright religion, and the victory of the straight path. So I desired to honor him with a noble gift and a pleasing offering.
أربعة أقسام
paragraphs.arabic: أربعة أقسام

paragraphs.text: Thus I presented him with this book, which I have named "Asās al-Taqdīs" (The Foundation of Sanctification), despite the distance of abode and the divergence of regions. And I asked God the Generous to benefit him through it in both abodes, by His grace and bounty. I have arranged it into four sections.
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Notes

#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: ن ز ه (N-Z-H)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: "نَزِهَ الرَّجُلُ نَزَاهَةً، وَتَنَزَّهَ عَنِ الأَمْرِ: تَبَاعَدَ وَتَطَهَّرَ" (naziha al-rajulu nazāhah, wa tanzzaha ʿan al-amri: tabāʿada wa taṭahhara) — "The man was pure, and he kept himself far from the matter: he distanced himself and purified himself."
| في الدلائل الدالة على أنه تعالى منزه عن الجسمية والحيز

paragraphs.text:
#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: The Rule of Predication and Exemption (Ḥukm al-Isnād wa al-Istithnāʾ)**
*Al-Kitāb*: "وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْجُمْلَةَ إِذَا دَخَلَهَا حَرْفُ النَّفْيِ فَإِنَّهَا تَدُلُّ عَلَى نَفْيِ الْحُكْمِ عَنْ جَمِيعِ أَفْرَادِ الْجِنْسِ" (wa-ʿlam anna al-jumlata idhā dakhalahā ḥarfu al-nafyi fa-innahā tadullu ʿalā nafyi al-ḥukmi ʿan jamīʿi afrādi al-jinsi) — "Know that when a negative particle enters a sentence, it indicates the negation of the predicate from all individuals of the genus."

#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say: Know, may God guide you, that this first section is devoted to the proofs which demonstrate that He — exalted be He — is utterly transcendent (munazzah) of corporeality (al-jismiyyah) and of occupying a spatial location (al-ḥayyiz). By this I mean that His essence is not like bodies, nor is He contained within any place, nor does He have direction, nor is He subject to the limitations of space or time. For the term "corporeality" denotes that which is extended, divisible, and receptive of accidents; and the term "spatial location" denotes that which is bounded and circumscribed. Both of these are impossible for the Necessary Existent, whose existence is pure and free from all such imperfections.
وفيه فصول
paragraphs.arabic: وفيه فصول

paragraphs.text: This section contains several chapters (fuṣūl), which I shall unfold in due order, each one establishing a distinct proof from the Qurʾān, from reason, and from the consensus of the righteous ancestors (al-salaf). The first chapter will address the verses that negate any likeness or resemblance; the second will address the verses that affirm His absolute sovereignty and His encompassing of all things without being encompassed; the third will address the rational arguments that demonstrate the impossibility of His being a body or in a place; and the fourth will address the refutation of those who have fallen into anthropomorphism (al-tashbīh) by misinterpreting the ambiguous verses (al-mutashābihāt). In all of this, I rely solely on God, and to Him I entrust my affair.
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Notes
ن ز ه (N-Z-H)

paragraphs.text: Know that the deniers of prophethood are sects:
تقرير القول بالنبوة عن طريق المعجزات الفصل الاول في شرح مذاهب الناس في هذا الباب
paragraphs.arabic: تقرير القول بالنبوة عن طريق المعجزات الفصل الاول في شرح مذاهب الناس في هذا الباب

paragraphs.text: The first sect: those who said that the God of the world is a necessary cause by essence, not a voluntary agent. For whoever denies that He—exalted be He—is a voluntary agent, and denies that He knows particulars, the door to establishing prophethood is closed before him. This method is the method of the philosophers.

اعلم (1) أن منكري النبوات فرق : الفرقة الأولى : الذين قالوا : إله العالم موجب بالذات لا فاعل بالاختيار. فإن كل من أنكر كونه تعالى فاعلا مختارا ، وأنكر كونه عالما بالجزئيات. فقد انسد عليه باب إثبات النبوات و[هذه الطريقة (2) ] هي طريقة الفلاسفة.
paragraphs.arabic: اعلم (1) أن منكري النبوات فرق : الفرقة الأولى : الذين قالوا : إله العالم موجب بالذات لا فاعل بالاختيار. فإن كل من أنكر كونه تعالى فاعلا مختارا ، وأنكر كونه عالما بالجزئيات. فقد انسد عليه باب إثبات النبوات و[هذه الطريقة (2) ] هي طريقة الفلاسفة.

paragraphs.text: The second sect: those who conceded that the God of the world is a voluntary agent, but they denied command, prohibition, and imposition of duty. They said: Since this is established, the doctrine of prophethood is nullified. For the prophets—peace be upon them—only came to establish the impositions of duty. And since the doctrine of imposition of duty is, in their view, false, the root has become false; and when the root is false, the branch is even more deserving of falsehood.

والفرقة الثانية : الذين سلموا أن إله العالم فاعل مختار ولكنهم أنكروا الأمر والنهي والتكليف. قالوا : وإذ ثبت هذا ، فقد بطل القول بالنبوة. لأن الأنبياء عليهم السلام إنما جاءوا بتقرير التكاليف. ولما كان القول بالتكليف عندهم باطلا ، فقد بطل الأصل [وعند بطلان الأصل (3) ] يكون الفرع أولى بالبطلان.
paragraphs.arabic: والفرقة الثانية : الذين سلموا أن إله العالم فاعل مختار ولكنهم أنكروا الأمر والنهي والتكليف. قالوا : وإذ ثبت هذا ، فقد بطل القول بالنبوة. لأن الأنبياء عليهم السلام إنما جاءوا بتقرير التكاليف. ولما كان القول بالتكليف عندهم باطلا ، فقد بطل الأصل [وعند بطلان الأصل (3) ] يكون الفرع أولى بالبطلان.

paragraphs.text: The third sect: those who conceded that the God of the world commanded His servants with things and prohibited them from things, except that they said: the intellects alone are sufficient for knowing those impositions of duty. So there was no benefit in sending the prophets—peace be upon them.

والفرقة الثالثة : الذين سلموا أن إله العالم أمر عباده بأشياء ، ونهاهم عن أشياء إلا انهم قالوا : العقول وحدها كافية في معرفة تلك التكاليف. فلم يكن في بعثة الأنبياء عليهم السلام فائدة. الفرقة الرابعة : الذين قالوا : لا طريق لنا إلى معرفة نبوة الأنبياء ، إلا بواسطة المعجزات ، والمعجزات لا دلالة فيها البتة على صدق الأنبياء ، وإذا لم يوجد شيء يدل على النبوة إلا المعجز ، وثبت أن المعجز لا يدل البتة
paragraphs.arabic: والفرقة الثالثة : الذين سلموا أن إله العالم أمر عباده بأشياء ، ونهاهم عن أشياء إلا انهم قالوا : العقول وحدها كافية في معرفة تلك التكاليف. فلم يكن في بعثة الأنبياء عليهم السلام فائدة. الفرقة الرابعة : الذين قالوا : لا طريق لنا إلى معرفة نبوة الأنبياء ، إلا بواسطة المعجزات ، والمعجزات لا دلالة فيها البتة على صدق الأنبياء ، وإذا لم يوجد شيء يدل على النبوة إلا المعجز ، وثبت أن المعجز لا يدل البتة

paragraphs.text: The fourth sect: those who said: we have no way to know the prophethood of the prophets except by means of miracles, and miracles have absolutely no indication of the truthfulness of the prophets. And when nothing exists that indicates prophethood except the miracle, and it is established that the miracle does not indicate at all the truthfulness of the prophet, then at that point the corruption of the doctrine of prophethood necessarily follows.

على صدق النبي ، فحينئذ يلزم فساد القول بالنبوة. ثم إن القائلين (1) بهذا القول ذكروا في الطعن في المعجزات وجوها كثيرة. فالفرقة الأولى (2): الذين أنكروا وجود المعجزات ، قالوا : خرق العادات ممتنع في العقول [والفرقة الثانية الذين سلموا إمكان انخراق العادات ؛ إلا أنهم قالوا : لم يوجد دليل يدل على أن الفاعل لتلك الأفعال الخارقة للعادات

paragraphs.text: Then those who held this doctrine mentioned many aspects in attacking miracles.

paragraphs.arabic: ، هو الله سبحانه. والفرقة (3) ] الثالثة الذين قالوا : هب أن الدليل دل على أن فاعل تلك الخوارق هو الله تعالى ، إلا أنها مع تسليم هذا الأصل لا تدل على صدق المدعي للرسالة. والفرقة الرابعة الذين قالوا : هب أن المعجز يدل على أن الله تعالى صدق ذلك المدعي في دعواه ، لكن تصديق الله إياه في دعواه. لا يدل على كونه صادقا ، بدليل : أن القول بالجبر حق ، ومتى كان

paragraphs.text: The first sect: those who denied the existence of miracles. They said: the breaking of customary practices is impossible in the intellects. The second sect: those who conceded the possibility of the breaking of customs, except that they said: no proof exists indicating that the agent of those acts breaking customs is God—glorified be He. The third sect: those who said: grant that the proof indicates that the agent of those breaking acts is God—exalted be He—yet even with conceding this root, they do not indicate the truthfulness of the claimant to the message. The fourth sect: those who said: grant that the miracle indicates that God—exalted be He—confirmed that claimant in his claim, yet God's confirming him in his claim does not indicate his being truthful, by the evidence that the doctrine of compulsion (jabr) is true. And whenever it is thus, it is necessary to be certain that the agent of all base acts is God. And whenever it is thus, it is impossible to say: such-and-such act is base, so it is impossible for God—exalted be He—to do it. And when it is thus, it is not base for God—exalted be He—to confirm the liar.

كذلك [وجب القطع بأن فاعل القبائح بأسرها هو الله ، ومتى كان كذلك (4) ] امتنع أن يقال : إن الفعل الفلاني : قبيح ، فيمتنع من الله تعالى فعله ، وإذا كان كذلك ، لم يقبح من الله تعالى : تصديق الكاذب. والفرقة الخامسة من الطاعنين في المعجزات : الذين قالوا : هب أن المعجزات تدل على صدق المدعي ، إلا أنا ما شاهدنا ظهور تلك المعجزات ، وإنما الغاية
paragraphs.arabic: كذلك [وجب القطع بأن فاعل القبائح بأسرها هو الله ، ومتى كان كذلك (4) ] امتنع أن يقال : إن الفعل الفلاني : قبيح ، فيمتنع من الله تعالى فعله ، وإذا كان كذلك ، لم يقبح من الله تعالى : تصديق الكاذب. والفرقة الخامسة من الطاعنين في المعجزات : الذين قالوا : هب أن المعجزات تدل على صدق المدعي ، إلا أنا ما شاهدنا ظهور تلك المعجزات ، وإنما الغاية

paragraphs.text: The fifth sect of those attacking miracles: those who said: grant that miracles indicate the truthfulness of the claimant, yet we have not witnessed the appearance of those miracles. The utmost limit is only that people have reported that they occurred in past times. But report does not yield certain knowledge. The only thing possible in it is the attainment of conjecture. Because this matter is a certain matter, building its establishment upon a path that yields only conjecture would be false and corrupt. These five sects are those who attack prophethood by means of attacking miracles.

القصوى : أن الناس أخبروا : أنها وقعت في الأزمنة الماضية ، إلا أن الخبر لا يفيد العلم اليقيني. وإنما القدر الممكن فيه : حصول الظن. لأن هذه المسألة مسألة يقينية. فبناء إثباتها على الطريق الذي لا يفيد إلا الظن : يكون باطلا فاسدا. فهذه الفرق الخمس هم الذين يطعنون (1) في النبوات ، بواسطة الطعن في المعجزات.
paragraphs.arabic: القصوى : أن الناس أخبروا : أنها وقعت في الأزمنة الماضية ، إلا أن الخبر لا يفيد العلم اليقيني. وإنما القدر الممكن فيه : حصول الظن. لأن هذه المسألة مسألة يقينية. فبناء إثباتها على الطريق الذي لا يفيد إلا الظن : يكون باطلا فاسدا. فهذه الفرق الخمس هم الذين يطعنون (1) في النبوات ، بواسطة الطعن في المعجزات.

paragraphs.text: As for the fifth sect of those attacking prophethood: those who said: there have been transmitted from them (the prophets) states that are not befitting for the investigators to occupy themselves with, and that necessitates attacking their being messengers from God—exalted be He.

وأما الفرقة الخامسة من الطاعنين في النبوات : الذين قالوا : إنه نقل عنهم أحوال لا يليق بالمحققين الاشتغال بها ، وذلك يوجب الطعن في كونهم رسلا من عند الله تعالى. والفرقة السادسة : الذين قالوا : لو أراد الله تعالى إرسال الرسل ، لكان يجب أن يكون رسولا من الملائكة ، وأن يظهر عليه معجزات قاهرة متوالية. وهذا القول حكاه الله تعالى في القرآن مرارا متوالية كثيرة.
paragraphs.arabic: وأما الفرقة الخامسة من الطاعنين في النبوات : الذين قالوا : إنه نقل عنهم أحوال لا يليق بالمحققين الاشتغال بها ، وذلك يوجب الطعن في كونهم رسلا من عند الله تعالى. والفرقة السادسة : الذين قالوا : لو أراد الله تعالى إرسال الرسل ، لكان يجب أن يكون رسولا من الملائكة ، وأن يظهر عليه معجزات قاهرة متوالية. وهذا القول حكاه الله تعالى في القرآن مرارا متوالية كثيرة.

paragraphs.text: The sixth sect: those who said: if God—exalted be He—had intended to send messengers, it would be necessary that the messenger be from the angels, and that overwhelming successive miracles appear upon him. This doctrine God—exalted be He—has narrated in the Qur'an in many successive instances.
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ن-ب-أ** | Word: النبوة | Definition: الإخبار عن الغيب بإعلام الله تعالى؛ وهي مشتقة من النبأ وهو الخبر ذو الشأن العظيم. (Prophethood: informing of the unseen by God's notification; derived from naba', which is news of great import.)

2. **Root: ك-ف-ر** | Word: الكفر | Definition: التغطية والستر؛ والكفار ستروا الحقائق وجحدوا ما أرسل به الأنبياء. (Disbelief: covering and veiling; the disbelievers concealed the truths and denied what the prophets were sent with.)

3. **Root: ف-ع-ل** | Word: الفاعل | Definition: من يصدر عنه الفعل باختيار وقدرة؛ والفاعل المختار خلاف الموجب بالذات. (Agent: one from whom the act proceeds by choice and power; the voluntary agent as opposed to the necessary cause.)

4. **Root: ع-ج-ز** | Word: المعجزة | Definition: أمر خارق للعادة مقرون بالتحدي سالم عن المعارضة؛ يدل على صدق مدعي النبوة. (Miracle: an affair breaking customary practice, coupled with challenge, free from opposition; indicating the truthfulness of the claimant to prophethood.)

5. **Root: خ-ر-ق** | Word: الخرق | Definition: القطع والإزالة؛ وانخراق العادة هو خروج الأمر عن جريان العادة المعتادة. (Rending: cutting and removal; the breaking of custom is the departure of an affair from the customary course.)

6. **Root: خ-ب-ر** | Word: الخبر | Definition: ما يحتمل الصدق والكذب لذاته؛ والمراد به هنا النقل المتواتر أو الآحاد. (Report: that which admits of truth and falsehood in itself; intended here as transmitted narration, whether mutawātir or solitary.)

7. **Root: ت-ك-ل-ف** | Word: التكليف | Definition: إلزام ما فيه كلفة ومشقة من الأمر والنهي؛ وهو خطاب الله تعالى للعباد بما يقتضي فعلًا أو تركًا. (Imposition of duty: obligating what involves burden and hardship of command and prohibition; it is God's address to servants regarding what requires doing or abandoning.)

paragraphs.text: Know that the deniers of moral obligation (taklīf) are two factions:

جانب الترك ، إما أن يتوقف على مرجح ، أولا يتوقف. فإن توقف على مرجح ، فذلك المرجح إن كان من العبد عاد التقسيم الأول فيه ، وإن كان من غيره ، فحينئذ يلزم الجبر ، وأما إن حصل ذلك الترجيح لا لمرجح ، أو يقال

paragraphs.text: Among them are those who build this denial upon the doctrine of compulsion (jabr), and among them are those who deny moral obligation not by building upon jabr but rather by other paths.
