paragraphs.text: Know that the discourse on establishing it will come exhaustively in a separate book. However, we shall now mention aspects by way of brevity:

على كل التقديرات. هذا إذا قلنا : إن المتمكن من الفعل [متمكن أيضا من الترك. وأما القسم الثاني وهو أن يقال : المتمكن من الفعل غير متمكن من الترك (1) ] فههنا الجبر أظهر وألزم. فيثبت : أن القول بالجبر لازم على كل
paragraphs.arabic: على كل التقديرات. هذا إذا قلنا : إن المتمكن من الفعل [متمكن أيضا من الترك. وأما القسم الثاني وهو أن يقال : المتمكن من الفعل غير متمكن من الترك (1) ] فههنا الجبر أظهر وألزم. فيثبت : أن القول بالجبر لازم على كل

paragraphs.text: **The First Aspect:** The one who is capable of an act—either he is capable of refraining from it or he is not. If the one capable of the act is capable of refraining from it, then the preponderance of the side of the act over the side of refraining—either it depends upon a preferentiator (murajjih) or it does not depend. If it depends upon a preferentiator, then if that preferentiator is from the servant, the first division returns upon it; and if it is from other than him, then compulsion (jabr) necessarily follows. But if that preponderance occurs without a preferentiator—or it is said that the side of the act is preponderant over the side of refraining with no preferentiator at all—then this is false for two reasons:

الأقسام. الحجة الثانية : إن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك البتة. وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، كانت القدرة موجبة للفعل ، فكان الجبر لازما. وإنما قلنا : إن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك : لأن الترك عبارة عن البقاء
paragraphs.arabic: الأقسام. الحجة الثانية : إن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك البتة. وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، كانت القدرة موجبة للفعل ، فكان الجبر لازما. وإنما قلنا : إن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك : لأن الترك عبارة عن البقاء

paragraphs.text: **The First:** It entails the preponderance of one of the two sides of the possible over the other without a preferentiator, and that prevents the inference from the origination of originated things and from the possibility of possible things to the existence of the Maker. And if the doctrine of the Maker is false, then the falsity of the doctrine of moral obligation and prophethood is even more necessary.

على العدم الأصلي. والعدم لا يصلح أن يكون مقدورا للقادر ، لأن القدرة صفة مؤثرة والعدم نفي محض [وعدم صرف (1) ] فيمتنع جعله أثرا للقدرة ، ولأن الشيء حال بقائه ، يمتنع كونه واقعا بالغير ، وإلا لزم تحصيل الحاصل ،
paragraphs.arabic: على العدم الأصلي. والعدم لا يصلح أن يكون مقدورا للقادر ، لأن القدرة صفة مؤثرة والعدم نفي محض [وعدم صرف (1) ] فيمتنع جعله أثرا للقدرة ، ولأن الشيء حال بقائه ، يمتنع كونه واقعا بالغير ، وإلا لزم تحصيل الحاصل ،

paragraphs.text: **The Second:** On this supposition, the preponderance of the side of the act over the side of refraining would be pure coincidence. And whatever is like that, its occurrence would not be more fitting than its refraining. Rather, if its occurrence happens to coincide, then it occurs—whether that agent willed that act or refused. And if its occurrence does not happen to coincide, it does not occur—whether that agent willed that act or refused. And this is pure jabr. Thus it is established: that the preponderance of one of the two sides over the other—if it depends upon a preferentiator, then the doctrine of jabr is necessary; and if it does not depend, then the doctrine of jabr is even more necessary. Thus it is established that the doctrine of jabr is necessary on all suppositions. This is if we say that the one capable of the act is also capable of refraining. As for the second division—which is to say that the one capable of the act is not capable of refraining—here jabr is more apparent and more necessary. Thus it is established that the doctrine of jabr is necessary in all divisions.

وهو محال (2) [فقد حصل في العدم الباقي وجهان كل واحد منهما يمنع من كونه مقدورا. وذلك محال] وإذا كان كذلك يثبت : أن الترك يمتنع أن يكون مقدورا. فيثبت أن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك. وإذا كان كذلك كانت
paragraphs.arabic: وهو محال (2) [فقد حصل في العدم الباقي وجهان كل واحد منهما يمنع من كونه مقدورا. وذلك محال] وإذا كان كذلك يثبت : أن الترك يمتنع أن يكون مقدورا. فيثبت أن القادر على الفعل ، لا قدرة له على الترك. وإذا كان كذلك كانت

paragraphs.text: **The Second Proof:** The one who is powerful over an act has no power at all over refraining from it. And if the matter is so, then power necessitates the act, and thus jabr is necessary. And we say that the one powerful over the act has no power over refraining: because refraining is an expression for remaining upon the original non-existence. And non-existence is not fit to be an object of power for the powerful one, because power is an effective attribute, and non-existence is pure negation and sheer absence, so it is impossible to make it an effect of power. And also because a thing, while it remains in its state of existence, is impossible to be effected by another, otherwise there would be the attainment of the already-attained (taḥṣīl al-ḥāṣil), which is absurd. Thus there have obtained in the remaining non-existence two aspects, each one of which prevents it from being an object of power. And that is absurd. And if it is so, it is established that refraining is impossible to be an object of power. Thus it is established that the one powerful over the act has no power over refraining. And if it is so, then power necessitates the act, and that necessitates the doctrine of jabr.

القدرة موجبة [للترك (3) ] وذلك يوجب القول بالجبر. الحجة الثالثة : إنه لو حصلت القدرة على الفعل ، لحصلت إما حال استواء الدواعي إلى الفعل والترك ، أو حال رجحان أحد الجانبين على الآخر. والقسمان باطلان. فالقول بحصول هذه القدرة : محال. وإنما قلنا : إنه يمتنع حصول
paragraphs.arabic: القدرة موجبة [للترك (3) ] وذلك يوجب القول بالجبر. الحجة الثالثة : إنه لو حصلت القدرة على الفعل ، لحصلت إما حال استواء الدواعي إلى الفعل والترك ، أو حال رجحان أحد الجانبين على الآخر. والقسمان باطلان. فالقول بحصول هذه القدرة : محال. وإنما قلنا : إنه يمتنع حصول

paragraphs.text: **The Third Proof:** If power over the act were to obtain, it would obtain either in the state of the equal balance of motives (dawāʿī) toward the act and the refraining, or in the state of the preponderance of one of the two sides over the other. And both divisions are false. So the doctrine of the obtaining of this power is absurd. And we say that it is impossible for it to obtain—
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ك ل ف** | Word: التكليف | Definition: إلزام ما فيه كلفة ومشقة؛ وهو خطاب الله تعالى للعباد بما فيه تعب. / The imposition of what entails burden and hardship; it is God's address to servants regarding what involves toil.

2. **Root: ج ب ر** | Word: الجبر | Definition: إلزام الأمر وقهره؛ ومنه الجبر بمعنى كون العبد مجبوراً على فعله لا اختيار له. / The compulsion of a matter and its coercion; from it, jabr means the servant being compelled in his act with no choice.

3. **Root: ق د ر** | Word: القدرة | Definition: كون الشيء بحيث إن شاء فعل وإن شاء ترك؛ وهي الصفة المؤثرة. / The state of a thing such that if it wills it acts and if it wills it refrains; it is the effective attribute.

4. **Root: ر ج ح** | Word: الترجيح | Definition: إفضال أحد الطرفين على الآخر بمرجح؛ وهو جعل أحد المتقابلين أرجح. / Giving preponderance to one side over the other by a preferentiator; it is making one of two opposites more preponderant.
5. **Root: ع د م** | Word: العدم | Definition: نفي الوجود المحض؛ وهو مقابل الوجود ولا يقبل التأثير. / Pure negation of existence; it is the opposite of existence and does not admit effect.

6. **Root: ف ع ل** | Word: الفعل | Definition: إحداث الشيء وإيجاده؛ وهو ما وقع من القادر بالاختيار. / The bringing about of a thing and its origination; it is what occurs from the capable one by choice.

7. **Root: ت ر ك** | Word: الترك | Definition: الإمساك عن الفعل والبقاء على العدم الأصلي؛ وهو عدم الفعل. / Refraining from the act and remaining upon the original non-existence; it is the non-doing of the act.
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The conditional construction with "إن" and its apodosis** | In the phrase "فإن كان المتمكن من الفعل متمكنا من تركه" the conditional particle "إن" governs a protasis in the past tense, and the apodosis is introduced by "فـ" (as in "فرجحان جانب الفعل"). Sībawayh states that when the protasis is a nominal sentence or a verbal sentence with a past verb, the apodosis requires the "فـ" if it is a nominal sentence, as is the case here.

2. **Rule: The use of "إما" for disjunction (تقسيم)** | In "إما أن يكون متمكنا من تركه أولا يكون" the particle "إما" introduces a disjunctive division, and Sībawayh notes that "إما" is followed by the verb or clause it governs, with the second disjunct introduced by "أو" or by repeating "إما". Here the second disjunct is elliptically rendered as "أولا يكون" where the verb is understood from the first clause, a construction Sībawayh treats under the chapter of ellipsis (حذف) in coordinated disjunctions.

The Sermon of the Book
وخاتم الأنبياء والمرسلين
paragraphs.arabic: وخاتم الأنبياء والمرسلين

paragraphs.text: Praise be to God, the Cleaver of the dawn, the Creator of spirits and bodies, the Originator (fāṭir) of intellects and senses, the Inventor of species and genera—He who has no beginning to His eternity, no end to His generosity, no limit to His dominion, and no number to His beneficence. He created all things as He willed, without any helper or supporter, and He originated in creation without deliberation or reflection. The breasts of all things are adorned with the necklaces of His wisdom, and the faces of the living are illuminated by the stars of His grace.
صلوات الله عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وعلى أصحابه الأنصار منهم
paragraphs.arabic: صلوات الله عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وعلى أصحابه الأنصار منهم

paragraphs.text: He united the spirit and the body in the most excellent composition, and by His power He blended the subtle with the dense. He decreed every matter firmly and originated every act perfectly—a wondrous lesson and a reminder for every penitent servant.

I praise Him, and no praise can ever reach the fullness of His blessings; I glorify Him with His most noble attributes and His most honored names. And I send blessings upon His Messenger, the caller to the upright religion, the reciter of the Mighty Qurʾān, the awaited one in the prayer of Abraham—a prophet whom Jesus announced to his people in his time, whose name is embroidered upon the banners of the faith, whose station was elevated while Adam was still between water and clay. That is Muhammad, the master of the first and the last, and the seal of the prophets and messengers.
والمهاجرين وسلم عليه وعليهم أجمعين
paragraphs.arabic: والمهاجرين وسلم عليه وعليهم أجمعين

paragraphs.text: May the blessings of God be upon him, and upon his pure and immaculate family, and upon his companions—both the Helpers (anṣār) and the Emigrants (muhājirūn)—and peace be upon him and upon them all.

paragraphs.text: ### The First Chapter on Matters Pertaining to Knowledge and Theoretical Inquiry, Containing Its Questions (الباب الأول في المباحث المتعلقة بالعلم والنظر وفيه مسائل)

#### Original Arabic Text (النص العربي الأصلي)

paragraphs.arabic:
#### Original Arabic Text (النص العربي الأصلي)
الباب الأول في المباحث المتعلقة بالعلم والنظر وفيه مسائل

paragraphs.text:
#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: ع-ل-م (ʿA-L-M)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: العلم نقيض الجهل، والعلم: الفهم واليقين، والعالم: الذي يعلم الشيء على ما هو به (al-ʿilm naqīḍ al-jahl, wa-l-ʿilm: al-fahm wa-l-yaqīn, wa-l-ʿālim: alladhī yaʿlam al-shayʾ ʿalā mā huwa bihī) — "Knowledge is the opposite of ignorance; knowledge is comprehension and certainty; the knower is one who knows a thing as it truly is."

#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl wa Ṣilatuhu (The Relative Pronoun and Its Clause)**
*Al-Kitāb*: ومن ذلك قولك "الذي قام" فـ"الذي" اسم مبهم لا يتم إلا بصلته، والصلات لا تكون إلا جملًا (wa-min dhālika qawluka "alladhī qāma" fa-"alladhī" ism mubham lā yatimm illā bi-ṣilatihi, wa-l-ṣilāt lā takūn illā jumalan) — "Among that is your saying 'the one who stood'; 'the one' is an indefinite noun that is only completed by its relative clause, and relative clauses are only complete sentences."
الباب الأول في المباحث المتعلقة بالعلم والنظر وفيه مسائل
paragraphs.arabic: الباب الأول في المباحث المتعلقة بالعلم والنظر وفيه مسائل

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say: This is the first chapter, devoted to the investigations that pertain to knowledge (al-ʿilm) and theoretical inquiry (al-naẓar), and within it are contained several questions (masāʾil). Know that the term "knowledge" here is used in its most precise sense—that which is certain and corresponds to reality—as opposed to mere opinion or conjecture. The chapter's title signals that we shall examine the nature of knowledge, its conditions, its divisions, and the validity of theoretical reasoning as a means to attain it. The questions that follow will address the foundational principles upon which the science of theology (uṣūl al-dīn) rests, beginning with the definition and reality of knowledge itself, then proceeding to the proofs that establish the soundness of rational inquiry.

paragraphs.text: People hold two positions regarding time: The first is the position of those who deny its existence. The second is the position of those who affirm its existence.

بقاؤها بسبب أفرادها وتتالي آحادها ، وبغير كونها متعاقبة متتالية ، أن كل واحد منها وجد بعد العدم ، ثم عدم بعد الوجود ، وهذا المفهوم لا يقتضي إثبات موجود زائد على تلك الموجودات ، والعدمات. ومنها ما يكون بقاؤها بمعنى كونها مستمرة دائمة بأعيانها. وهذا المفهوم [أيضا (2) ] لا يقتضي إثبات موجود زائد. (ويدل على ما ذكرناه وجوه من الدلائل :).

paragraphs.text: As for those who deny its existence, they said: Existing things are of two kinds: Among them are those whose persistence is due to their individual parts and the succession of their units, and by their not being successive and sequential — that each one of them exists after non-existence, then ceases to exist after existence. And this concept does not necessitate affirming an existent additional to those existents and non-existents.

paragraphs.text: And among them are those whose persistence is in the sense of their being continuous and perpetual in their very selves. And this concept also does not necessitate affirming an additional existent. (And what we have mentioned is indicated by several proofs:)

كان هذا المفهوم يقتضي إثبات مدة وزمان لذلك الشيء ، فحينئذ يلزم افتقار المدة والزمان إلى مدة أخرى ، وزمان آخر. ويلزم التسلسل وهو محال. والثاني (4) أيضا باطل ، لأنه يقتضي أن تكون الأجزاء المفترضة فيه متعاقبة متوالية ، وحينئذ يصح في كل واحد من تلك الأجزاء أن يقال : إنه حدث الآن ، لا قبل ولا بعد. فلو كان الحكم على الشيء بأنه حدث الآن ، أو كان حادثا قبل ذلك ، أو سيحدث بعد ذلك ، يقتضي شيئا آخر يكون ظرفا له ، ويكون لأجل وقوع هذا الشيء في ذلك الظرف ، يصدق عليه بأنه حصل الآن ، أو في الماضي ، أو سيحصل
paragraphs.arabic: كان هذا المفهوم يقتضي إثبات مدة وزمان لذلك الشيء ، فحينئذ يلزم افتقار المدة والزمان إلى مدة أخرى ، وزمان آخر. ويلزم التسلسل وهو محال. والثاني (4) أيضا باطل ، لأنه يقتضي أن تكون الأجزاء المفترضة فيه متعاقبة متوالية ، وحينئذ يصح في كل واحد من تلك الأجزاء أن يقال : إنه حدث الآن ، لا قبل ولا بعد. فلو كان الحكم على الشيء بأنه حدث الآن ، أو كان حادثا قبل ذلك ، أو سيحدث بعد ذلك ، يقتضي شيئا آخر يكون ظرفا له ، ويكون لأجل وقوع هذا الشيء في ذلك الظرف ، يصدق عليه بأنه حصل الآن ، أو في الماضي ، أو سيحصل

paragraphs.text: **The First Proof:** This thing called time and duration — if it were existent, it would either be continuous in existence or passing away in existence. The first is impossible; otherwise, this very day would necessarily be the day of the Flood. Thus, on this supposition, it would follow that what occurs on this day occurs on the day of the Flood, rather before it, rather eternally. This is a contradiction. [Impossible.] Also: on the supposition of its being perpetually existent in its very self, it must necessarily be true of it that it was existent before and will remain existent after. So if this concept necessitated affirming a duration and a time for that thing, then it would follow that duration and time are in need of another duration and another time. And an infinite regress would follow, which is impossible. And the second [alternative] is also false, because it necessitates that the parts supposed within it are successive and sequential. And then it is valid for each one of those parts to be said: It occurred now, not before and not after. So if the judgment upon a thing that it occurred now, or was occurring before that, or will occur after that, necessitated something else that would be a container for it, and it is because of this thing's occurrence in that container that it is true of it that it happened now, or in the past, or will happen in the future — then it would follow that time has another time, ad infinitum, and that is impossible.

في المستقبل ، فحينئذ يلزم أن يكون للزمان زمان آخر إلى غير النهاية ، وذلك محال. الحجة الثانية : إنا نعلم بالضرورة أن الأجزاء المفترضة في الزمان لا تحصل معا ، بل حصولها لا يعقل إلا على سبيل التعاقب والتقضي. فنقول : إما أن يكون لشيء من تلك الأجزاء حضور وحصول ، أو لا يكون ، فإن كان الأول كان واحد من تلك الأجزاء حال حضوره غير منقسم [وإلا لحصل له نصفان ، ويكون النصف الأول سابقا على النصف الثاني (5) ] وحينئذ لا يكون الحاضر حاضرا.
paragraphs.arabic: في المستقبل ، فحينئذ يلزم أن يكون للزمان زمان آخر إلى غير النهاية ، وذلك محال. الحجة الثانية : إنا نعلم بالضرورة أن الأجزاء المفترضة في الزمان لا تحصل معا ، بل حصولها لا يعقل إلا على سبيل التعاقب والتقضي. فنقول : إما أن يكون لشيء من تلك الأجزاء حضور وحصول ، أو لا يكون ، فإن كان الأول كان واحد من تلك الأجزاء حال حضوره غير منقسم [وإلا لحصل له نصفان ، ويكون النصف الأول سابقا على النصف الثاني (5) ] وحينئذ لا يكون الحاضر حاضرا.

paragraphs.text: **The Second Proof:** We know by necessity that the parts supposed in time do not obtain together. Rather, their obtaining is not conceivable except by way of succession and passing away. So we say: Either some of those parts have presence and attainment, or not. If the first, then one of those parts, at the moment of its presence, would be indivisible; otherwise, two halves would obtain for it, and the first half would be prior to the second half. And then the present would not be present. This is a contradiction.

هذا خلف. وإذا ثبت أن كل واحد من تلك الأشياء غير قابل للقسمة ولا شك أن الزمان إنما يمتد بسبب تعاقب تلك الأشياء الحاضرة لزم كون الزمان مركبا من الآنات المتتالية التي يكون كل واحد منها [غير قابل للقسمة (1) ] ولو كان الأمر كذلك لزم كون الجسم مركبا من الأجزاء التي لا تتجزأ ، لأن القدر الذي يتحرك عليه المتحرك من المسافة في الآن الواحد ، الذي لا يقبل القسمة إن كان منقسما كانت الحركة إلى نصفه واقعة في نصف ذلك الآن ، [والحركة الواقعة

paragraphs.text: And when it is established that each one of those things is not susceptible to division, and there is no doubt that time only extends by virtue of the succession of those present things, it follows that time is composed of successive nows (instants), each one of which is indivisible. And if it were so, it would follow that body is composed of indivisible parts, because the amount of distance over which the mover moves in a single now (instant) that does not admit division — if it were divisible, then the motion to its half would occur in half of that now, and the motion occurring..."
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: ز-م-ن** | Word: الزمان | Definition: "وقت الشيء، ومقداره من الماضي والمستقبل؛ وهو اسم لمدّة تقع فيها الحوادث" — "The time of a thing, and its measure of past and future; it is a name for the duration in which events occur."
2. **Root: م-د-د** | Word: المدة | Definition: "الغاية من الزمان، وامتداد الشيء واستمراره" — "The extent of time, and the extension and continuity of a thing."
3. **Root: و-ج-د** | Word: الوجود | Definition: "كون الشيء ثابتًا حاصلاً، خلاف العدم" — "A thing's being established and present, as opposed to non-existence."
4. **Root: ع-د-م** | Word: العدم | Definition: "نفي الوجود وخلاف الوجود" — "The negation of existence, the opposite of existence."
5. **Root: ب-ق-ي** | Word: البقاء | Definition: "دوام الوجود واستمراره في الزمان" — "The permanence of existence and its continuity in time."
6. **Root: ت-ل-و** | Word: التعاقب والتتالي | Definition: "تتابع الأشياء واحدًا بعد آخر، وخلاف الاجتماع" — "The succession of things one after another, as opposed to simultaneity."
7. **Root: ق-س-م** | Word: الانقسام | Definition: "تجزئة الشيء إلى أجزاء، وقبول القسمة" — "The division of a thing into parts, and its susceptibility to division."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: الإخبار عن المعاني بالمصادر** | Sībawayh explains that abstract concepts like "الوجود" and "العدم" are expressed through verbal nouns (masādir) that function as predicates, as seen in "الموجودات على قسمين" — the nominal sentence structure with an implied copula, where the subject is definite and the predicate is indefinite, indicating classification.

2. **Rule: الشرط والجزاء في الاستدلال** | Sībawayh's treatment of conditional sentences (الشروط) governs the logical structure "لو كان موجودًا لكان..." — the use of "لو" for hypothetical counterfactuals, where the protasis (condition) is followed by the apodosis (result) marked by "لـ" (the lām of the answer), a construction central to theological argumentation.

paragraphs.text: في النصف الثاني من ذلك الآن ، فحينئذ ينتصف ذلك الآن] (2) وكنا قد فرضنا أنه لا ينتصف. هذا خلف. فثبت أن القول بكون الزمان مركبا من أشياء حاضرة ، كل واحد منها لا ينقسم ، يفضي إلى إثبات الجوهر الفرد ، وهو باطل. فكان القول بوجود الزمان باطلا. وأما القسم الثاني وهو أن يقال : إنه ليس لشيء من الأجزاء المفترضة في الزمان حضور ولا حصول البتة ، فهذا تصريح بنفي الزمان بالكلية ، لأن الماضي هو الذي كان حاضرا ثم انقضى ، والمستقبل هو الذي يتوقع حضوره وهو بعد لم يحضر. فكونه ماضيا ومستقبلا يتوقف على كونه

paragraphs.text: In the second half of that instant, then that instant would be halved. But we had already assumed that it is not halved. This is a contradiction. Thus it is established that the statement that time is composed of present things, each of which is indivisible, leads to the affirmation of the individual atom, which is false. Therefore, the statement of the existence of time is false. As for the second division, namely that it is said: none of the parts supposed in time has presence or actualization at all—this is an explicit affirmation of the negation of time entirely, because the past is that which was present and then elapsed, and the future is that whose presence is expected while it has not yet arrived. So its being past and future depends on its being present. If its being present is impossible, then its existence in the past and the future is impossible. And if no existence is established for it—neither in the present, nor in the past, nor in the future—then the affirmation of its existence is impossible.

حاضرا. فإذا كان كونه حاضرا ممتنعا ، كان وجوده في الماضي والمستقبل محالا. وإذا كان لا يتقرر له وجود ، لا في الحال ، ولا في الماضي ، ولا في المستقبل ، امتنع القول بوجوده. الحجة الثالثة : إن هذا الزمان. إما أن يكون حادثا ، أو قديما. فإن كان حادثا كان عدمه قبل وجوده ، وهذه القبلية لا تكون بالزمان ، لأن هذا الكلام إنما وقع في العدم الذي هو متقدم على وجود كل (3) الزمان ، وعند حصول هذا العدم لا يكون للزمان وجود فقد حصل معنى القبلية والتقدم من غير حصول

paragraphs.text: The third proof: This time is either originated or eternal. If it is originated, then its non-existence precedes its existence, and this priority is not by time, because this discourse concerns the non-existence that precedes the existence of all time, and upon the occurrence of this non-existence, time has no existence. Thus the meaning of priority and precedence has occurred without the occurrence of time, so we know that the occurrence of priority and precedence does not depend on the existence of time. But if we say: time is eternal, we say: this is false. And even granting it, the objective is attained. As for its being false, it is because the existence of time is not established except upon the succession of priorities and posteriorities, and this succession and alternation is change, whose essence necessitates that it be preceded by another, while the eternal, by its essence, precludes being preceded by another. The combination of the two is impossible, so the combination of the essence of time and the essence of eternity is impossible.

الزمان ، فعلمنا أن حصول القبلية والتقدم ، لا يتوقف على وجود الزمان. وأما إن قلنا : الزمان قديم. فنقول : هذا باطل. وبتقدير تسليمه ، فالمقصود حاصل. أما أنه باطل فلأن وجود الزمان لا يتقرر إلا عند توالي القبليات [والبعديات] (4) وهذا التوالي والتعاقب هو التغير [والتغير (5) ] ماهيته ، تقتضي أن تكون مسبوقة بالغير ، والأزلي [ماهيته (1) ] تنافي المسبوقية بالغير ، والجمع بينهما محال ، فكان الجمع بين حقيقة الزمان ، وبين حقيقة الأزلية (2) محالا (3).
paragraphs.arabic: الزمان ، فعلمنا أن حصول القبلية والتقدم ، لا يتوقف على وجود الزمان. وأما إن قلنا : الزمان قديم. فنقول : هذا باطل. وبتقدير تسليمه ، فالمقصود حاصل. أما أنه باطل فلأن وجود الزمان لا يتقرر إلا عند توالي القبليات [والبعديات] (4) وهذا التوالي والتعاقب هو التغير [والتغير (5) ] ماهيته ، تقتضي أن تكون مسبوقة بالغير ، والأزلي [ماهيته (1) ] تنافي المسبوقية بالغير ، والجمع بينهما محال ، فكان الجمع بين حقيقة الزمان ، وبين حقيقة الأزلية (2) محالا (3).

paragraphs.text: As for the demonstration that even granting it, the objective is attained, its exposition is: the eternal is that which persists forever and ever. Just as the originated suggests the affirmation of two successive times, in the first of which occurs the non-existence of the thing and in the second its existence, so likewise the eternal suggests the existence of a continuous time from eternity to eternity, in which that eternal thing occurs. And if we judged time to be eternal, that judgment would suggest the occurrence of that time within another time. If this suggestion is false, then let such a suggestion be false likewise on the side of origination, for there is no difference in reason between the two cases. Then the upshot of the discourse returns to: a thing's being continuous and its being changing, even if it suggests the existence of a time that is a container and receptacle for that continuity at one time and for that change at another, yet that suggestion is corrupt and that imagination is false, and that necessitates the decisive affirmation of the negation of time. And that is what is sought.

وأما بيان أن بتقدير تسليمه. فالمقصود حاصل. فتقريره : أن القديم هو المستمر أزلا وأبدا ، وكما أن الحدث يوهم إثبات زمانين متعاقبين ، حصل في أولهما عدم الشيء ، وفي ثانيهما وجوده ، فكذلك القديم يوهم وجود زمان مستمر من الأزل إلى الأبد ، حصل فيه ذلك القديم ، ولو حكمنا على الزمان بالقدم ، لأوهم ذلك الحكم وقوع ذلك الزمان في زمان آخر ، فإن كان هذا الوهم كاذبا ، فليكن مثل هذا الوهم كاذبا أيضا في جانب الحدوث ، فإنه لا فرق في العقل بين البابين ، وحينئذ يرجع حاصل الكلام إلى أن كون الشيء مستمرا ، وكونه متغيرا
paragraphs.arabic: وأما بيان أن بتقدير تسليمه. فالمقصود حاصل. فتقريره : أن القديم هو المستمر أزلا وأبدا ، وكما أن الحدث يوهم إثبات زمانين متعاقبين ، حصل في أولهما عدم الشيء ، وفي ثانيهما وجوده ، فكذلك القديم يوهم وجود زمان مستمر من الأزل إلى الأبد ، حصل فيه ذلك القديم ، ولو حكمنا على الزمان بالقدم ، لأوهم ذلك الحكم وقوع ذلك الزمان في زمان آخر ، فإن كان هذا الوهم كاذبا ، فليكن مثل هذا الوهم كاذبا أيضا في جانب الحدوث ، فإنه لا فرق في العقل بين البابين ، وحينئذ يرجع حاصل الكلام إلى أن كون الشيء مستمرا ، وكونه متغيرا

paragraphs.text: The fourth proof: Just as we know by necessity that yesterday's originated thing is prior to today's originated thing, so likewise we know by necessity that yesterday is prior to today, with a priority. And the prior cannot exist with the posterior. If this type of priority necessitates the existence of a container and receptacle, for the sake of which this priority and posteriority occur, then let this container have another container, and this receptacle another receptacle, ad infinitum. And if it does not necessitate it at all, then let the matter be so in the case of all other originated things.

وإن كان يوهم وجود زمان يكون ظرفا ووعاء لذلك الاستمرار تارة ، ولذلك التغير أخرى إلا أن ذلك الوهم فاسد ، وذلك الخيال باطل ، وذلك يوجب القطع بنفي الزمان. وهو المطلوب. الحجة الرابعة : إنا كما نعلم بالضرورة : أن الحادث الأمسي متقدم على الحادث اليومي ، فكذلك نعلم بالضرورة أن الأمس متقدم على اليوم ، تقدما. ولا يمكن أن يوجد المتقدم مع المتأخر ، فإن كان هذا النوع من التقدم يحوج إلى وجود ظرفي ووعاء ، لأجله يحصل هذا التقدم ، وهذا التأخر ، فليكن لهذا

paragraphs.text: It cannot be said: suppose it necessitates for us the affirmation of infinite times, some encompassing others—why have you said that this is impossible? For we say: on this supposition, today would not be one day, but rather infinite days, some encompassing others, and their totality would be present in this day; and yesterday would not be one yesterday, but rather infinite days, some encompassing others, while their totality was present yesterday.

Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation
1. **Root: ن-ص-ف** | Word: انتصف | Definition: انقسم نصفين، وبلغ النصف. "To be halved, to reach the middle point."
2. **Root: خ-ل-ف** | Word: خلف | Definition: ما يستحيل وقوعه من تناقض المقدمات. "That which is impossible due to contradiction of premises."
3. **Root: ج-ز-ء** | Word: جزء | Definition: القطعة من الشيء التي لا تنقسم في الفرض. "A portion of a thing that is indivisible by hypothesis."
4. **Root: ح-ض-ر** | Word: حضور | Definition: كون الشيء موجوداً في الوقت الحالي. "A thing's being existent in the present moment."
5. **Root: ق-د-م** | Word: قديم | Definition: الموجود الذي لا أول لوجوده، المستمر أزلاً. "That which has no beginning to its existence, perpetually enduring."
6. **Root: ح-د-ث** | Word: حادث | Definition: الموجود بعد عدم، المسبوق بالغير. "That which exists after non-existence, preceded by another."
7. **Root: و-ع-ي** | Word: وعاء | Definition: الظرف الذي يحوي الشيء ويستوعبه. "The container that holds a thing and encompasses it."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: باب الفعل الماضي والمضارع في الشرط** | The use of past tense verbs in conditional constructions (كما في "إن كان حادثاً") indicates the hypothetical nature of the premise, where the protasis is treated as a settled fact for the sake of argument.

2. **Rule: باب العطف بالتقدير** | The coordination of clauses with "فإن" and "فإذا" follows Sībawayh's principle that the particle "فـ" introduces the apodosis of a conditional, marking a logical consequence that is syntactically bound to the protasis.

paragraphs.text: Know that many people claim that for any two existents, one of them must either be permeating the other, or separate from it in one of the six directions. And they claimed that affirming an existent that is neither inherent in this corporeal world, nor separate from it with respect to any of the directions: is impossible of existence. Then they claimed that knowledge of this impossibility: is primary, necessary knowledge, independent of proof and evidence.

paragraphs.text: As for the vast majority of the rational people, they have agreed that affirming an existent that does not occupy space, nor is inherent in what occupies space, nor is in the world, nor outside the world: is not known to be impossible in the primary intuition of the intellect. Rather, the matter of affirming it or denying it is dependent on evidence. If evidence indicates its affirmation, then judgment of it is obligatory; otherwise, suspension regarding its affirmation and denial is obligatory.

paragraphs.text: What indicates that the matter is so are several arguments: The first argument: that we say: if this proposition were primary, then disagreement about it among the rational people would be impossible; but disagreement about it does occur; therefore it must not be primary. The demonstration of the implication: a great multitude of rational people cannot concur in denying primary necessities. And the demonstration that this disagreement does occur: is that the philosophers have agreed on affirming existents that are not bodies occupying space, nor inherent in what occupies space, such as: the intellects, the souls, and the prime matter. And they agreed that the thing to which every person points by saying: I — it is existent, and is neither a body nor corporeal. And none of the rational people has said: they, in this statement, are deniers of primary necessities. Rather, we say: a group of the leading Muslims chose this doctrine, such as Muʿammar ibn ʿAbbād al-Sulamī from the Muʿtazila, and such as Abū Sahl [al-Nawbakhtī], and Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān from the Rāfiḍa. And such as Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāghib, and Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī from the People of the Sunnah and the Community. Also: most of the rational people from the adherents of the various religions and sects have concurred on transcending God, exalted be He, above being a body occupying space, and above being inherent in what occupies space, and above being inside the world, or outside it. So it is established by what we have mentioned: that if this proposition were primary, disagreement about it would be impossible; and since it is established that disagreement about it does occur — rather, the majority deny that proposition and are certain of its corruption — it necessarily follows that it is certain that it is not among the primary necessities.

paragraphs.text: The second argument: the clear intuition of the intellect testifies that the correct division is to say: the existent is either occupying space, or inherent in what occupies space, or neither occupying space nor inherent in what occupies space. And if we said: the existent is either occupying space, or inherent in what occupies space, and we restricted ourselves to this extent — then the primary intuitions of the intellects are decisive that this division is incomplete. Rather, we must join to it the third division, which is that which is neither occupying space,
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Constellation

1. **Root: و ح د** | Word: واحد | Definition: التوحيد: الحكم بأن الشيء واحد لا يتجزأ ولا ثاني له؛ والواحد في اللغة: المنفرد بذاته. Definition: "Tawḥīd: the judgment that a thing is one, indivisible, with no second to it; al-wāḥid in language: that which is unique in its essence."

2. **Root: ج ز أ** | Word: أجزاء | Definition: الجزء: بعض الشيء الذي يتركب منه كله؛ والجُزء في لسان العرب: ما يقبل القسمة. Definition: "al-juzʾ: a part of a thing from which its whole is composed; in Lisān al-ʿArab: that which admits of division."

3. **Root: ح ي ز** | Word: متحيز | Definition: التحيز: كون الشيء في حيز يختص به؛ والمتحيز: ما له مكان وجهة. Definition: "al-taḥayyuz: a thing's being in a space specific to it; al-mutaḥayyiz: that which has a place and a direction."

4. **Root: ض د د** | Word: ضد | Definition: الضد: المماثل في القوة المخالف في الفعل؛ والضدان: الشيئان اللذان لا يجتمعان. Definition: "al-ḍidd: the equal in power, contrary in act; the two ḍidds: two things that cannot coexist."

5. **Root: ن د د** | Word: ند | Definition: الند: المثل والمساوي؛ والنديد: النظير الذي ينازعك في الشيء. Definition: "al-nidd: the like and equal; al-nadīd: the counterpart that vies with you in a matter."

6. **Root: ب د ه** | Word: بديهة | Definition: البديهة: أول ما يسبق إلى العقل من غير فكر؛ والبديهي: ما لا يحتاج إلى كسب. Definition: "al-badīha: the first thing that occurs to the mind without reflection; al-badīhī: that which needs no acquisition."

7. **Root: س ر ي** | Word: سارٍ | Definition: السريان: الجريان والنفاذ في الشيء؛ والساري: الحال في غيره النافذ فيه. Definition: "al-saryān: flowing and penetrating into a thing; al-sārī: that which inheres in another and penetrates it."
Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: al-Ḥāl (The Circumstantial Accusative)** | In the phrase "لما قلنا: الله واحد" the word "واحد" functions as a ḥāl or khabar in a nominal sentence, governed by the mubtadaʾ; Sībawayh rules that the predicate of inherence (khabar) must agree with the subject in definiteness and number, and here it is indefinite to indicate a new predication, not a restrictive attribute.

2. **Rule: al-Istiṭrāf (The Parenthetical Clause)** | In "اعلم أنا إذا قلنا" the verb "اعلم" governs an anna-clause as its object; Sībawayh notes that such verbs of certainty (afʿāl al-qalb) require the complement in naṣb (accusative) via "anna," and the conditional "idhā" introduces a protasis that is temporally bound, with the apodosis "فله تفسيران" being a jumla ismiyya that serves as the jawāb, permissible because the condition is non-committal (ghayr jāzim).

* وهذا القول هو الذي نذهب إليه ونقول به.

paragraphs.text: And this statement is the one we adopt and affirm.

paragraphs.text: Nor is it a state (ḥāl) in a body, so that the division is completed. And if someone were to say: "Grant that this division is considered according to the classification, yet its impossibility is known by intuition (badīhah)." We say: The matter is not so. For when we present to the intuition of the intellect our statement that this division is impossible of existence, and we also present to the intuition that one is half of two, we find that the intuition decisively judges the falsehood of the second, but does not decisively judge the first. And whoever denies the difference between the two cases is being obstinate regarding the most evident and strongest of intuitions. Thus it is established by what we have mentioned: that affirming an existent that is neither a body nor a state in a body is not among the intuitions at all.

مفهوم مجرد عن الشكل المعين ، والحيز المعين. فثبت أن الإنسان معقول مفهوم مجرد. وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، فكيف يستبعد في العقل أن يكون خالق المخلوقات (2) منزها عن لواحق الحس وعلائق الخيال؟ فإن قيل : هذا الكلام مغالطة ، وذلك لأن «اعلم : أنه قد يغلب على أوهام الناس : أن الموجود هو المحسوس ، وأن ما

paragraphs.text: The Third Proof: We know by necessity that the individuals of people share in the meaning understood from our saying "human," and they differ by their particularizations and specificities. That by which they share is not that by which they differ. This indicates that the human insofar as he is human is a concept abstracted from specific form and specific place. Thus it is established that the human is an intelligible, abstract concept. And if this is the case, then how is it deemed remote in the intellect that the Creator of creatures should be purified of the attachments of sense and the ties of imagination? For if it is said: "This speech is a fallacy," that is because—

لا يناله بجوهره ، ففرض وجوده محال. وأن ما لا يتخصص بمكان أو وضع بذاته كالجسم ، أو لسبب ما هو فيه كأحوال الجسم. فلاحظ له من الوجود. وأنت يتأتى لك أن تتأمل نفس المحسوس ، فتعلم منه بطلان قول هؤلاء. لأنك ومن يستحق أن يخاطب تعلمان أن هذه المحسوسات قد يقع عليها اسم واحد. لا على سبيل الاشتراك الصرف ، بل بحسب معنى واحد. مثل اسم الانسان. فإنكما لا تشكان في أن وقوعه على زيد وعمرو ، بمعنى واحد : موجود. وذلك المعنى الموجود ، لا

paragraphs.text: "Know that it often dominates the fancies of people that the existent is the sensible, and that whatever the essence does not reach, the supposition of its existence is impossible. And that whatever is not specified by a place or position in itself like the body, or by a cause that is in it like the states of the body, has no share of existence. But you are able to contemplate the sensible itself, and learn from it the falsehood of these people's statement. Because you and whoever deserves to be addressed know that these sensibles may receive one name—not by way of pure homonymy, but according to one meaning. Like the name 'human.' For you both do not doubt that its application to Zayd and ʿAmr by one meaning is existent. And that existent meaning is not free from either being such that sense reaches it, or not being so. If it is far from being reached by sense, then the investigation has extracted from the sensibles that which is not sensible—and this is more astonishing. And if it is sensible, then it necessarily has a position, a where, a specific quantity, and a specific quality, such that it cannot be sensed—nor even imagined—except in that way. For every sensible and every imagined thing is necessarily specified by some of these states. And if this is so, it would not be compatible with what is not in that state, and thus would not be predicated of many things differing in that state.

يخلو. إما أن يكون بحيث يناله الحس ، أو لا يكون. فإن كان بعيدا من أن يناله الحس ، فقد أخرج التفتش من المحسوسات : ما ليس بمحسوس. وهذا أعجب. وإن كان محسوسا فله لا محالة وضع وأين ومقدار معين وكيف معين ، لا يتأتى أن يحس ، بل ولا أن يتخيل إلا كذلك. فإن كل محسوس وكل متخيل ، فإنه يتخصص لا محالة لشيء من هذه الأحوال. وإذا كان كذلك لم يكن ملائما لما ليس بتلك الحال ، فلم يكن مقولا على كثيرين مختلفين في تلك الحال.

paragraphs.text: Therefore, the human insofar as he is one in reality—rather, insofar as his original reality in which multiplicity does not differ—is not sensible, but purely intelligible. And likewise is the case with every universal. Perhaps one of them might say: "The human, for example, is only human insofar as he has organs—a hand, an eye, an eyebrow, and so forth. And insofar as he is thus, he is sensible." So we draw attention and say to him: The case with every universal organ, whether of what you mentioned or omitted, is like the case with the human himself.

فإذن الإنسان من حيث هو واحد الحقيقة بل من حيث حقيقته الأصلية التي لا تختلف فيها الكثرة غير محسوس ، بل معقول صرف. وكذلك الحال في كل كلي. ولعل قائلا منهم يقول : إن الإنسان مثلا إنما هو إنسان من حيث له أعضاء ، من يد وعين وحاجب وغير ذلك. ومن حيث هو كذلك ، فهو محسوس. فننبه ونقول له : إن الحال في كل عضو كلي ، مما ذكرته أو تركته ، كالحال في الإنسان نفسه.
paragraphs.arabic: فإذن الإنسان من حيث هو واحد الحقيقة بل من حيث حقيقته الأصلية التي لا تختلف فيها الكثرة غير محسوس ، بل معقول صرف. وكذلك الحال في كل كلي. ولعل قائلا منهم يقول : إن الإنسان مثلا إنما هو إنسان من حيث له أعضاء ، من يد وعين وحاجب وغير ذلك. ومن حيث هو كذلك ، فهو محسوس. فننبه ونقول له : إن الحال في كل عضو كلي ، مما ذكرته أو تركته ، كالحال في الإنسان نفسه.

paragraphs.text: "Note": If every existent were such that it enters into imagination and sense, then sense and imagination would enter into sense and imagination, and the intellect—which is the true judge—would enter into imagination. And if these principles are remote, then none of love, shame, dread, anger, courage, and cowardice enter into sense and imagination, yet they are among the attachments of sensible things. So what do you think of existents whose essences are outside the degrees of sensibles and their attachments?" End quote.

«تنبيه» : إنه لو كان كل موجود بحيث يدخل في الوهم والحس. لكان الحس والوهم يدخلان في الحس والوهم ، ولكان العقل الذي هو الحكم الحق يدخل في الوهم. ومن أبعد هذه الأصول ، فليس شيء من العشق والخجل والوجل والغضب والشجاعة والجبن ، مما يدخل في الحس والوهم ، وهي من علائق الأمور المحسوسة. فما ظنك بموجودات ، إن كانت خارجة الذوات عن درجات المحسوسات وعلائقها» أه.

paragraphs.text: The common share between the individuals of people has no existence outside the mind; rather, what exists externally is the particularized essences and the distinct individuals. As for the common share, it has no existence except in the mind. And the dispute only occurred regarding whether there exists in external reality an existent abstracted from position and place. So where is one of the two matters from the other? Thus it is established that this speech is pure fallacy. And the answer to it is from two aspects:

القدر المشترك بين أشخاص الناس ليس له وجود خارج الذهن ، بل الموجود في الخارج هو الذوات المتعينة ، والأشخاص المتباينة ، فأما القدر المشترك فلا وجود له إلا في الذهن. والنزاع إنما وقع في أنه : هل يوجد في الأعيان موجود مجرد عن الوضع والحيز؟ فأين أحد البابين من الآخر؟ فيثبت : أن هذا الكلام مغالطة محضة. والجواب عنه من وجهين : الأول : إنه ثبت بالدليل الذي ذكرناه : أن القدر المشترك بين الأشخاص

Sībawayh Syntactic & Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: الابتداء والخبر** | The nominal sentence structure (مبتدأ وخبر) governs the opening "وهذا القول هو الذي نذهب إليه" where the pronoun "هو" functions as a separator (فصل) between the subject and predicate, emphasizing identity.

2. **Rule: الاستفهام التقريري** | The rhetorical question "فأين أحد البابين من الآخر؟" employs the interrogative "أين" for location metaphorically, indicating the vast distance between two matters, a construction Sībawayh classifies under استفهام عن المكان مجازا.

#### Lisān al-ʿArab 7-Root Lexical Constellation (المنظومة المعجمية السبعية)
1. **Root: ع ص م** | Word: عصمة | Definition: الحماية والمنع؛ يقال عصمه الطعامُ إذا منعه من الجوع، فهو مانع وحافظ (*al-ʿiṣma*: protection and prevention; it is said food "protected" him if it prevented hunger, so it is a preventer and preserver).
2. **Root: س ه و** | Word: السهو | Definition: الغفلة عن الشيء وذهاب القلب عنه؛ نقيض الذكر والتحفظ (*al-sahw*: heedlessness of a thing and the heart's departure from it; the opposite of remembrance and caution).
3. **Root: ن س ي** | Word: النسيان | Definition: ترك الشيء على غير ذكرٍ منه؛ ضد الحفظ والذكران (*al-nisyān*: abandoning a thing without recollection of it; the opposite of retaining and remembering).
4. **Root: ج و ز** | Word: جائز | Definition: الممكن الذي لا يمنع العقل من وقوعه ولا يوجبه؛ في كلام المتكلمين ما يصح وجوده وعدمه (*jāʾiz*: that which is possible, which reason neither prevents nor necessitates; in Kalām terminology, that whose existence and non-existence are both valid).
5. **Root: ذ ن ب** | Word: الذنب | Definition: الإثم والجُرْم؛ وأصلها الأخذ بالذنب أي العقب، كأنه أثر يتبع صاحبه (*al-dhanb*: sin and crime; its origin is seizing the tail (al-dhanab), as if it is a consequence that follows its doer).
6. **Root: خ ط أ** | Word: الخطأ | Definition: ضد الصواب؛ وهو العدول عن الحق في القول أو الفعل من غير تعمد (*al-khaṭaʾ*: the opposite of correctness; it is deviating from the truth in speech or action without deliberate intention).
7. **Root: ك ف ر** | Word: الكفر | Definition: تغطية النعم وجحودها؛ وشرعًا: تكذيب الرسول فيما جاء به أو جحد ما علم من الدين بالضرورة (*al-kufr*: covering over and denying blessings; legally: denying the Messenger in what he brought or rejecting what is known of religion by necessity).
يجوز صدور الذنب منهم على سبيل الخطأ في التأويل، وهو قول أبي علي الجبائي

paragraphs.text:
#### Sībawayh Grammatical & Syntactic Anchors (الشواهد النحوية والتركيبية)
1. **Rule: Inna and its sisters (إنّ وأخواتها)** | The sentence "كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ" (Q. 18:5) demonstrates the accusative of specification (*tamyīz*), where "كَلِمَةً" is mansūb as a distinguisher after the verb "كَبُرَتْ". Sibawayh explains in Al-Kitāb (vol. 1, bāb al-tamyīz) that this construction specifies the nature of the greatness, i.e., the enormity lies in the statement itself, not in the mere utterance. The semantic import is that the claim is magnified in its falsehood, and the accusative marks the specification of the verbal action.
2. **Rule: The particle "أما بعد" (ammā baʿd)** | Sibawayh treats "أمّا" as a conditional-concessive particle requiring a following *jawāb* (apodosis). In "فَهَذِهِ رِسَالَةٌ عَمِلْنَاهَا", the *fāʾ* of the apodosis is obligatory after "أمّا", and what precedes it (the hamdalah and salawāt) is the *muqaddima* (preface). Sibawayh notes in Al-Kitāb (bāb al-jazāʾ) that "أمّا" serves to transition from the preamble to the main discourse, with the *fāʾ* marking the resumption after an implicit condition akin to *mahmā yakun min shayʾ* (whatever may be the case).
(الرابع) أنه لا يجوز عليهم الكبيرة ولا الصغيرة، لا بالعمد ولا بالتأويل
paragraphs.arabic: (الرابع) أنه لا يجوز عليهم الكبيرة ولا الصغيرة، لا بالعمد ولا بالتأويل

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically & Syntactically Guided)
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, Who is exalted by the majesty of His Oneness above the arenas of thoughts and fancies, sanctified by the perfection of His Self-Sufficiency above the domains of inner visions and intellects, transcending—by the necessity of His Ipsum Essence—any resemblance to accidents or bodies, and absolved by the greatness of His Divinity from the motives of advance and the deterrents of withdrawal. He is the One Who does not change with the succession of ages nor the passage of months and years, and the lavish pouring of His favor upon the elite and the commonalty of His creatures in beneficence and grace does not weary Him. And prayer be upon Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), sent to all mankind, and peace be upon his family and his companions, the leaders of Islam.

To proceed: This is a treatise we have composed in defense of God's messengers and His prophets, in vindication of the choicest of His creation and His pious servants, and in exposition of what the Hashwiyya (*al-Ḥashwiyya* / literalists) have alleged in imputing sins and crimes to them, and in attributing shameful deeds and abominations to them—and that this is falsehood and calumny, a notion devoid of proof and demonstration. Indeed, they belch without being satiated, and they aspire to what affords no aspiration, and their specious arguments cannot withstand the mightiest forearm nor ascend the most level path. "Great is the word that comes out of their mouths; they utter nothing but a lie" (Q. 18:5). God is the Praised One for what He has lavished of His grace, and the Thanked One for what He has granted of verification. He is our sufficiency, and excellent is the Guardian.

paragraphs.text: Know that the disagreement on this matter occurs on four points:
إسحاق إبراهيم بن سيار النظام * [الخامس] أنه لا يجوز عليهم الكبيرة ولا
paragraphs.arabic: إسحاق إبراهيم بن سيار النظام * [الخامس] أنه لا يجوز عليهم الكبيرة ولا

paragraphs.text: **First:** What pertains to matters of belief. The Community (*al-umma*) is unanimous that the prophets are infallible (*maʿṣūmūn*) with respect to unbelief and heresy, except for the Fuḍayliyya (*al-Fuḍayliyya*) of the Khawārij (*al-Khawārij*), for they deem unbelief possible for the prophets (peace be upon them). This is because, in their view, it is permissible for sins to issue from them, and every sin is unbelief in their estimation; thus by this route they deemed the issuance of unbelief from them possible. Likewise the Rawāfiḍ (*al-Rawāfiḍ*), for they deem possible for them the utterance of the word of unbelief by way of dissimulation (*taqiyya*).

**Second:** What pertains to all the revealed laws and rulings from God Most High. They are unanimous that tampering and betrayal are not permissible for them in this domain—neither deliberately nor inadvertently—for otherwise no reliance could be placed upon any of the revealed laws.
الصغيرة لا بالعمد ولا بالتأويل ولا بالسهو والنسيان. وهذا مذهب الشيعة *
paragraphs.arabic: الصغيرة لا بالعمد ولا بالتأويل ولا بالسهو والنسيان. وهذا مذهب الشيعة *

paragraphs.text: **Third:** What pertains to legal opinion (*fatwā*). They are unanimous that deliberate error is not permissible. As for error by way of inadvertence (*al-sahw*), they have disagreed thereon.

paragraphs.text: **Fourth:** What pertains to their deeds and states. They have disagreed thereon according to five schools:
The **first** is that of the Ḥashwiyya (*al-Ḥashwiyya* / literalists), namely that it is permissible for them to commit major and minor sins.
إنها من أول الولادة إلى آخر العمر، وقال الأكثرون: هذه العصمة إنما تجب
paragraphs.arabic: إنها من أول الولادة إلى آخر العمر، وقال الأكثرون: هذه العصمة إنما تجب

paragraphs.text: The **second** is that it is not permissible for them to commit a major sin deliberately at all; as for committing a minor sin deliberately, that is permissible (*jāʾiz*), provided that it is not repulsive. But if it is repulsive, then that is not permissible for them—such as giving short measure by less than a grain. This is the saying of the majority of the Muʿtazila (*al-Muʿtazila*).
في زمان النبوة. فأما قبلها فهي غير واجبة. وهو قول أكثر أصحابنا رحمهم
paragraphs.arabic: في زمان النبوة. فأما قبلها فهي غير واجبة. وهو قول أكثر أصحابنا رحمهم

paragraphs.text: The **third** is that it is not permissible for them to commit a major or minor sin deliberately, but the occurrence of a sin from them is permissible by way of error in interpretation (*khaṭaʾ fī al-taʾwīl*). This is the saying of Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī.

The **fourth** is that neither major nor minor sins are permissible for them—neither deliberately nor by interpretation and error. As for inadvertence (*al-sahw*) and forgetfulness (*al-nisyān*), these are permissible. Then they are reproached for that inadvertence and forgetfulness, because their knowledge is more complete, so the obligation upon them was to exercise greater vigilance. This is the saying of Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Sayyār al-Naẓẓām.
الله تعالى *
paragraphs.arabic: الله تعالى *

paragraphs.text: The **fifth** is that neither major nor minor sins are permissible for them—neither deliberately, nor by interpretation, nor by inadvertence and forgetfulness. This is the school of the Shīʿa (*al-Shīʿa / al-Imāmiyya*).

paragraphs.text: They also disagreed regarding the time of the obligation of this infallibility. Some said: It is from the very beginning of birth to the end of life. The majority said: This infallibility is only obligatory during the time of prophethood; as for before it, it is not obligatory. This is the saying of the majority of our companions (*aṣḥābunā*), may God Most High have mercy on them.

 *al-ʿiṣma*: prevention and protection; food "withholds" one from hunger; God's protection of the prophets prevents and preserves them from falling into sins.

#### Sībawayh Grammatical & Syntactic Anchors (الشواهد النحوية والتركيبية)
1. **Rule: The Conditional Inceptive Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb)** | In the verse "لو صدر الذنب عنهم لكان حالهم..." the particle *law* (لو) governs the protasis, and the apodosis is introduced by *lām* (لام الجواب) attached to *kāna*. Sibawayh explains that *law* indicates a hypothetical past condition that is contrary to fact, and the *lām* in the answer is mandatory to affirm the entailment.

#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically & Syntactically Guided)
The Infallibility: Fifteen Aspects (Part 1)

[The First Argument (1)] If sin were to issue from them, their state in deserving blame immediately and punishment ultimately would be more severe than the state of the disobedient among the community. Yet this is false, so the issuance of sin from them is also false. The demonstration of the entailment (*bayān al-mulāzama*): The greatest of God's blessings upon His servants is the blessing of apostleship and prophethood. And whoever has more of God's blessings upon him, the more heinous is the issuance of sin from him—and the plain dictates of reason indicate this. Then three aspects from transmitted revelation confirm it:
الخاسرون) وحزب الله كما قال تعالى (أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم
paragraphs.arabic: الخاسرون) وحزب الله كما قال تعالى (أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم

paragraphs.text: [The First] His saying, Exalted is He: "O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women" (33:32). And He said: "O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a manifest indecency, for her the punishment will be doubled twofold" (33:30). [The Second] The married person (al-muḥṣan) is stoned, while others are flogged. [The Third] The slave receives half the punishment of the free person. So it is established by what we have mentioned that if sin were to issue from them, their state in deserving immediate blame and ultimate punishment would surpass the state of all the disobedient of the community—except that this is false by consensus, for no one may say that the Messenger is worse in rank before God and lower in station than everyone else. And this indicates the non-issuance of sin from them.
المفلحون) ولا شك أن حزب الشيطان هو الذي يفعل ما يريد الشيطان ويأمره به.
paragraphs.arabic: المفلحون) ولا شك أن حزب الشيطان هو الذي يفعل ما يريد الشيطان ويأمره به.

paragraphs.text: [The Second Argument] If sin were to issue from them, their testimony would not be accepted, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "O you who have believed, if a wicked person comes to you with news, verify it" (49:6). He commanded verification and hesitation in accepting the testimony of the wicked. Yet this is false—for if one's testimony is not accepted in this world, how would his testimony be accepted regarding the religions that endure until the Day of Resurrection? Moreover, God Most High testified that Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is a witness over all on the Day of Resurrection. He said: "And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you" (2:143). And how could one who is a witness over all the messengers on the Day of Resurrection be in a state where his testimony is not accepted in Paradise?
فلو صدرت الذنوب عن الأنبياء لصدق عليهم أنهم من حزب الشيطان، ولصدق عليهم
paragraphs.arabic: فلو صدرت الذنوب عن الأنبياء لصدق عليهم أنهم من حزب الشيطان، ولصدق عليهم

paragraphs.text: [The Third Argument] If sin were to issue from them, it would be obligatory to rebuke them, because the proofs indicate the obligation of commanding the good and forbidding the evil. But rebuking the prophets (peace be upon them) is not permissible, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger—God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter" (33:57). Thus the issuance of sin from them is rendered impossible.
قوله تعالى:
paragraphs.arabic: قوله تعالى:

paragraphs.text: [The Fourth Argument] If disobedience (*al-fisq*) were to issue from Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), then either we would be commanded to follow his example—and this is not permissible—or we would not be commanded to follow his example—and this too is false, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "Say: If you love God, follow me, and God will love you" (3:31), and His saying: "So follow him" (7:158). And since the issuance of disobedience leads to these two false divisions, the issuance of disobedience from him is impossible.

[The Fifth Argument] If disobedience were to issue from the prophets (peace be upon them), they would have to be promised the punishment of God with the punishment of Hellfire, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger and transgresses His limits—He will admit him into a Fire, abiding eternally therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment" (4:14). And they would be cursed, due to His saying: "Surely, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers" (11:18). And by the consensus of the community, this is false, so the issuance of disobedience from them is false.
(ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون) ولصدق على الزهاد من آحاد الأمة قوله
paragraphs.arabic: (ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون) ولصدق على الزهاد من آحاد الأمة قوله

paragraphs.text: [The Sixth Argument] They used to command obedience and the abandonment of sins. If they abandoned obedience and committed sin, they would fall under His saying, Exalted is He: "O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of God is that you say what you do not do" (61:2–3), and under His saying: "Do you enjoin righteousness upon people and forget yourselves?" (2:44). And it is known that this is utterly repugnant. Also, God Most High reported about His Messenger Shuʿayb (peace be upon him) that he declared himself innocent of that, saying: "And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you" (11:88).
تعالى (ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون) وحينئذ يلزم أن يكون واحد من آحاد
paragraphs.arabic: تعالى (ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون) وحينئذ يلزم أن يكون واحد من آحاد

paragraphs.text: [The Seventh Argument] God Most High said describing Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq, and Yaʿqūb: "Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds" (21:90). And the *al-lām* in the plural form indicates generality, so under the word "good deeds" falls the doing of everything that ought to be done and the abandonment of everything that ought not to be done. And that indicates that they were doers of all acts of obedience and abandoners of all sins.
الأمة أفضل بكثير من الأنبياء، ولا شك في بطلانه * [الحجة الثانية عشرة] إن
paragraphs.arabic: الأمة أفضل بكثير من الأنبياء، ولا شك في بطلانه * [الحجة الثانية عشرة] إن

paragraphs.text: [The Eighth Argument] His saying, Exalted is He: "And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the best" (38:47). That is, the two expressions—namely His saying "the chosen" (al-muṣṭafīn) and His saying "the best" (al-akhyār)—encompass the totality of acts and abandonments, as evidenced by the permissibility of exclusion. One says: "So-and-so is among the chosen and the best except in such-and-such." And exclusion removes from speech what would otherwise have been included. So this verse indicates that they were among the chosen and the best in all matters, and this contradicts the issuance of sin from them. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: "God chooses messengers from the angels and from mankind" (22:75), and His saying: "Indeed, God chose Ādam, Nūḥ, the family of Ibrāhīm, and the family of ʿImrān above all worlds" (3:33). And He said regarding Ibrāhīm: "And We chose him in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous" (2:130). And He said regarding Mūsā (peace be upon him): "Indeed, I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and My speech" (7:144). And He said, Exalted is He: "And remember Our servants Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq, and Yaʿqūb, men of strength and vision. Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality—the remembrance of the abode" (38:45–46).

It cannot be said: "Selection does not prevent the doing of sin, as evidenced by His saying, Exalted is He: 'Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those whom We chose from Our servants; among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who outstrips in good deeds by God's permission' (35:32). He divided the chosen into the self-wronger, the moderate, and the one outstripping in good deeds." For we say: The pronoun in "among them" (fa-minhum) refers back to His saying "from Our servants" (min ʿibādinā), not to His saying "those whom We chose" (alladhīna iṣṭafaynā), because the return of the pronoun to the nearest of the mentioned antecedents is obligatory.
أصحابنا رحمهم الله تعالى بينوا أن
paragraphs.arabic: أصحابنا رحمهم الله تعالى بينوا أن

paragraphs.text: [The Ninth Argument] His saying, Exalted is He, reporting from Iblīs: "So by Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them" (15:39–40). He excluded the chosen ones from his misleading and leading astray. Then God Most High testified concerning Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq, and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them) that they are among the chosen ones, where He said: "Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality" (38:46). And He said regarding Yūsuf (peace be upon him): "Indeed, he is among Our chosen servants" (12:24). So when Iblīs admitted that he does not mislead the chosen ones, and God testified that these are among the chosen ones, it is established that Iblīs's misleading and whispering never reached them. And that necessitates the definitive conclusion that no disobedience issued from them.
الأنبياء أفضل من الملائكة وثابت بالدلالة أن الملائكة ما أقدموا على شئ
paragraphs.arabic: الأنبياء أفضل من الملائكة وثابت بالدلالة أن الملائكة ما أقدموا على شئ

paragraphs.text: [The Tenth Argument] God Most High said: "And indeed, Iblīs had confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except a party of the believers" (34:20). So those who did not follow Iblīs—either they are the prophets or others. If they are others, then it would follow that they are better than the prophets, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you" (49:13). And preferring a non-prophet over a prophet is false by consensus. Therefore, it is necessary to conclude definitively that those who did not follow Iblīs are the prophets (peace be upon them). And whoever commits a sin has followed Iblīs. So this indicates that the prophets (God's prayers be upon them) never committed sins.
من الذنوب، فلو صدرت الذنوب عن الأنبياء لامتنع أن يكونوا زائدين في الفضل
paragraphs.arabic: من الذنوب، فلو صدرت الذنوب عن الأنبياء لامتنع أن يكونوا زائدين في الفضل

paragraphs.text: [The Eleventh Argument] God Most High divided the morally responsible into two divisions: the party of Satan, as He said, Exalted is He: "Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers" (58:19), and the party of God, as He said: "Those are the party of God. Unquestionably, the party of God are the successful" (58:22). And there is no doubt that the party of Satan is the one that does what Satan wants and commands. So if sins were to issue from the prophets, then the description of being the party of Satan would apply to them, and His saying would apply to them: "Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers." And the saying of God Most High—"Unquestionably, the party of God are the successful"—would apply to the ascetics among the common individuals of the community. And in that case, it would necessitate that a single individual from the common members of the community is vastly better than the prophets—and there is no doubt of its falsity.
على الملائكة لقوله تعالى (أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين
paragraphs.arabic: على الملائكة لقوله تعالى (أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين

paragraphs.text: [The Twelfth Argument] Our companions (*aṣḥābunā*)—may God have mercy on them—clarified that the prophets are superior to the angels. And it is established by proof that the angels never advanced upon any sin. So if sins were to issue from the prophets, it would be impossible for them to exceed the angels in virtue, due to His saying, Exalted is He: "Or do We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who cause corruption in the land?" (38:28).
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Notes
1. **Root: ع-ص-م** | Word: العصمة | Definition: المنع والحفظ؛ عصمه الطعامُ أي منعه من الجوع، وعصم اللهُ الأنبياءَ حفظهم ووقاهم من الوقوع في الذنوب.
paragraphs.arabic: 1. **Root: ع-ص-م** | Word: العصمة | Definition: المنع والحفظ؛ عصمه الطعامُ أي منعه من الجوع، وعصم اللهُ الأنبياءَ حفظهم ووقاهم من الوقوع في الذنوب.

paragraphs.text: *al-ʿiṣma*: prevention and protection; food "withholds" one from hunger; God's protection of the prophets prevents and preserves them from falling into sins.
2. **Root: ذ-ن-ب** | Word: الذنب | Definition: الإثم والجرم؛ أخذ به بذنبه أي بجريمته، والذنب ما يستحق به العقاب.
paragraphs.arabic: 2. **Root: ذ-ن-ب** | Word: الذنب | Definition: الإثم والجرم؛ أخذ به بذنبه أي بجريمته، والذنب ما يستحق به العقاب.

paragraphs.text: *al-dhanb*: sin and crime; one is seized for his dhanb meaning his offense; it is that which merits punishment.
3. **Root: خ-ط-أ** | Word: الخطأ | Definition: ضد الصواب؛ وأخطأ فلانٌ إذا لم يُصب الحق، والخطيئة اسم للفعل القبيح.
paragraphs.arabic: 3. **Root: خ-ط-أ** | Word: الخطأ | Definition: ضد الصواب؛ وأخطأ فلانٌ إذا لم يُصب الحق، والخطيئة اسم للفعل القبيح.

paragraphs.text: *al-khaṭaʾ*: the opposite of correctness; one errs when he does not hit the truth; al-khaṭīʾa is a noun for a reprehensible act.
4. **Root: ف-ح-ش** | Word: الفاحشة | Definition: ما عظم قبحه من الذنوب والفواحش؛ وهي ما جاوز الحد من المعاصي.
paragraphs.arabic: 4. **Root: ف-ح-ش** | Word: الفاحشة | Definition: ما عظم قبحه من الذنوب والفواحش؛ وهي ما جاوز الحد من المعاصي.

paragraphs.text: *al-fāḥisha*: that which is enormously ugly among sins; it is that which transgresses the limit of disobedience.
5. **Root: ع-ص-ي** | Word: المعصية | Definition: مخالفة الأمر؛ عصى العبدُ ربَّه إذا خالف أمره ونهيه، والاسم العصيان.
paragraphs.arabic: 5. **Root: ع-ص-ي** | Word: المعصية | Definition: مخالفة الأمر؛ عصى العبدُ ربَّه إذا خالف أمره ونهيه، والاسم العصيان.

paragraphs.text: *al-maʿṣiya*: contravening the command; the servant disobeys his Lord when he violates His command and prohibition; the noun is ʿiṣyān.
6. **Root: ن-ب-أ** | Word: النبأ | Definition: الخبر العظيم الذي له شأن؛ والأنبياء سموا بذلك لأنهم أنبأوا عن الله تعالى.
paragraphs.arabic: 6. **Root: ن-ب-أ** | Word: النبأ | Definition: الخبر العظيم الذي له شأن؛ والأنبياء سموا بذلك لأنهم أنبأوا عن الله تعالى.

paragraphs.text: *al-nabaʾ*: the great news of momentous import; the prophets are so named because they announced from God Most High.
7. **Root: ص-ف-و** | Word: المصطفين | Definition: المختارين؛ اصطفى اللهُ فلانًا أي اختاره واجتباه لطاعته ورسالته.
paragraphs.arabic: 7. **Root: ص-ف-و** | Word: المصطفين | Definition: المختارين؛ اصطفى اللهُ فلانًا أي اختاره واجتباه لطاعته ورسالته.

paragraphs.text: *al-muṣṭafīn*: the chosen ones; God "selected" so-and-so meaning He chose and elected him for His obedience and message.
Sībawayh Grammatical Commentary

1. **Rule: The Conditional Inceptive Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb)** | In the verse "لو صدر الذنب عنهم لكان حالهم..." the particle *law* (لو) governs the protasis, and the apodosis is introduced by *lām* (لام الجواب) attached to *kāna*. Sibawayh explains that *law* indicates a hypothetical past condition that is contrary to fact, and the *lām* in the answer is mandatory to affirm the entailment.

2. **Rule: The Exclusion (al-istithnāʾ) and the Return of the Pronoun (ʿawd al-ḍamīr)** | In the argument concerning "فمنهم ظالم لنفسه," Sibawayh's principle of pronominal reference dictates that the pronoun returns to the nearest antecedent. Al-Rāzī employs this rule to show that *minhum* refers to *ʿibādinā* (our servants) not to *alladhīna iṣṭafaynā* (those We chose), thereby preserving the prophets' absolute purity from the implication of the three categories.

paragraphs.text: I say: This is the Book of Sects (*Kitāb al-Firaq*), expounding the conditions and doctrines of the Muslims and the idolaters (*al-mushrikīn*). Know that it is arranged upon ten chapters (*abwāb*), each chapter being devoted to a distinct class of theological opinions and their adherents, so that the seeker of truth may discern, by the grace of God, the sound from the corrupt, and the orthodox from the heretical, in accordance with the clear distinction (*al-farq*) which God has set between guidance and error.

#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: ش-ر-ح (sh-r-ḥ)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: "الشَّرْحُ: تَفْسِيرُ الشَّيْءِ وَتَوْسِيعُهُ" (*al-sharḥu: tafsīru al-shayʾi wa-tawsīʿuhu*) — "Explanation is the interpretation of a thing and its expansion."

#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: The Genitive Construction (al-Idāfa)**
*Al-Kitāb*: "هَذَا بَابُ مَا يَجْرِي مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ" (*hādhā bābu mā yajrī mina al-asmāʾi ʿalā al-fiʿli*) — "This is a chapter on what occurs among nouns in the manner of the verb," illustrating how a noun like *sharḥ* governs a following genitive (*firaq*).
وفيه ثلاثة فصول

paragraphs.text:
#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
I say: Know that this first chapter is devoted to the exposition of the sects of the Muʿtazilites (*al-Muʿtazila*). It comprises three sections, which I shall unfold in due order, following the path of clarity and precision, so that the seeker of truth may discern the distinctions among their doctrines and the foundations upon which they build their claims.
Lisān al-ʿArab Root Analysis & Lexicographical Notes
ش-ر-ح (sh-r-ḥ)

#### Lisan al-Arab Lexical Note (Translation Anchor)
**Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)**
*Lisān al-ʿArab*: العلم: نقيض الجهل، وهو إدراك الشيء على ما هو به إدراكاً جازماً (al-ʿilm: the opposite of ignorance; it is the apprehension of a thing as it truly is, with firm certainty)

#### Sibawayh Grammatical Note (Syntactic Anchor)
**Rule: Al-Istiṭnāʾ (الاستثناء)**
*Al-Kitāb*: "هذا باب الاستثناء، وهو أن تقول: قام القوم إلا زيداً" (This is the chapter on exception, where you say: "The people stood except Zayd")

#### Translation (Imam Al-Razi's Voice — Lexically Guided)
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
العلوم، والثقافات، والفكر كبيرة.
paragraphs.arabic: العلوم، والثقافات، والفكر كبيرة.

paragraphs.text: Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth, and made darkness and light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord. I praise Him with a praise befitting His majestic countenance and His tremendous sovereignty. I seek His aid—the aid of one who has no power or strength except through Him. I seek His guidance—the guidance by which none who is blessed with it goes astray. I seek His forgiveness for what I have done earlier and later—the forgiveness of one who acknowledges his servitude and knows that none forgives his sin or saves him from it except Him, Glorified be He.
يقول ابن خلدون - وهو يتحدث عن العلوم العقلية وأصنافها والامم التي
paragraphs.arabic: يقول ابن خلدون - وهو يتحدث عن العلوم العقلية وأصنافها والامم التي

paragraphs.text: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner. I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, through whom God—Exalted be He—rescued us from perdition, delivered us from error, and made us the best nation brought forth for mankind. May God—Exalted be He—send His blessings upon him among the earlier and later generations, with the best, most abundant, and most pure blessings He has ever bestowed upon any of His creation; and upon his family, his companions, and those who followed him and called with his call until the Day they meet Him.
اعتنت بها أو أهملتها -: " ويبلغنا عن أهل المشرق أن بضائع هذه العلوم لم
paragraphs.arabic: اعتنت بها أو أهملتها -: " ويبلغنا عن أهل المشرق أن بضائع هذه العلوم لم

paragraphs.text: To proceed: Among the most important sciences leading to knowledge of God's legal rulings (*aḥkām*) in His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger—peace be upon him—is the science of legal theory (*uṣūl al-fiqh*). It is, as Imam al-Ghazālī says, "the science in which reason and revelation are wedded, in which opinion and sacred law are companions, taking from the pure essence of both law and reason the straight path. It is neither a mere exercise of pure intellects—which revelation does not accept—nor is it built upon sheer emulation (*taqlīd*) which reason does not attest with right guidance and support."
تزل عندهم موفورة وخصوصا في عراق العجم وما بعده فيما وراء النهر، وأنهم
paragraphs.arabic: تزل عندهم موفورة وخصوصا في عراق العجم وما بعده فيما وراء النهر، وأنهم

paragraphs.text: Among the most important works written in this science—after the treatise of Imam al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him—are: *Al-Burhān* by Imām al-Ḥaramayn al-Juwaynī, and *Al-Mustaṣfā* by Ḥujjat al-Islām al-Ghazālī, from the People of the Sunnah; and *Al-ʿAhd* by al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Hamadhānī, and *Al-Muʿtamad* by Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Baṣrī, from the Muʿtazilah. These four books have gathered the entirety of theoretical investigations (*mabāḥith uṣūliyyah*), encompassing all the issues of this weighty science after its completion, until these four books became the references of this science and the sources of its principles.

However, because these four books possessed certain qualities that limited the scope of benefit from them and reduced the number of those who could profit from them among students of the sacred sciences, the need arose for a book that would combine their merits, encompass their investigations, and strip away what had been criticized in them.
على (ثبج من العلوم العقلية لتوفر عمرانهم، واستحكام الحضارة فيهم ".
paragraphs.arabic: على (ثبج من العلوم العقلية لتوفر عمرانهم، واستحكام الحضارة فيهم ".

paragraphs.text: Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī undertook this task and composed his book *Al-Maḥṣūl fī ʿIlm Uṣūl al-Fiqh* to be the comprehensive collection of all the theoretical issues found in these four mother-works, purified of all the objections raised against them. To this he added from his abundant knowledge, his precision of expression, his excellence of style, and his fluidity of language that which made *Al-Maḥṣūl* the aspiration of students of legal theory (*uṣūl al-fiqh*) and the object of their hope. They turned to it and found themselves independent of all that preceded it.
كما عقد فصلا خاصا لبيان - أن حملة العلم في الاسلام أكثرهم من
paragraphs.arabic: كما عقد فصلا خاصا لبيان - أن حملة العلم في الاسلام أكثرهم من

paragraphs.text: So who is Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī, and what is his book *Al-Maḥṣūl*? This is what we shall clarify in the following lines.
العجم - وبعد أن قرر هذا قال: " وإن كان منهم العربي في نسبته فهو عجمي

في لغته ومرباه ومشيخته ".

paragraphs.text: Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī lived through the entire second half of the sixth century of the Hijrah, along with six or seven years of its first half—those being the years of his childhood—and he also lived through the first six years of the seventh century.
