### | بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

قال الشيخ الإمام الهمام، حجة الإسلام، زين الدين أبو حامد محمد بن محمد
بن محمد الغزالي الطوسي، رضي الله تعالى عنه وأرضاه: لما كانت السعادة التي
هي مطلوب الأولين والآخرين لا تنال إلا بالعلم والعمل، وافتقر كل واحد
منهما إلى الإحاطة بحقيقته ومقداره، ووجب معرفة العلم والتمييز بينه وبين
غيره بمعيار، وفرغنا منه، وجب معرفة العمل المسعد، والتمييز بينه وبين
العمل المشقي. فافتقر ذلك أيضا إلى ميزان، فأردنا أن نخوض فيه ونبين أن
الفتور عن طلب السعادة حماقة، ثم نبين العلم وطريق تحصيله، ثم نبين العمل
المسعد وطريقه. وكل ذلك بطريقة تترقى عن حد طريق التقليد إلى حد الوضوح، لو
استقصى بحقيقته وطول الكلم فيه ارتقى إلى حد البرهان على الشروط التي

ذكرناها في " معيار العلم ". وإن كنا لسنا نطول الكلام به، ولكن نرشد إلى
أصوله وقوانينه.

### | بيان أن الفتور عن طلب السعادة حماقة

السعاة الآخروية التي نعني بها بقاء بلا فناء، ولذة بلا عناء، وسرور بلا
حزن، وغنى بلا فقر، وكمال بلا نقصان، وعز بلا ذل، وبالجملة كل ما يتصور أن
يكون مطلوب طالب ومرغوب راغب، وذلك أبد الآباد، وعلى وجه لا تنقصه تصرم
الأحقاب والآماد، بل لو قدرنا الدنيا مملوءة بالدرر، وقدرنا طائرا يختطف في
كل ألف سنة حبة واحدة منها، لفنيت الدرر ولم ينقص من أبد الآباد شيء، فهذا
لا يحتاج إلى استحثاث على طلبه، وتقبيح الفتور فيه بعد اعتقاد وجوده، إذ
كان عاقل يتسارع إلى أقل منه، ولا يصرف عنه كون الطريق إليه متوعرا، ومحوجا
إلى ترك لذات الدنيا، واحتمال أنواع من التعب هنا. فإن المدة في احتمال
التعب منحصرة، والفائت فيها قليل. واللذات الدنيوية منصرمة منقضية. والعاقل
يتيسر عليه ترك القليل نقدا في طلب أضعافه نسيئة. ولذلك ترى الخلق كلهم في
التجارات والصناعات، وحتى في طلب العلم، يحتملون من الذل والخسران، والتعب
والنصب، ما يعظم مقاساته طمعا في حصول لذة لهم في المستقبل، تزيد على ما
يفوتهم في الحال زيادة محدودة، فكيف لا يسمحون بتركه في الحال للتوصل إلى
مزايا غير مقدرة ولا محدودة. ولم يخلق في الدنيا عاقل هو حريص على طلب
المال، كلف بذل الدينار وانتظار شهر ليعتاض منه بعد مضي الشهر الإكسير
الأعظم الذي يقلب النحاس ذهبا إبريزا، إلا تسمح نفسه ببذله، وإن كان ذلك
فواتا في الحال. حتى أن من لم يحتمل ألم الجوع مثلا، في مثل هذه المدة
ليتوصل به إلى هذه النعم الجسيمة، لم يعد عاقلا، ولعل ذلك لا يتصور وجوده
في الخلق، مع أن الموت وراء الإنسان بالمرصاد، والذهب لا ينفع في الآخرة.
وربما يموت في الشهر أو بعد الشهر بيوم فلا ينتفع بالذهب. وكل ذلك لا يفتر
رأيه في البذل، طمعا في هذا العوض. فكيف يفتر رأي العاقل في مقاساة
الشهوات، في أيام العمر وأقصاها مائة سنة، والعوض الحاصل عنها سعادة لا آخر
لها؟ ولكن فتور الخلق عن سلوك طريق السعادة لضعف إيمانهم باليوم الآخر،
وإلا فالعقل الناقص قاض بالتشمير لسلوك طريق السعادة فضلا عن الكامل.

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: س ع د (sa-ʿa-da)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of ease, prosperity, and good fortune; the opposite of wretchedness (shaqāwah).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Saʿādah (happiness) is the state of being facilitated toward the good in this life and the next; ultimate saʿādah is the attainment of everlasting bliss in the Hereafter, which is the very object of human striving.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes worldly prosperity; metaphorical/theological usage extends to eternal felicity in the afterlife, which is the true and abiding happiness.
- Root: ط ل ب (ṭa-la-ba)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to search out, to demand; the act of pursuing something desired or required.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء، عينا كان أو معنى" — Seeking is the investigation into the existence of a thing, whether concrete or conceptual. The seeker (ṭālib) and the sought (maṭlūb) are paired terms in the Quranic lexicon.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to request or pursue a thing. Metaphorical: the soul's innate inclination toward what perfects it — here, the rational pursuit of eternal happiness over transient pleasure.
- Root: خ ل ق (kha-la-qa)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To measure, to proportion, to create; the act of bringing something into existence according to a determined measure.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation is fundamentally the act of right proportioning; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) or from another thing. The "creatures" (khalq) are all beings brought forth by divine measure.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's measuring and cutting. Metaphorical: God's creation of beings upon a measure necessitated by wisdom — hence "all creatures" (al-khalq) refers to all of humanity in their varied pursuits.
- Root: ش ه ر (sha-ha-ra)
 * Lisan / Ayn: A month; a period marked by the visibility of the new moon; that which is well-known or made public.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشهر: مدة مشهورة بإهلال الهلال" — The month is a duration made known by the sighting of the crescent. It is a finite, measured unit of time.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lunar month. Metaphorical: any limited, determinate period — here, the bounded span of worldly endurance contrasted with the unbounded eternity of the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is complete in itself, allowing for rhetorical emphasis and extended periodic structure without grammatical rupture.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The Shaykh, the Imām, the Illustrious, the Proof of Islam, the Ornament of the Religion, Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī al-Ṭūsī — may Allah Most High be pleased with him and grant him His satisfaction — said:

Since happiness (saʿādah), which is the quest of the first and the last, is attained only through knowledge and action; and since each of the two requires encompassing its true reality and its measure; and since it was incumbent to know knowledge and to distinguish it from what is other than it by a criterion — and we have completed that [in our work "The Criterion of Knowledge"] — so too it became incumbent to know the action that brings happiness, and to distinguish it from the action that brings misery. This likewise required a criterion. Therefore, I desired to plunge into this matter and to explain that languor in seeking happiness is folly; then to explain knowledge and the path of acquiring it; then to explain the action that brings happiness and its path. All of this in a manner that ascends beyond the limit of the path of blind imitation (taqlīd) to the limit of clarity — and were it to be exhaustively pursued in its true reality and the discourse lengthened therein, it would ascend to the limit of demonstration (burhān) upon the conditions which we have mentioned in "The Criterion of Knowledge." Although we shall not lengthen the discourse, we shall point to its principles and its canons.
The Exposition that Languor in Seeking Happiness is Folly

The otherworldly happiness (al-saʿādāt al-ākhirāwiyyah) which we mean is: abiding without perishing, pleasure without toil, joy without sorrow, wealth without poverty, perfection without deficiency, glory without abasement — and in sum, everything that can be conceived as sought by a seeker and desired by a desirer. And this is for all eternity (abad al-ābād), in a manner that the passing of ages and epochs does not diminish it. Nay, were we to suppose the world filled with pearls, and suppose a bird that snatches away, in every thousand years, a single grain from them, the pearls would be exhausted while nothing of all eternity would be diminished. This [happiness], then, needs no urging toward seeking it, nor any disparagement of languor therein, after the belief in its existence [is established] — for no rational person would hasten to something less than it, nor would he be turned away from it by the fact that the path to it is rugged, and that it necessitates abandoning the pleasures of this world and enduring various kinds of toil here. For the duration of enduring toil is finite, and what is lost therein is little, while worldly pleasures are cut off and passing away. And the rational person finds it easy to abandon a little in ready cash in pursuit of its multiples on credit. For this reason, you see all creatures in their trades and crafts — and even in seeking knowledge — enduring humiliation, loss, toil, and fatigue, the magnitude of whose endurance is great, out of hope for obtaining a pleasure in the future that exceeds what they miss in the present by a limited increase. How, then, would they not readily abandon the present for attaining advantages that are neither measured nor limited? And there has not been created in this world a rational person who is eager in seeking wealth, devoted to spending a dinar and waiting a month in order to receive, after the month has passed, the greatest elixir (al-iksīr al-aʿẓam) that turns copper into pure gold — except that his soul would readily spend it, even though that is a loss in the present. So much so that whoever would not endure the pain of hunger, for example, for such a duration, in order to attain thereby these immense blessings, would not be counted rational — and perhaps the existence of such a person among creatures is inconceivable — even though death lies in ambush behind man, and gold avails not in the Hereafter. And perhaps he dies within the month, or a day after the month, and so derives no benefit from the gold. Yet all of that does not weaken his resolve in spending, out of hope for this compensation. How, then, would the resolve of the rational person weaken in enduring the passions, during the days of his life — the utmost of which is a hundred years — when the compensation obtained thereby is a happiness that has no end? But the languor of creatures in traversing the path of happiness is due to the weakness of their faith in the Last Day. Otherwise, even the deficient intellect would judge it incumbent to gird oneself for traversing the path of happiness — let alone the perfect one.

### | AUTO INTRODUCTION

There is no wonder that Imām al-Ghazālī was distinguished and titled the Proof of Islam (Ḥujjat al-Islām) and its decisive separator (fayṣal). This is especially so when the researcher casts a scrutinizing glance upon his environment and circumstances, for he will encounter a host of cultural and social disorder — indeed, one might say cognitive disorder — for at him and through him converged a cluster of cognitive and intellectual currents that dominated the Eastern arena, expressing that inherited and emergent cognitive-cultural intermixture alike.

And whoever sounds the depths of Abū Ḥāmid's books will encounter something of contradiction and divergence: between one close to Greek philosophy in its entirety and a scholar in divine unity (tawḥīd); between one who magnifies and venerates organized rational thought and one who affirms the necessity of affective intuition (ḥads wijdānī) and luminous Sufi inspiration (ilhām ṣūfī nūrānī). Perhaps this sounder casts a glance at the surface and reads a preliminary reading, for successive readings unveil that cognitive intersection which converged at al-Ghazālī — while he, in the depth of his writings, adopts rational thought bound by the limits of faith as a first postulate and premise for departure. This on one hand; and on a second hand, al-Ghazālī was a philosopher pursuing the rational course within the realm of the finite and the intuitive-inspirational direction within the realm of the infinite, for reason falls short in that horizon of determination, certainty, and strict order.

The distinction of the Imām, the Proof, here is that very book before us, in which we ascend from Greek meanings to Islamic meanings — not by distortion, but by planting, naturalization, and pouring into Arabic molds, the like of which is rarely found among his peers.

So it is no wonder that *The Touchstone of Contemplation* was a turning point that followed *The Criterion of Knowledge* (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm), consolidating this complete digestion of logic and transforming it into Islamic meanings and a complete Arabic tongue.

We have assembled the introduction as follows:
- The cultural and intellectual environment.
- The social and economic environment.
- General political circumstances.
- The life of al-Ghazālī and his personality.
- The nature of the book and its subjects.

### | AUTO التقديم

لا غرابة في أن يتميز الإمام الغزالي ويلقب بحجة الإسلام وفيصله.
ولا سيما إذا ألقى الباحث نظرة فاحصة على بيئته وظروفه، حيث سيعثر على
جملة من الاضطراب الثقافي والاجتماعي، بل ويمكن القول المعرفي، إذ تقاطعت
عنده وبه مجموعة التيارات المعرفية والفكرية التي سادت ساحة المشرق معبرة
عن ذاك الاختلاط المعرفي والثقافي الموروث والحادث معا.
وإن السابر لكتب أبي حامد يعثر على شي ء من التعارض والتباين بين قريب
للفلسفة بأسها اليوناني وبين عالم في التوحيد، بين ممجد معظم للفكر العقلي
المنظم وبين آخذ بضرورة الحدس الوجداني والإلهام الصوفي النوراني. ولعل هذا
السابر يلقي نظرة على السطح ويقرأ قراءة أولية، إذ القراءات المتتالية تكشف
الغطاء عن ذاك التقاطع المعرفي الذي التقى عند الغزالي، بينما هو في عمق

كتاباته متبن للفكر العقلي الملتزم بحدود الإيمان فرضية ومسلمة أولى
للانطلاق، هذا من جهة، ومن جهة ثانية، كان الغزالي فيلسوفا آخذا بالمنحى
العقلي في إطار المتناهي وبالاتجاه الحدسي الإلهامي في إطار اللامتناهي إذ
العقل يعجز في ذاك الأفق عن التحديد واليقين والنظم الصارم.
إن ميزة الإمام الحجة هنا ذاك السفر الذي بين أيدينا وفيه نعرج من
المعاني اليونانية إلى المعاني الإسلامية ليس بتحوير إنما بغرس وتطبيع PageV01P003
وانسكاب بقوالب العربية قل نظيره عند مماثليه.
فلا عجب إن كان محك النظر نقطة تحول أعقبت معيار العلم فرسخت هذا الهضم
الكامل للمنطق وحولته إلى معاني إسلامية ولسن عربي كامل.
وقد جمعنا التقديم على ما يلي:
- البيئة الثقافية والفكرية.
- البيئة الاجتماعية والاقتصادية.
- الظروف السياسية العامة.
- حياة الغزالي وشخصيته.
- طبيعة الكتاب وموضوعاته.

PageV01P004

- Root: حكم (ḥ-k-m)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To judge, to arbitrate, to render a decisive verdict; the core sense of separating truth from falsehood with authority.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intellectual faculty of discernment (al-ʿaql) that distinguishes verity from error; the act of decisive judgment upon matters of knowledge.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the judge's ruling. Metaphorical (majāz): the mind's verdict upon a proposition, as in "the touchstone" (miḥakk) which tests the purity of metal.
- Root: نظر (n-ẓ-r)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To look, to gaze, to contemplate; the act of visual and intellectual inspection.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theoretical reflection (naẓar) as the systematic movement of thought toward knowledge; the rational scrutiny that yields certainty.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical: intellectual examination and deliberation, as in "the touchstone of contemplation" (miḥakk al-naẓar) — that which tests the validity of thought.
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; that which binds and restrains; the faculty of understanding and discernment.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The power prepared for the reception of knowledge, and the knowledge acquired thereby; the instrument of rational comprehension.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the rope that hobbles a camel. Metaphorical: the intellect that restrains the soul from error and binds one to sound judgment.
- Root: ميز (m-y-z)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To separate, to distinguish, to sift apart.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The separation between similar things; the power in the mind by which meanings are extracted and discerned.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to part one thing from another. Metaphorical: "It almost bursts with rage" (takādu tamayyazu min al-ghayẓ) — the intensity of differentiation.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, affirming the attribute exclusively to it and negating it from all else, as in "not by distortion, but by planting."

So it is no wonder that *The Touchstone of Contemplation* was a turning point that followed *The Criterion of Knowledge* (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm), consolidating this complete digestion of logic and transforming it into Islamic meanings and a complete Arabic tongue.

We have assembled the introduction as follows:
- The cultural and intellectual environment.
- The social and economic environment.
- General political circumstances.
- The life of al-Ghazālī and his personality.
- The nature of the book and its subjects.

paragraphs.text: Know that this chapter is of immense importance, so I desired to present it first due to the universal need for it. A group of our companions have authored works on this subject, among them Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṣaymarī, the teacher of the author of al-Ḥāwī; then al-Khaṭīb Abū Bakr al-Ḥāfiẓ al-Baghdādī; then the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ. Each of them mentioned precious gems (nafāʾis) that the other two did not mention. I have studied the books of all three and summarized from them a concise compilation encompassing everything of importance they mentioned, and I have added to it precious gems from the scattered statements of our companions. And with Allah is success.
**An Introduction on the Importance of Issuing Legal Rulings (Iftāʾ), the Gravity of Its Danger, and Its Great Merit**

Know that issuing legal rulings (al-iftāʾ) is of grave consequence, great standing, and abundant merit — because the muftī is the heir of the prophets, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them, and is the one fulfilling the communal obligation (farḍ al-kifāyah). However, he is exposed to error.
For this reason, they said: "The muftī is the one who reports on behalf of Allah, the Exalted" (al-muftī muwaqqiʿ ʿan Allāh taʿālā).
We have narrated from Ibn al-Munkadir that he said: "The scholar stands between Allah, the Exalted, and His creation — so let him consider carefully how he enters between them."

We have narrated from the Salaf (righteous predecessors) and the virtuous among the later generations many well-known instances of refraining from issuing legal rulings (al-tawaqquf ʿan al-fatwā). We shall mention some of them as a means of blessing (tabarrukan).

We have narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā that he said: "I encountered one hundred and twenty of the Anṣār from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah pray upon him and grant him peace. When one of them was asked about a legal question, he would refer it to another, and that one to another, until it would return to the first one."

In another narration: "Not one of them would narrate a ḥadīth except that he wished his brother had sufficed him of it, and not one would be asked for a legal ruling except that he wished his brother had sufficed him of the fatwā."
It is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Whoever issues legal rulings on everything he is asked about is insane."

It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī, al-Ḥasan, and Abū Ḥuṣayn — with the ḥāʾ opened (fatḥ al-ḥāʾ) — the tābiʿūn, that they said: "Indeed, one of you issues a legal ruling on a question which, had it been presented to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, he would have gathered for it the people of Badr."
It is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, the tābiʿī: "I encountered people such that when one of them was asked about something, he would speak while trembling."
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān: "When the scholar neglects saying 'I do not know' (lā adrī), his vital points have been struck."
It is narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah and Saḥnūn: "The boldest of people in issuing legal rulings is the least of them in knowledge."

It is narrated from al-Shāfiʿī — and he had been asked about a question and did not answer, so it was said to him [about that], whereupon he said: "Until I know whether the merit lies in silence or in answering."
It is narrated from al-Athram: "I heard Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal frequently saying 'I do not know' (lā adrī) — and that was regarding matters in which the various opinions were known."
It is narrated from al-Haytham ibn Jamīl: "I witnessed Mālik being asked forty-eight questions, and he said 'I do not know' regarding thirty-two of them."

It is also narrated from Mālik that he would sometimes be asked fifty questions and would not answer even one of them. He used to say: "Whoever answers a question — before answering, he should present himself before Paradise and the Fire and consider how his deliverance will be, then answer."
He was asked about a question and said "I do not know," so it was said to him: "It is a light, easy question." He became angry and said: "There is nothing light in knowledge."

Al-Shāfiʿī said: "I have never seen anyone in whom Allah, the Exalted, gathered the instruments of legal ruling (ālat al-fatwā) as He gathered them in Ibn ʿUyaynah — yet more silent than him regarding legal rulings."

Abū Ḥanīfah said: "Were it not for the fear of Allah, the Exalted, that knowledge would be lost, I would not have issued legal rulings — for they have the pleasure (al-mahnaʾ) and upon me lies the burden (al-wizr)."
Their statements on this matter are numerous and well-known.

Al-Ṣaymarī and al-Khaṭīb said: "Rarely does one who eagerly pursues legal rulings, races toward it, and persists upon it — except that his divine assistance (tawfīq) diminishes and his affairs become disordered. But if he is averse to it, not preferring it as long as he finds an alternative (mandūḥah), and refers the matter to others — then Allah's assistance to him is greater, and correctness in his answers is more predominant."

They cited as evidence his saying, may Allah pray upon him and grant him peace, in the authentic ḥadīth: "Do not ask for positions of authority (al-imārah), for if you are given it due to your asking, you will be entrusted to it; but if you are given it without asking, you will be aided upon it."
**A Section on Knowing Who is Qualified for Issuing Legal Rulings**

Al-Khaṭīb said: "It behooves the Imām (ruler) to examine the conditions of the muftīs. Whoever is qualified for issuing legal rulings, he should confirm him; and whoever is not qualified, he should prevent him, forbid him from returning to it, and threaten him with punishment if he returns."
The way for the Imām to know who is qualified for legal rulings is that he should ask the scholars of his time and rely upon the reports of trustworthy persons.

Then he narrated with his chain of transmission from Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "I did not issue legal rulings until seventy witnesses testified for me that I was qualified for that."
In another narration: "I did not issue legal rulings until I asked those more knowledgeable than myself whether they saw me as a suitable place for that."
Mālik said: "It is not fitting for a man to consider himself qualified for anything until he asks those more knowledgeable than himself."

paragraphs.text:
OpenITI#

# 
# آداب الفتوى والمفتي والمستفتي
# اعلم أن هذا الباب مهم جدا فأحببت تقديمه لعموم الحاجة إليه وقد صنف في

هذا جماعة من أصحابنا منهم أبو القاسم الصيمري شيخ صاحب الحاوي ثم الخطيب

أبو بكر الحافظ البغدادي ثم الشيخ أبو عمرو ابن الصلاح وكل منهم ذكر نفائس

لم يذكرها الآخران وقد طالعت كتب الثلاثة ولخصت منها جملة مختصرة مستوعبة

لكل ما ذكروه من المهم وضممت إليها نفائس من متفرقات كلام الأصحاب وبالله

التوفيق

| مقدمة في أهمية الإفتاء وعظم خطره وفضله
# اعلم أن الإفتاء عظيم الخطر كبير الموقع كثير الفضل لأن المفتي وارث

الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم وقائم بفرض الكفاية لكنه معرض للخطأ
# 
# ولهذا قالوا المفتي موقع عن الله تعالى
# وروينا عن ابن المنكدر قال العالم بين الله تعالى وخلقه فلينظر كيف يدخل

بينهم
# وروينا عن السلف وفضلاء الخلف من التوقف عن الفتيا أشياء كثيرة معروفة

نذكر منها أحرفا تبركا
# وروينا عن عبد الرحمن ابن أبي ليلى قال أدركت عشرين ومئة من الأنصار من

أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل أحدهم عن المسألة فيردها هذا إلى

هذا وهذا إلى هذا حتى ترجع إلى الأول
# وفي رواية ما منهم من يحدث بحديث إلا ود أن أخاه كفاه إياه ولا يستفتى عن

شيء إلا ود أن أخاه كفاه الفتيا
# وعن ابن مسعود وابن عباس رضي الله عنهم من أفتى في كل ما يسأل فهو مجنون
# 
# وعن الشعبي والحسن وأبي حصين بفتح الحاء التابعيين قالوا إن أحدكم ليفتي

في المسألة ولو وردت على عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لجمع لها أهل بدر
# وعن عطاء بن السائب التابعي أدركت أقواما يسأل أحدهم عن الشيء فيتكلم وهو

يرعد
# وعن ابن عباس ومحمد بن عجلان إذا أغفل العالم لا أدري أصيبت مقاتله
# وعن سفيان بن عيينة وسحنون أجسر الناس على الفتيا أقلهم علما
# وعن الشافعي وقد سئل عن مسألة فلم يجب فقيل له فقال حتى أدري أن الفضل في

السكوت أو في الجواب
# وعن الأثرم سمعت أحمد بن حنبل يكثر أن يقول لا أدري وذلك فيما عرف

الأقاويل فيه
# 
# وعن الهيثم بن جميل شهدت مالكا سئل عن ثمان وأربعين مسألة فقال في ثنتين

وثلاثين منها لا أدري
# وعن مالك أيضا أنه ربما كان يسأل عن خمسين مسألة فلا يجيب في واحدة منها

وكان يقول من أجاب في مسألة فينبغي قبل الجواب أن يعرض نفسه على الجنة

والنار وكيف خلاصه ثم يجيب
# وسئل عن مسألة فقال لا أدري فقيل هي مسألة خفيفة سهلة فغضب وقال ليس في

العلم شيء خفيف
# وقال الشافعي ما رأيت أحدا جمع الله تعالى فيه من آلة الفتيا ما جمع في

ابن عيينة أسكت منه على الفتيا
# وقال أبو حنيفة لولا الفرق من الله تعالى أن يضيع العلم ما أفتيت يكون

لهم المهنأ وعلي الوزر
# وأقوالهم في هذا كثيرة معروفة
# 
# قال الصيمري والخطيب وقل من حرص على الفتيا وسابق إليها وثابر عليها إلا

قل توفيقه واضطرب في أمره وإن كان كارها لذلك غير موثر له ما وجد عنه

مندوحة وأحال الأمر فيه على غيره كانت المعونة له من الله أكثر والصلاح في

جوابه أغلب
# واستدلا بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الصحيح لا تسأل الإمارة فإنك

إن أعطيتها عن مسألة أو كلت إليها وإن أعطتها عن غير مسألة أعنت عليها

| فصل في معرفة من يصلح للفتوى
# قال الخطيب ينبغي للإمام أن يتصفح أحوال المفتين فمن صلح للفتيا أقره ومن

لا يصلح منعه ونهاه أن يعود وتواعده بالعقوبة إن عاد وطريق
# 
# الإمام إلى معرفة من يصلح الفتيا أن يسأل علماء وقته ويعتمد أخبار

الموثوق بهم
# ثم روى بإسناده عن مالك رحمه الله قال ما أفتيت حتى شهد لي سبعون أني أهل

لذلك
# وفي رواية ما أفتيت حتى سألت من هو أعلم مني هل يراني موضعا لذلك
# قال مالك ولا ينبغي لرجل أن يرى نفسه أهلا لشيء حتى يسأل من هو أعلم منه

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: فتي (f-t-y)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes youth, freshness, and by extension, clarity and cutting decisiveness — the young man (fatā) who cuts through ambiguity; the muftī is one who cuts through legal ambiguity with decisive clarity.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fatwā is the clarification of a legal matter (bayān al-ḥukm); the muftī stands as the heir of prophetic function in explaining God's command.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the act of giving a definitive answer to a question. Metaphorical (majāz): the muftī as one who "cuts" (yaqtāʿ) the matter decisively, like a young man's sharp resolve.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the marking/tracing of a path (taʿlīm as branding); the ʿālim is one marked by God's signs.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is apprehension of a thing by its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi) — two kinds: apprehension of essence, and judgment upon existence.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as certainty. Metaphorical: "he is from the lofty banners (aʿlām) of knowledge" — the scholar as a visible landmark guiding travelers.
- Root: دري (d-r-y)
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Dirāyah is knowledge attained through skillful means (maʿrifah mudrakah bi-ḍarb min al-ḥiyal) — perceptive discernment.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to know with penetration. Metaphorical: mudārāh — gentle coaxing, as if outwitting (mukhātalah) the other to reach truth.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification (Bāb al-Takhṣīṣ) — the conditional restriction of general statements by subsequent qualifiers, as in "the muftī is an heir of the prophets" being specified by "but he is exposed to error."
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)

Know that this chapter is of immense importance, so I desired to present it first due to the universal need for it. A group of our companions have authored works on this subject, among them Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṣaymarī, the teacher of the author of al-Ḥāwī; then al-Khaṭīb Abū Bakr al-Ḥāfiẓ al-Baghdādī; then the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ. Each of them mentioned precious gems (nafāʾis) that the other two did not mention. I have studied the books of all three and summarized from them a concise compilation encompassing everything of importance they mentioned, and I have added to it precious gems from the scattered statements of our companions. And with Allah is success.
**An Introduction on the Importance of Issuing Legal Rulings (Iftāʾ), the Gravity of Its Danger, and Its Great Merit**

Know that issuing legal rulings (al-iftāʾ) is of grave consequence, great standing, and abundant merit — because the muftī is the heir of the prophets, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them, and is the one fulfilling the communal obligation (farḍ al-kifāyah). However, he is exposed to error.
For this reason, they said: "The muftī is the one who reports on behalf of Allah, the Exalted" (al-muftī muwaqqiʿ ʿan Allāh taʿālā).
We have narrated from Ibn al-Munkadir that he said: "The scholar stands between Allah, the Exalted, and His creation — so let him consider carefully how he enters between them."

We have narrated from the Salaf (righteous predecessors) and the virtuous among the later generations many well-known instances of refraining from issuing legal rulings (al-tawaqquf ʿan al-fatwā). We shall mention some of them as a means of blessing (tabarrukan).

We have narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā that he said: "I encountered one hundred and twenty of the Anṣār from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah pray upon him and grant him peace. When one of them was asked about a legal question, he would refer it to another, and that one to another, until it would return to the first one."

In another narration: "Not one of them would narrate a ḥadīth except that he wished his brother had sufficed him of it, and not one would be asked for a legal ruling except that he wished his brother had sufficed him of the fatwā."
It is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Whoever issues legal rulings on everything he is asked about is insane."

It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī, al-Ḥasan, and Abū Ḥuṣayn — with the ḥāʾ opened (fatḥ al-ḥāʾ) — the tābiʿūn, that they said: "Indeed, one of you issues a legal ruling on a question which, had it been presented to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, he would have gathered for it the people of Badr."
It is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, the tābiʿī: "I encountered people such that when one of them was asked about something, he would speak while trembling."
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān: "When the scholar neglects saying 'I do not know' (lā adrī), his vital points have been struck."
It is narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah and Saḥnūn: "The boldest of people in issuing legal rulings is the least of them in knowledge."

It is narrated from al-Shāfiʿī — and he had been asked about a question and did not answer, so it was said to him [about that], whereupon he said: "Until I know whether the merit lies in silence or in answering."
It is narrated from al-Athram: "I heard Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal frequently saying 'I do not know' (lā adrī) — and that was regarding matters in which the various opinions were known."
It is narrated from al-Haytham ibn Jamīl: "I witnessed Mālik being asked forty-eight questions, and he said 'I do not know' regarding thirty-two of them."

It is also narrated from Mālik that he would sometimes be asked fifty questions and would not answer even one of them. He used to say: "Whoever answers a question — before answering, he should present himself before Paradise and the Fire and consider how his deliverance will be, then answer."
He was asked about a question and said "I do not know," so it was said to him: "It is a light, easy question." He became angry and said: "There is nothing light in knowledge."

Al-Shāfiʿī said: "I have never seen anyone in whom Allah, the Exalted, gathered the instruments of legal ruling (ālat al-fatwā) as He gathered them in Ibn ʿUyaynah — yet more silent than him regarding legal rulings."

Abū Ḥanīfah said: "Were it not for the fear of Allah, the Exalted, that knowledge would be lost, I would not have issued legal rulings — for they have the pleasure (al-mahnaʾ) and upon me lies the burden (al-wizr)."
Their statements on this matter are numerous and well-known.

Al-Ṣaymarī and al-Khaṭīb said: "Rarely does one who eagerly pursues legal rulings, races toward it, and persists upon it — except that his divine assistance (tawfīq) diminishes and his affairs become disordered. But if he is averse to it, not preferring it as long as he finds an alternative (mandūḥah), and refers the matter to others — then Allah's assistance to him is greater, and correctness in his answers is more predominant."

They cited as evidence his saying, may Allah pray upon him and grant him peace, in the authentic ḥadīth: "Do not ask for positions of authority (al-imārah), for if you are given it due to your asking, you will be entrusted to it; but if you are given it without asking, you will be aided upon it."
**A Section on Knowing Who is Qualified for Issuing Legal Rulings**

Al-Khaṭīb said: "It behooves the Imām (ruler) to examine the conditions of the muftīs. Whoever is qualified for issuing legal rulings, he should confirm him; and whoever is not qualified, he should prevent him, forbid him from returning to it, and threaten him with punishment if he returns."
The way for the Imām to know who is qualified for legal rulings is that he should ask the scholars of his time and rely upon the reports of trustworthy persons.

Then he narrated with his chain of transmission from Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "I did not issue legal rulings until seventy witnesses testified for me that I was qualified for that."
In another narration: "I did not issue legal rulings until I asked those more knowledgeable than myself whether they saw me as a suitable place for that."
Mālik said: "It is not fitting for a man to consider himself qualified for anything until he asks those more knowledgeable than himself."

EPUB/chap_01.xhtml.title: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 1: The Author's Introduction and Praise

paragraphs.text: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Our Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the ascetic, the scrupulous, Muḥyī al-Dīn Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf ibn Murrā ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥusayn ibn Ḥizām al-Nawawī — may God Most High have mercy upon him — said: Amen.

Praise be to God, the Benign, the Munificent, whose blessings are too vast to be enumerated or counted; the Creator of subtle kindness (al-luṭf) and right guidance; the Guide to the path of rectitude; the One who grants success through His generosity to the ways of soundness; the Bestower of favor by His care for the Sunnah of His Beloved, His Intimate Friend, His Servant, and His Messenger — may God's blessings and peace be upon him and upon those whom He has graciously favored among His servants; the One who singled out this Community (al-ummah) — may God increase it in honor — with the knowledge of the chain of transmission (ʿilm al-isnād), in which no other nation has shared with it across the succession of ages and epochs; the One who appointed for the preservation of this noble, honorable, and purified Sunnah select individuals among the hadith masters and critical examiners (al-ḥuffāẓ al-nuqqād), and made them its defenders throughout all times and lands, expending their utmost capacity in clarifying the sound from the corrupt among its chains, out of fear of diminishment from it or increase [of corruption], and for its preservation on behalf of the Community — may God increase it in honor — until the Day of Summoning (yawm al-tanād); exhausting their efforts in deep comprehension (al-tafaqquh) of its meanings and in extracting rulings and subtle points (al-latāʾif) from it; persisting in that both in groups and individually; striving earnestly in its elucidation and the clarification of its aspects with seriousness and diligence. And there shall not cease, by God's praise and His grace, groups undertaking this throughout all ages until the end of the world and the approach of the Final Return (al-maʿād), even if some lands among them have become desolate and they have neared extinction.

I praise Him with the most complete praise for His blessings, especially for the blessing of Islam, and for having made us part of the Community of the best of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors — Muḥammad, His servant, His Messenger, His Beloved, and His Intimate Friend, the Seal of the Prophets, the Possessor of the Great Intercession (al-shafāʿah al-ʿuẓmā), the Banner of Praise (liwāʾ al-ḥamd), and the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd), the Master of the Messengers, singled out for the dazzling miracle (al-muʿjizah al-bāhirah) that endures across the succession of years, with which he challenged the most eloquent of generations, and by which he silenced the disputants, and through which the disgrace of those who obstinately refused to submit to it became manifest — [that miracle] preserved from any alteration by the heretics (al-mulḥidīn) ever reaching it. I mean by that the Mighty Qurʾān, the speech of our Lord, which the Trustworthy Spirit (al-rūḥ al-amīn) descended with upon his heart, that he might be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue.

And he was chosen with other miracles exceeding one thousand in number, and with the comprehensive words (jawāmiʿ al-kalim), and the leniency of his sacred law, and the removal of the burdens of those who came before. He was honored by the preference of his Community — may God increase it in honor — over the nations that preceded, and by the fact that his Companions — may God be pleased with them — are the best of the generations that have been, and that all of them are decisively affirmed as upright (maqṭūʿ bi-ʿadālatihim) according to those whose opinion is relied upon among the scholars of the Muslims. And He made the consensus (ijmāʿ) of his Community a decisive proof, like the Clear Book (al-kitāb al-mubīn), and the statements of his Companions spread without opposition to that among the verifying scholars. He was singled out by the abundance of motives among his Community — may God increase it in honor — for the preservation of his sacred law, its codification, its transmission from the authoritative hadith masters (al-ḥuffāẓ al-musnidīn), and its reception from the skilled and God-conscious experts, and for diligence in clarifying it to those seeking guidance, and perseverance in teaching it, seeking the pleasure of the Lord of the Worlds, and for exertion in defending its methodology with clear proofs and in suppressing the heretics and innovators (al-mulḥidīn wa-al-mubtadiʿīn). May God's blessings and peace be upon him, upon all the other prophets, upon the families of each, upon their Companions, the Followers (al-tābiʿīn), and all of God's righteous servants. And may He grant us success in following him perpetually in his words, his deeds, and all his states, sincerely and persistently in that, diligently.

And I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner to Him, affirming His oneness and acknowledging what is obligatory upon all of creation of submission to His lordship. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, chosen from among His creation, singled out for the comprehensiveness of his message and the preference of his Community — may God's blessings and peace be upon him, upon his family, his Companions, and his progeny.

To proceed: Verily, engagement in knowledge is among the most virtuous acts of drawing near [to God] (al-qurub), the most exalted of acts of obedience, the most important of the types of good, and the most emphatic of acts of worship. It is the most worthy thing in which the precious moments of time should be spent, and toward the attainment and mastery of which those of pure breaths have girded themselves, and to which the hasteners to good deeds have rushed with concern, and toward adorning themselves with which the contenders for noble honors have raced. Numerous verses of the Qurʾān, well-known authentic hadiths, and the luminous statements of the Salaf — may God be pleased with them — have concurred upon what I have mentioned. There is no need to cite them here, for they are among the clear and evident matters.

And among the most important types of knowledge is the verified understanding of the prophetic hadiths (al-aḥādīth al-nabawiyyah) — I mean the knowledge of their texts (mutūn): their sound (ṣaḥīḥ), their good (ḥasan), and their weak (ḍaʿīf); their continuous (muttaṣil), their interrupted (mursal), their broken-chain (munqaṭiʿ), their problematic (muʿḍal), their inverted (maqlūb), their well-known (mashhūr), their rare (gharīb), their strong (ʿazīz), their mass-transmitted (mutawātir), their solitary (āḥād), their individual (afrād), their recognized (maʿrūf), their anomalous (shādhdh), their rejected (munkar), and their defective (muʿallal).

# 
# صحيح مسلم شرح النووي
# 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال شيخنا الامام العالم الزاهد الورع محي الدين

يحيى بن شرف بن مرى بن حسن بن حسين بن حزام النووي رحمه الله تعالى آمين

الحمد لله البر الجواد الذي جلت نعمه عن الاحصاء والاعداد خالق اللطف

والارشاد الهادى إلى سبيل الرشاد الموفق بكرمه لطرق السداد المان بالاعتناء

بسنة حبيبه وخليله عبده ورسوله صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعلى من لطف به من

العباد المخصص هذه الامة زادها الله شرفا بعلم الاسناد الذي لم يشركها فيه

أحد من الأمم على تكرر العصور والآباد الذي نصب لحفظ هذه السنة المكرمة

الشريفة المطهرة خواص من الحفاظ النقاد وجعلهم ذابين عنها في جميع الازمان

والبلاد باذلين وسعهم في تبيين الصحة من طرقها والفساد خوفا من الانتقاص

منها والازدياد وحفظا لها على الأمة زادها الله شرفا إلى يوم التناد

مستفرغين جهدهم في التفقه في معانيها واستخراج الاحكام واللطائف منها

مستمرين على ذلك في جماعات وآحاد مبالغين في بيانها وايضاح وجوهها بالجد

والاجتهاد ولا يزال على القيام بذلك بحمد الله ولطفه جماعات في الاعصار

كلها إلى انقضاء الدنيا واقبال المعاد وان قلو وخملت بلدان منهم وقربوا من

النفاد أحمده أبلغ حمد على نعمه خصوصا على نعمة الاسلام وأن جعلنا من أمة

خير الأولين والآخرين وأكرم السابقين واللاحقين محمد عبده ورسوله وحبيبه

وخليله خاتم النبيين صاحب الشفاعة العظمى ولواء الحمد والمقام المحمود سيد

المرسلين المخصوص بالمعجزة الباهرة المستمرة على تكرر السنين التي تحدى بها

أفصح القرون وأفحم بها المنازعين وظهر بها خزي من لم ينقد لها من المعاندين

المحفوظة من أن يتطرق اليها تغيير الملحدين أعنى بها القرآن العزيز كلام

ربنا الذي نزل به الروح الأمين على قلبه ليكون من المنذرين بلسان عربي مبين

والمصطفى بمعجزات أخر زائدات على الألف والمئين وبجوامع الكلم وسماحة

شريعته ووضع اصر المتقدمين المكرم بتفضيل أمته زادها الله شرفا
# 
# على الأمم السابقين وبكون أصحابه رضي الله عنهم خير القرون الكائنين

وبأنهم كلهم مقطوع بعدالتهم عند من يعتد به من علماء المسلمين ويجعل اجماع

أمته حجة مقطوعا بها كالكتاب المبين وأقوال أصحابه المنتشرة من غير مخالفة

لذلك عند العلماء المحققين المخصوص بتوفر دواعي أمته زادها الله شرفا على

حفظ شريعته وتدوينها ونقلها عن الحفاظ المسندين وأخذها عن الحذاق المتقين

والاجتهاد في تبيينها للمسترشدين والدؤوب في تعليمها احتسابا لرضا رب

العالمين والمبالغة في الذب عن منهاجه بواضح الأدلة وقمع الملحدين

والمبتدعين صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعلى سائر النبيين وآل كل وصحابتهم

والتابعين وسائر عباد الله الصالحين ووفقنا للاقتداء به دائمين في أقواله

وأفعاله وسائر أحواله مخلصين مستمرين في ذلك دائبين وأشهد أن لا اله

الاالله وحده لا شريك له اقرارا بوحدانيته واعترافا بما يجب على الخلق كافة

من الاذعان لربوبيته واشهد ان محمد عبده ورسوله المصطفى من بريته والمخصوص

بشمول رسالته وتفضيل امته صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعلى آله واصحابه وعترته

اما بعد فإن الاشتغال بالعلم من افضل القرب واجل الطاعات واهم انواع الخير

وآكد العبادات واولى ما انفقت فيه نفائس الأوقات وشمر في ادراكه والتمكن

فيه اصحاب الانفاس الزكيات وبادر إلى الاهتمام به المسارعون إلى الخيرات

وسابق إلى التحلى به مستبقو المكرمات وقد تظاهرت على ما ذكرته جمل من

الآيات الكريمات والاحاديث الصحيحة المشهورات واقاويل السلف رضىالله عنهم

النيرات ولاضرورة لذكرها هنا لكونها من الواضحات الجليات ومن اهم انواع

العلوم تحقيق معرفة الاحاديث النبويات اعني معرفة متونها صحيحها وحسنها

وضعيفها متصلها ومرسلها ومنقطعها ومعضلعا ومقلوبها ومشهورها وغريبها

وعزيزها متوارتها وآحادها وافرادها معروفها وشاذها ومنكرها ومعللها

اما بعد فإن الاشتغال بالعلم من افضل القرب واجل الطاعات واهم انواع الخير

وآكد العبادات واولى ما انفقت فيه نفائس الأوقات وشمر في ادراكه والتمكن

فيه اصحاب الانفاس الزكيات وبادر إلى الاهتمام به المسارعون إلى الخيرات

وسابق إلى التحلى به مستبقو المكرمات وقد تظاهرت على ما ذكرته جمل من

الآيات الكريمات والاحاديث الصحيحة المشهورات واقاويل السلف رضىالله عنهم

النيرات ولاضرورة لذكرها هنا لكونها من الواضحات الجليات ومن اهم انواع

العلوم تحقيق معرفة الاحاديث النبويات اعني معرفة متونها صحيحها وحسنها

وضعيفها متصلها ومرسلها ومنقطعها ومعضلعا ومقلوبها ومشهورها وغريبها

وعزيزها متوارتها وآحادها وافرادها معروفها وشاذها ومنكرها ومعللها

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes praise, commendation, and gratitude directed toward one who is deserving by virtue of beneficence.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When applied to God, ḥamd signifies praise for His absolute perfection and boundless grace; it is the theological acknowledgment of divine beneficence (niʿmah) as an act of worship.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is praise for specific excellence; metaphorical (majāz) extends to praising an act, a place, or a quality, as in "I praised his conduct."
- Root: كرم (K-R-M)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes nobility, generosity, and honor; the noble one (karīm) is one whose goodness is manifest.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When predicated of God, karam is His name for overflowing beneficence and grace; when of man, it denotes praiseworthy character and actions, only realized when manifested.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: honor and generosity shown to another; metaphorical: a land "generous" in vegetation, or clouds "generous" in rain.
- Root: زاد (Z-Y-D)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes increase, augmentation, and surplus.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Increase (ziyādah) is that which is added to a thing's essence; it may be praiseworthy (as in growth in faith) or blameworthy (as excess beyond need).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: quantitative addition; metaphorical: intensification of a quality or state.
- Root: لطف (L-Ṭ-F)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes subtlety, gentleness, and refined kindness; also divine grace that reaches creation imperceptibly.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine luṭf is God's subtle beneficence in guiding and aiding His servants through means imperceptible to them.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical smallness or delicacy; metaphorical: spiritual subtlety and gracious providence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Allows for extended subordinate clauses between a preposition and its object, as in the long chains of relative clauses and descriptive phrases here, which are grammatically permissible when the intervening material is semantically integral to the sentence.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Our Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the ascetic, the scrupulous, Muḥyī al-Dīn Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf ibn Murrā ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥusayn ibn Ḥizām al-Nawawī — may God Most High have mercy upon him — said: Amen.

Praise be to God, the Benign, the Munificent, whose blessings are too vast to be enumerated or counted; the Creator of subtle kindness (al-luṭf) and right guidance; the Guide to the path of rectitude; the One who grants success through His generosity to the ways of soundness; the Bestower of favor by His care for the Sunnah of His Beloved, His Intimate Friend, His Servant, and His Messenger — may God's blessings and peace be upon him and upon those whom He has graciously favored among His servants; the One who singled out this Community (al-ummah) — may God increase it in honor — with the knowledge of the chain of transmission (ʿilm al-isnād), in which no other nation has shared with it across the succession of ages and epochs; the One who appointed for the preservation of this noble, honorable, and purified Sunnah select individuals among the hadith masters and critical examiners (al-ḥuffāẓ al-nuqqād), and made them its defenders throughout all times and lands, expending their utmost capacity in clarifying the sound from the corrupt among its chains, out of fear of diminishment from it or increase [of corruption], and for its preservation on behalf of the Community — may God increase it in honor — until the Day of Summoning (yawm al-tanād); exhausting their efforts in deep comprehension (al-tafaqquh) of its meanings and in extracting rulings and subtle points (al-latāʾif) from it; persisting in that both in groups and individually; striving earnestly in its elucidation and the clarification of its aspects with seriousness and diligence. And there shall not cease, by God's praise and His grace, groups undertaking this throughout all ages until the end of the world and the approach of the Final Return (al-maʿād), even if some lands among them have become desolate and they have neared extinction.

I praise Him with the most complete praise for His blessings, especially for the blessing of Islam, and for having made us part of the Community of the best of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors — Muḥammad, His servant, His Messenger, His Beloved, and His Intimate Friend, the Seal of the Prophets, the Possessor of the Great Intercession (al-shafāʿah al-ʿuẓmā), the Banner of Praise (liwāʾ al-ḥamd), and the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd), the Master of the Messengers, singled out for the dazzling miracle (al-muʿjizah al-bāhirah) that endures across the succession of years, with which he challenged the most eloquent of generations, and by which he silenced the disputants, and through which the disgrace of those who obstinately refused to submit to it became manifest — [that miracle] preserved from any alteration by the heretics (al-mulḥidīn) ever reaching it. I mean by that the Mighty Qurʾān, the speech of our Lord, which the Trustworthy Spirit (al-rūḥ al-amīn) descended with upon his heart, that he might be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue.

And he was chosen with other miracles exceeding one thousand in number, and with the comprehensive words (jawāmiʿ al-kalim), and the leniency of his sacred law, and the removal of the burdens of those who came before. He was honored by the preference of his Community — may God increase it in honor — over the nations that preceded, and by the fact that his Companions — may God be pleased with them — are the best of the generations that have been, and that all of them are decisively affirmed as upright (maqṭūʿ bi-ʿadālatihim) according to those whose opinion is relied upon among the scholars of the Muslims. And He made the consensus (ijmāʿ) of his Community a decisive proof, like the Clear Book (al-kitāb al-mubīn), and the statements of his Companions spread without opposition to that among the verifying scholars. He was singled out by the abundance of motives among his Community — may God increase it in honor — for the preservation of his sacred law, its codification, its transmission from the authoritative hadith masters (al-ḥuffāẓ al-musnidīn), and its reception from the skilled and God-conscious experts, and for diligence in clarifying it to those seeking guidance, and perseverance in teaching it, seeking the pleasure of the Lord of the Worlds, and for exertion in defending its methodology with clear proofs and in suppressing the heretics and innovators (al-mulḥidīn wa-al-mubtadiʿīn). May God's blessings and peace be upon him, upon all the other prophets, upon the families of each, upon their Companions, the Followers (al-tābiʿīn), and all of God's righteous servants. And may He grant us success in following him perpetually in his words, his deeds, and all his states, sincerely and persistently in that, diligently.

And I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner to Him, affirming His oneness and acknowledging what is obligatory upon all of creation of submission to His lordship. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, chosen from among His creation, singled out for the comprehensiveness of his message and the preference of his Community — may God's blessings and peace be upon him, upon his family, his Companions, and his progeny.

To proceed: Verily, engagement in knowledge is among the most virtuous acts of drawing near [to God] (al-qurub), the most exalted of acts of obedience, the most important of the types of good, and the most emphatic of acts of worship. It is the most worthy thing in which the precious moments of time should be spent, and toward the attainment and mastery of which those of pure breaths have girded themselves, and to which the hasteners to good deeds have rushed with concern, and toward adorning themselves with which the contenders for noble honors have raced. Numerous verses of the Qurʾān, well-known authentic hadiths, and the luminous statements of the Salaf — may God be pleased with them — have concurred upon what I have mentioned. There is no need to cite them here, for they are among the clear and evident matters.

And among the most important types of knowledge is the verified understanding of the prophetic hadiths (al-aḥādīth al-nabawiyyah) — I mean the knowledge of their texts (mutūn): their sound (ṣaḥīḥ), their good (ḥasan), and their weak (ḍaʿīf); their continuous (muttaṣil), their interrupted (mursal), their broken-chain (munqaṭiʿ), their problematic (muʿḍal), their inverted (maqlūb), their well-known (mashhūr), their rare (gharīb), their strong (ʿazīz), their mass-transmitted (mutawātir), their solitary (āḥād), their individual (afrād), their recognized (maʿrūf), their anomalous (shādhdh), their rejected (munkar), and their defective (muʿallal).

EPUB/chap_01.xhtml.title: Gardens of the Righteous — Section 1 (Author's Introduction & Opening Homily)

paragraphs.text: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Indeed, all praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, we seek His aid, and we seek His forgiveness. And we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our own souls and from the wickedness of our deeds. Whomsoever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whomsoever He leads astray, none can guide. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him.

«And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, His trustee over His revelation, His chosen one from among His creation, and His envoy between Him and His servants — sent with the upright religion and the straight path. Allah sent him as a mercy to the worlds, an Imam for the God-fearing, and a proof against all of creation» (1).

{«O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims»} [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. {«O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever over you an Observer»} [al-Nisāʾ: 1]. {«O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice — He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment»} [al-Aḥzāb: 70–71].

To proceed: I praise Allah — first and last, outwardly and inwardly — upon the completion of the work on this great book, "Gardens of the Righteous" (Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn). It is that book which was among the very first scholarly texts I read, and I have continually returned to this book, memorized its hadiths, and advised people to give it their utmost care — because of its immense virtue, its comprehensive selection of prophetic traditions, and its arrangement into chapters of righteousness and piety.

EPUB/chap_01.xhtml.title: The Epitome of Legal Judgments — Section 1: The Obligation to Follow the Authentic Sunnah and the Methodology of This Abridgment

paragraphs.text: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the worker [of righteous deeds], the abstinent, the ascetic, the ḥāfiẓ, Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf ibn Murī ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥizām al-Nawawī — may Allah have mercy upon him — said:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds, and His blessings and peace be upon our master Muḥammad, the best of His creation, and upon the rest of the prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner to Him, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger — may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and increase him in virtue and honor in His sight.

To proceed: It is incumbent upon every person to adorn himself with the moral character of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and to follow his words, his actions, and his tacit approvals in legal judgments, etiquettes, and all other landmarks of Islam. He must rely in all of that upon what is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and avoid what is weak (ḍaʿīf). He must not be deceived by those who contravene the authentic Sunnah, nor must he imitate those who rely upon weak hadiths. For Allah — glorified and exalted is He — has said: {وَمَا آتَاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانتَهُوا} "And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it" (al-Ḥashr: 7). And He, exalted is He, said: {لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ} "Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent exemplar" (al-Aḥzāb: 21). And He, exalted is He, said: {قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ} "Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins" (Āl ʿImrān: 31). These verses, and what carries their meaning, urge the following of him — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and prohibit innovation and fabrication. Allah — glorified and exalted is He — has commanded us, at times of dispute, to refer back to Allah and the Messenger, meaning the Book and the Sunnah. All of this applies to a Sunnah that has been established as authentic. As for what has not been established as authentic, how could it be a Sunnah? And how could one attribute to the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — that he said it or did it, without any valid justification for doing so? And do not be deceived by the multitude of those who are lax in acting upon and citing weak hadiths as evidence in legal judgments, even if they are authors and leading imāms in jurisprudence and other fields. They have done so extensively in their books, yet were they to be asked about that, they would answer that they do not rely upon the weak in such matters. Rather, the scholars have only permitted [acting upon weak hadiths] in stories (qaṣaṣ) and in the virtues of deeds (faḍāʾil al-aʿmāl) that contain nothing contradicting what has been firmly established in the principles of the Sacred Law — such as the virtue of glorifying Allah (tasbīḥ), the various remembrances (adhkār), urging noble character traits, renunciation of this world, and similar matters whose principles are known and firmly established.

I have sought Allah's guidance — the Generous, the Kind, the Merciful — in compiling an abridgment on legal judgments in which I rely upon the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and the good (ḥasan), and I have set apart the weak in the concluding portions of the chapters as a warning of its weakness, lest anyone be deceived by it. I shall mention therein, Allah willing, numerous passages [folio 1/a] that are the foundational principles of legal rulings, and I shall attribute them to the well-known books, explicitly stating their authenticity and goodness. I shall also draw attention to some of their obscure meanings and the precise vocalization of their wording. Whatever is found in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, or in one of them, I limit myself to attributing it to them, or to one of them, for the intended purpose is achieved — namely, demonstrating its authenticity — for the two of them are authentic by the consensus of the Muslims. As for what is found in other than the two, I mention the group of well-known transmitters who reported it, such as Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, al-Dāraquṭnī, al-Ḥākim, al-Bayhaqī, and other distinguished ḥāfiẓ authors. Whatever is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim — may Allah have mercy upon them — I say at its end: "Agreed upon" (muttafaq ʿalayh). If their wording is identical, I suffice with "Agreed upon"; otherwise, I say: "Its wording is that of so-and-so." And if one of them, or someone else, adds an addition to it, I draw attention to it. Whatever is agreed upon by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, I say at its end: "Narrated by the three." Anything other than this, I explicitly state its attribution.

Know that the Sunans of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī contain the authentic, the good, and the weak — but their weak [hadiths] are few. For this reason, the imāms have said: The foundational books of Islam from among the hadith collections are five: the two Ṣaḥīḥs and these three. Nothing of the authentic and the good falls outside these five except a little. Al-Tirmidhī has explicitly stated, in most of his books, the clarification of the authentic, the good, and the weak, though he neglected to clarify a portion of them. Abū Dāwūd said: "I have gathered in this book of mine the authentic and what resembles it and approaches it. Whatever contains severe weakness, I have made clear. Whatever I have not mentioned anything about is sound (ṣāliḥ), and some of it is more authentic than others." This is his wording, and its implication is that whatever Abū Dāwūd left unqualified is authentic or good, admissible as evidence — unless something appears in it that necessitates its weakness. I have committed myself in this abridgment not to neglect clarifying anything of the hadiths regarding their authenticity, goodness, or weakness. The good (ḥasan) is like the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) in the permissibility of citing it as evidence in legal judgments, though it is below it [in rank]. As for the weak, I draw attention to it very briefly. Upon Allah the Generous is my reliance, to Him is my delegation, and upon Him is my support. Allah suffices me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
From the Commander of the Believers, Abū Ḥafṣ — —may Allah be pleased with him—

EPUB/chap_01.xhtml.title: Section 1 — The Inaugural Homily (Khuṭbah) on the Distinction of This Community through the Science of Chain Transmission (ʿIlm al-Isnād)

paragraphs.text:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
O Lord, may Your gentleness be perpetual.

The Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the worker [of righteousness], the eminent one, the complete one, the God-fearing, the ascetic — Muḥyī al-Dīn — may God preserve him, guarded, and kept in the eye of His care — said:

Praise be to God, Possessor of abundant blessings and [Supreme] judgments, Who favored the community of Muḥammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — above all other communities, [that community] which He singled out with the science of chain transmission (ʿilm al-isnād), in which He gave no created being any share alongside them — as an honor to His servant, His Messenger, His beloved, and His intimate friend (khalīl), Muḥammad, the master of all mankind. Upon him be from Him the most excellent of prayers, blessings, and peace, perpetually increasing without cessation — and upon his family, his wives, his progeny, and his righteous, noble Companions, and those who followed them in excellence from among the distinguished and the luminaries. To proceed:

Indeed, when God — glorified be He — singled out this community — may God increase it in honor — with the science of chain transmission, He appointed for the task of preserving it select individuals from among the critical hadith masters (al-ḥuffāẓ al-nuqqād), and made them defenders of the Sunnah of His Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — in all times and lands, expending their utmost effort in clarifying soundness from its chains and corruption [therein], out of fear of diminishment from it or augmentation [of spurious material], and in refutation of what the people of vain desires and obstinacy had fabricated, and as a protection for the community until the Day of the Great Summons (yawm al-tanād). They strove in this with utmost seriousness and diligence, and there shall not cease — by the praise of God and His gentleness — to be groups of select servants undertaking this until the end of the world and the advent of the Hereafter, even if they be few and near to extinction.

Know that the science of hadith is among the most virtuous of the sciences, the most deserving of attentive care, and the most worthy of that for which the distinguished and the verifying scholars among the learned gird their loins — for it is the science that penetrates most deeply into the various branches of knowledge, especially jurisprudence (fiqh), which is the very eye of those branches. For this reason, the errors of those devoid of it among the jurist-authors have multiplied, and the defect has become manifest in the speech of those deficient in it among the scholars. Indeed, the standing of hadith in times past was great, its matter august and immense: vast were the multitudes of its students, lofty were the ranks of its preservers and bearers. Yet in these times, most of that has vanished, and nothing remains but traces of what once was. God is the One Whose aid is sought, and upon Him is reliance.

This is a book in which — God willing, the Generous, the Clement, the Merciful — I have abridged the knowledge of the sciences of hadith [as set forth in the work] of the Shaykh, the Imām, the preserver (ḥāfiẓ), the precise, the brilliant, the masterful, the verifier, the remnant of the verifying scholars and the righteous knowers of God, possessor of praiseworthy works and beneficial compositions, Abū ʿAmr ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāfiʿī, known as Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may God be pleased with him, and grant him satisfaction, and honor his resting place and his abode, and gather us together with him in the abode of His generosity among those whom He has chosen. For his book — may God have mercy on him — although it is concise and eloquent in its brevity, the aspirations of the people of these times have weakened with respect to memorizing it, and aspirations are ever descending into indolence and languor.

paragraphs.text: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and grant them peace. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. To proceed:

This is an important treatise on the "Commentary on Sunan Abi Dawud" — may Allah have mercy upon him — in which I confine myself to the choicest of discourse, concerning what relates to its variant readings (lughāt), its expressions (alfāẓ), its chains of transmission (asānīd), and its subtleties (daqāʾiq); and the precise voweling (ḍabṭ) of whatever may be problematic among the expressions of the texts (mutūn) and the names; and indicating some of what is derived from the ḥadīth of legal rulings (aḥkām) and other matters; and drawing attention to the authenticity (ṣiḥḥah) of a ḥadīth, or its goodness (ḥusn), or its weakness (ḍuʿf); and clarifying the correctness of what differs among the manuscript copies. And with Allah is the success.
Section 1

We have related from Imam Abi Dawud — the author of the book, may Allah have mercy upon him — that he said: "I have mentioned in this book of mine the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and what resembles it and approaches it." And in another narration from him, its meaning being that he mentions in every chapter the most authentic (aṣaḥḥ) of what he knew in that chapter. And he said: "Whatever ḥadīth in my book contains severe weakness (wahn shadīd), I have indeed clarified it. And whatever I have not mentioned anything concerning, it is sound (ṣāliḥ) — and some of them are more authentic than others."

So upon this basis: whatever we find in the "Sunan Abi Dawud" that is not in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Ṣaḥīḥayn) or one of them, and no one whose opinion is relied upon has explicitly ruled on its authenticity or goodness, and Abu Dawud has not declared it weak — then it is ḥasan (good) according to Abu Dawud, or ṣaḥīḥ (authentic). So we rule by the certain measure (al-qadr al-muḥaqqaq): namely, that it is ḥasan. For if one whose opinion is relied upon has explicitly declared it weak, or the knowledgeable one sees in its chain (sanad) what necessitates weakness and there is no compensating factor (jābir) for it, we rule by its weakness.

And al-Ḥāfiẓ Abu ʿAbdillāh ibn Mandah has said: "Abu Dawud does transmit the weak chain (al-isnād al-ḍaʿīf) when he finds no other in the chapter, because it is stronger in his view than the opinion of men (raʾy al-rijāl)."

And know that there have occurred in the "Sunan Abi Dawud" ḥadīths of apparent weakness that he did not clarify, despite their being unanimously agreed upon as weak among the muḥaddithūn — such as the mursal (interrupted at the Companion level) and the munqaṭiʿ (broken chain), and his narration from an unknown (majhūl) person: such as "a shaykh" or "a man" and the like. So it may be said: This contradicts his statement: "Whatever contains severe weakness, I have clarified it!"
And its answer is: Since the weakness of this type is apparent, its very appearance sufficed in place of explicit clarification of it.

paragraphs.text: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
**Foreword**
All praise is due to Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah.
To proceed:

This is a beneficial and useful book — the book "The Forty Hadith" (al-Arbaʿūn al-Nawawiyyah) of Imam al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy upon him. With it are the additions (ziyādāt) of al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab, may Allah have mercy upon him. The one who undertook the verification of its hadiths (takhrīj) and the ruling upon them is my brother in Allah, al-Shirbīnī ibn Fāʾiq al-Shirbīnī, may Allah preserve him. By this, the benefit of the book increased, and the advantages derived from it multiplied. I have examined the work of my brother — may Allah preserve him — and found it beneficial and successful, and to Allah belongs all praise.
I ask Allah to increase him in success (tawfīq) and right guidance (sadād), and in perseverance in seeking sacred knowledge and calling to Allah.
O Allah, send blessings upon our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.

Written by:
Abū ʿAbdillāh Muṣṭafā ibn al-ʿAdawī
**The Verifier's Introduction**
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our trustworthy Messenger, and upon his family and all his companions.
To proceed:

Indeed, the Book of the Forty (al-Arbaʿūn) of Imam al-Nawawi — may Allah have mercy upon him — is a great book, by which Allah benefited His servants in the easts of the earth and its wests. And the book increased in benefit by what al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī — may Allah have mercy upon him — added to it, as a completion (tatimmah) of these hadiths. It was from Allah's grace upon me that He facilitated my access to this book, and I found that despite the good it contains, it nevertheless included some weak hadiths (aḥādīth ḍaʿīfah). So I sought the aid of Allah the Exalted and commenced ruling upon these hadiths as authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) or weak (ḍaʿīf), while mentioning the cause of weakness in brief. Then I presented these hadiths to his eminence, Shaykh Muṣṭafā ibn al-ʿAdawī — may Allah preserve him — to complete the benefit.
I hope from Allah that He benefits His servants through it, and that He grants us sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and acceptance (qabūl).
O Allah, send blessings upon our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, abundantly. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.

Written by:
al-Shirbīnī ibn Fāʾiq al-Shirbīnī

# المؤلف: أبو زكريا محيي الدين يحيى بن شرف النووي (المتوفى: 676ه)
# تعليق وتحقيق: الدكتور ماهر ياسين الفحل رئيس قسم الحديث - كلية العلوم

الإسلامية - جامعة الأنبار (وقد جعل تحقيقه للكتاب مجانا فجزاه الله خيرا)
# الناشر: دار ابن كثير للطباعة والنشر والتوزيع، دمشق - بيروت
# الطبعة: الأولى، 1428 ه - 2007 م
# عدد الأجزاء: 1
# أعده للشاملة/ واسم كان الإندونيسي
# [ترقيم الكتاب موافق للمطبوع وهو مذيل بالحواشي] 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
# إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا

وسيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له.
# «وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، وأمينه على وحيه، وخيرته من خلقه، وسفيره

بينه وبين عباده، المبعوث بالدين القويم، والمنهج المستقيم، أرسله الله

رحمة للعالمين، وإماما للمتقين، وحجة على الخلائق أجمعين» (1)
# {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون}

[آل عمران: 102]. {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق

منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به

والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} [النساء: 1] {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا

الله وقولوا قولا سديدا يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله

ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما} [الأحزاب: 70 - 71]. أما بعد: فإني أحمد الله

أولا وآخرا وظاهرا وباطنا على إنهاء العمل بهذا الكتاب العظيم " رياض

الصالحين "، ذلك الكتاب الذي كان من أول كتب العلم قراءة لي، وكنت دائما

أرجع إلى هذا الكتاب وأحفظ من أحاديثه وأنصح الناس في العناية به؛ لأنه
