# الطبعة: الأولى، 1428 ه - 2007 م
# عدد الأجزاء: 1
# أعده للشاملة/ واسم كان الإندونيسي
# [ترقيم الكتاب موافق للمطبوع وهو مذيل بالحواشي] 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
# إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا

وسيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له.
# «وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، وأمينه على وحيه، وخيرته من خلقه، وسفيره

بينه وبين عباده، المبعوث بالدين القويم، والمنهج المستقيم، أرسله الله

رحمة للعالمين، وإماما للمتقين، وحجة على الخلائق أجمعين» (1)
# {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون}

[آل عمران: 102]. {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق

منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به

والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} [النساء: 1] {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا

الله وقولوا قولا سديدا يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله

ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما} [الأحزاب: 70 - 71]. أما بعد: فإني أحمد الله

أولا وآخرا وظاهرا وباطنا على إنهاء العمل بهذا الكتاب العظيم " رياض

الصالحين "، ذلك الكتاب الذي كان من أول كتب العلم قراءة لي، وكنت دائما

أرجع إلى هذا الكتاب وأحفظ من أحاديثه وأنصح الناس في العناية به؛ لأنه

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise, commendation, and eulogy rendered for benefits received; the opposite of ذم (blame).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ḥamd is praise for voluntary, deliberate beneficence (niʿmah ikhtiyāriyyah), distinguishing it from mere madḥ (praise) which may be for involuntary qualities.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — praise for a good deed; metaphorical (majāz) — the absolute, eternal praise of Allah which precedes and exceeds all contingent acts.
- Root: هدى (h-d-y)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Guidance, direction, showing the way; also the gift (hidayyah) and the guide.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — hidāyah is of two kinds: (1) general guidance (irshād) granted to all, and (2) specific guidance (tawfīq) granted only to the righteous; the verse «من يهده الله فلا مضل له» affirms the latter as exclusively divine.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — pointing the way; metaphorical — Allah's act of creating faith and steadfastness in the heart.
- Root: ضلل (ḍ-l-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Deviation from the straight path, error, perishing, being lost.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ḍalāl is the departure from the correct path, whether intentionally (error of belief) or unintentionally (forgetfulness); its opposite is rushd (right guidance).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — straying from the road; metaphorical — spiritual misguidance and deprivation of divine grace.
- Root: سدد (s-d-d)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness, correctness, rightness; to aim correctly; to be upright.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — sadād is the correct and sound saying that is free from falsehood and error, aligning with truth and justice.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — an arrow hitting its target; metaphorical — speech that is upright, truthful, and free from deviation.
- Root: صلح (ṣ-l-ḥ)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Soundness, goodness, righteousness; the opposite of corruption (fasād).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ṣalāḥ is the state of being sound and upright in deeds; it is contrasted with both fasād (corruption) and sayyiʾah (evil deed) in the Qur'an.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a thing being sound and fit; metaphorical — deeds being rendered acceptable and rewarded by Allah.
- Root: فوز (f-w-z)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Salvation, deliverance, triumph, attainment of what is desired with safety.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fawz is the attainment of good and deliverance from evil; the "great triumph" (fawz ʿaẓīm) is eternal salvation in the Hereafter.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — escaping danger and attaining one's goal; metaphorical — the ultimate success of Paradise and escape from Hellfire.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of the Interjection (Bāb al-Iʿtirāḍ) — The phrase «أما بعد» (amā baʿd) functions as a transitional interjection separating the introductory homily (khuṭbah) from the main discourse, governed by the implicit conditional structure "whatever follows, then..." (ammā baʿdu fa-innī...).
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Indeed, all praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, we seek His aid, and we seek His forgiveness. And we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our own souls and from the wickedness of our deeds. Whomsoever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whomsoever He leads astray, none can guide. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him.

«And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, His trustee over His revelation, His chosen one from among His creation, and His envoy between Him and His servants — sent with the upright religion and the straight path. Allah sent him as a mercy to the worlds, an Imam for the God-fearing, and a proof against all of creation» (1).

{«O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims»} [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. {«O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever over you an Observer»} [al-Nisāʾ: 1]. {«O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice — He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment»} [al-Aḥzāb: 70–71].

To proceed: I praise Allah — first and last, outwardly and inwardly — upon the completion of the work on this great book, "Gardens of the Righteous" (Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn). It is that book which was among the very first scholarly texts I read, and I have continually returned to this book, memorized its hadiths, and advised people to give it their utmost care — because of its immense virtue, its comprehensive selection of prophetic traditions, and its arrangement into chapters of righteousness and piety.

# 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم (قال الشيخ الإمام العالم العامل الورع الزاهد

الحافظ محي الدين أبو زكريا يحيى بن شرف بن مري بن حسن بن حسين بن محمد بن

حزام النووي رحمه الله) . الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلواته وسلامه على سيدنا

محمد خير خلقه وعلى سائر النبيين وآل كل وسائر الصالحين، وأشهد أن لا إله

إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وزاده فضلا وشرفا لديه. أما بعد. فإنه ينبغي لكل أحد أن يتخلق بأخلاق رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويقتدي بأقواله وأفعاله وتقريره في الأحكام

والآداب وسائر معالم الإسلام وأن يعتمد في ذلك ما صح ويجتنب ما ضعف ولا

يغتر بمخالفي السنن الصحيحة ولا يقلد معتمدي الأحاديث الضعيفة فإن الله

سبحانه وتعالى قال: (وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا) وقال

تعالى: (لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة) وقال تعالى: (قل إن كنتم

تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم) . فهذه الآيات وما في

معناهن حث على اتباعه صلى الله عليه وسلم ونهانا عن الابتداع والاختراع،

وأمرنا الله سبحانه وتعالى عند التنازع بالرجوع إلى الله والرسول أي الكتاب

والسنة، وهذا كله في سنة صحت، أما ما لم تصح فكيف تكون سنة، وكيف يحكم على

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قاله أو فعله من غير مسوغ لذلك، ولا

تغترن بكثرة المتساهلين
# 
# في العمل، والاحتجاج في الأحكام بالأحاديث الضعيفة وإن كانوا مصنفين

وأئمة في الفقه وغيره، وقد أكثروا من ذلك في كتبهم، ولو سئلوا عن ذلك

لأجابوا بأنه لا يعتمد في ذلك الضعيف، وإنما أباح العلماء [العمل بالضعيف

في القصص وفضائل الأعمال التي ليست فيها مخالفة لما تقرر في أصول الشرع

مثل: فضل التسبيح، وسائر الأذكار، والحث على مكارم الأخلاق، والزهد في

الدنيا، وغير ذلك مما أصوله معلومة مقررة. وقد استخرت الله الكريم الرؤوف

الرحيم في جمع مختصر في الأحكام اعتمد فيه الصحيح والحسن وأفرد الضعيف في

أواخر الأبواب تنبيها على ضعفه لئلا يغتر به، واذكر فيه إن شاء الله جملا

متكاثرة [1 / أ] هي أصول قواعد الأحكام وأضيفها إلى الكتب المشهورة مصرحا

بصحتها وحسنها، وأنبه على بعض خفي معانيها وضبط لفظها، فما كان في صحيحي

البخاري ومسلم أو أحدهما اقتصرت على إضافته إليهما أو غليه لحصول المقصود

وهو بيان صحته، فإنهما صحيحان بإجماع المسلمين، وما كان في غيرهما ذكرت

جماعة ممن رواه من المشهورين كأبي داود، والترمذي، والنسائي، والدارقطني،

والحاكم، والبيهقي وغيرهم من أعلام الحفاظ المصنفين، فما كان في صحيحي

البخاري ومسلم رحمهما الله قلت في آخره: متفق عليه، فإن اتفق لفظهما اقتصرت

على " متفق عليه "، وغلا قلت: لفظه لفلان، وإن زاد أحدهما أوغيرهما زيادة

فيه نبهت عليها. وما اتفق عليه أبو داود، والترمذي، والنسائي قلت في آخره:

" رواه الثلاثة "، وما سوى هذا أصرح بإضافته. واعلم أن سنن أبي داود

والترمذي والنسائي فيها الصحيح والحسن والضعيف، لكن ضعفها يسير، ولهذا قال

الأئمة: أصول الإسلام من كتب الحديث خمسة:
# 
# الصحيحان، وهذه الثلاثة، ولا يخرج عن هذه الخمسة من الصحيح والحسن إلا

قليل. وقد صرح الترمذي في أكثر كتبه ببيان الصحيح، والحسن، والضعيف، وأهمل

بيان جمل منه. وقال أبو داود، " جمعت في كتابي هذا الصحيح وما يشبهه

ويقاربه، وما كان فيه ضعف شديد بينته، وما لم أذكر فيه شيئا فهو صالح،

وبعضها أصح من بعض ". هذا لفظه، ومقتضاه أن ما أطلقه أبو داود فهو صحيح أو

حسن يحتج به، إلا أن يظهر فيه ما يقتضي ضعفه. وقد التزمت في هذا المختصر أن

لا أهمل بيان شيء من الأحاديث في الصحة والحسن والضعف. والحسن كالصحيح في

جواز الاحتجاج به في الأحكام، وإن كان دونه، وأما الضعيف فأنبه عليه مختصرا

جدا. وعلى الله الكريم اعتمادي وإليه تفويضي واستنادي، حسبي الله ونعم

الوكيل، لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العزيز الحكيم. عن أمير المؤمنين أبي حفص

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
 * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes measuring, fashioning, and creating; also moral disposition (khuluq) as an ingrained character trait.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khuluq is the inner form (al-ṣūrah al-bāṭinah) of the soul by which one acts, paralleling al-khalq as the outer form.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical creation and shaping. Metaphorical: adopting a moral character (takhalluqa) as one "fashions" one's soul.
- Root: أسوة (uswah)
 * Lisan / Ayn: A model or exemplar to be followed; derived from the notion of treating a matter with care and deliberation.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context (الأحزاب/21), al-uswah denotes the Prophet as the complete exemplar whose conduct is binding in all that is authentically transmitted.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: an exemplar. Metaphorical: the believer's entire life becomes a following (iqtidā') of the prophetic model.
- Root: صحح (ṣaḥḥa)
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "صح من علته" — soundness from illness; a sound body.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "صح عند القاضي حقه وصحت شهادته" — legal soundness; "المذهب الصحيح" — the correct doctrine. Here, the term is transferred from bodily health to the epistemic reliability of hadith transmissions.
 * Lisan al-Arab: The one who brings falsehoods is called "مُصَحْصِحٌ" — showing that ṣiḥḥah (soundness) is the opposite of falsehood and error.
- Root: ضعف (ḍaʿufa)
 * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الضعف: خلاف القوة" — weakness is the opposite of strength; it may be in the soul, the body, or one's condition. Al-Khalil said: al-ḍuʿf (with ḍammah) is bodily weakness, while al-ḍaʿf (with fatḥah) is weakness in intellect and judgment.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "هو في أضعاف الكتاب" — within the folds of the book. In hadith terminology, ḍaʿīf is that which lacks the conditions of soundness — a metaphorical extension from physical frailty to deficiency in the chain or text.
- Root: رسل (rasala)
 * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root denotes being sent forth with composure. The messenger (rasūl) is one sent with a message.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — God sent punishment upon them. In hadith terminology, the chain of transmission (sanad) is called "isnād" from the notion of "support," and the transmitters are "ruwāt" who "send forth" the prophetic words.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the author uses restrictive constructions (e.g., "إنما أباح العلماء"), the predicate is confined exclusively to what follows, excluding all else. This governs the precise scope of permissibility for weak hadith.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the worker [of righteous deeds], the abstinent, the ascetic, the ḥāfiẓ, Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf ibn Murī ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥizām al-Nawawī — may Allah have mercy upon him — said:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds, and His blessings and peace be upon our master Muḥammad, the best of His creation, and upon the rest of the prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner to Him, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger — may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and increase him in virtue and honor in His sight.

To proceed: It is incumbent upon every person to adorn himself with the moral character of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and to follow his words, his actions, and his tacit approvals in legal judgments, etiquettes, and all other landmarks of Islam. He must rely in all of that upon what is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and avoid what is weak (ḍaʿīf). He must not be deceived by those who contravene the authentic Sunnah, nor must he imitate those who rely upon weak hadiths. For Allah — glorified and exalted is He — has said: {وَمَا آتَاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانتَهُوا} "And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it" (al-Ḥashr: 7). And He, exalted is He, said: {لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ} "Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent exemplar" (al-Aḥzāb: 21). And He, exalted is He, said: {قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ} "Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins" (Āl ʿImrān: 31). These verses, and what carries their meaning, urge the following of him — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and prohibit innovation and fabrication. Allah — glorified and exalted is He — has commanded us, at times of dispute, to refer back to Allah and the Messenger, meaning the Book and the Sunnah. All of this applies to a Sunnah that has been established as authentic. As for what has not been established as authentic, how could it be a Sunnah? And how could one attribute to the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — that he said it or did it, without any valid justification for doing so? And do not be deceived by the multitude of those who are lax in acting upon and citing weak hadiths as evidence in legal judgments, even if they are authors and leading imāms in jurisprudence and other fields. They have done so extensively in their books, yet were they to be asked about that, they would answer that they do not rely upon the weak in such matters. Rather, the scholars have only permitted [acting upon weak hadiths] in stories (qaṣaṣ) and in the virtues of deeds (faḍāʾil al-aʿmāl) that contain nothing contradicting what has been firmly established in the principles of the Sacred Law — such as the virtue of glorifying Allah (tasbīḥ), the various remembrances (adhkār), urging noble character traits, renunciation of this world, and similar matters whose principles are known and firmly established.

I have sought Allah's guidance — the Generous, the Kind, the Merciful — in compiling an abridgment on legal judgments in which I rely upon the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and the good (ḥasan), and I have set apart the weak in the concluding portions of the chapters as a warning of its weakness, lest anyone be deceived by it. I shall mention therein, Allah willing, numerous passages [folio 1/a] that are the foundational principles of legal rulings, and I shall attribute them to the well-known books, explicitly stating their authenticity and goodness. I shall also draw attention to some of their obscure meanings and the precise vocalization of their wording. Whatever is found in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, or in one of them, I limit myself to attributing it to them, or to one of them, for the intended purpose is achieved — namely, demonstrating its authenticity — for the two of them are authentic by the consensus of the Muslims. As for what is found in other than the two, I mention the group of well-known transmitters who reported it, such as Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, al-Dāraquṭnī, al-Ḥākim, al-Bayhaqī, and other distinguished ḥāfiẓ authors. Whatever is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim — may Allah have mercy upon them — I say at its end: "Agreed upon" (muttafaq ʿalayh). If their wording is identical, I suffice with "Agreed upon"; otherwise, I say: "Its wording is that of so-and-so." And if one of them, or someone else, adds an addition to it, I draw attention to it. Whatever is agreed upon by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, I say at its end: "Narrated by the three." Anything other than this, I explicitly state its attribution.

Know that the Sunans of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī contain the authentic, the good, and the weak — but their weak [hadiths] are few. For this reason, the imāms have said: The foundational books of Islam from among the hadith collections are five: the two Ṣaḥīḥs and these three. Nothing of the authentic and the good falls outside these five except a little. Al-Tirmidhī has explicitly stated, in most of his books, the clarification of the authentic, the good, and the weak, though he neglected to clarify a portion of them. Abū Dāwūd said: "I have gathered in this book of mine the authentic and what resembles it and approaches it. Whatever contains severe weakness, I have made clear. Whatever I have not mentioned anything about is sound (ṣāliḥ), and some of it is more authentic than others." This is his wording, and its implication is that whatever Abū Dāwūd left unqualified is authentic or good, admissible as evidence — unless something appears in it that necessitates its weakness. I have committed myself in this abridgment not to neglect clarifying anything of the hadiths regarding their authenticity, goodness, or weakness. The good (ḥasan) is like the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) in the permissibility of citing it as evidence in legal judgments, though it is below it [in rank]. As for the weak, I draw attention to it very briefly. Upon Allah the Generous is my reliance, to Him is my delegation, and upon Him is my support. Allah suffices me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
From the Commander of the Believers, Abū Ḥafṣ — —may Allah be pleased with him—

Section 47 — On the Etiquette of the Hadith Scholar and the Proper Conduct of Delivering Hadith (Section 47)
Section 48 — On the Etiquette of the Hadith Scholar and the Seeker (Chapter 28: Knowledge of the Etiquette of the Student of Hadith) (Section 48)
Section 49 — On the Age for Beginning to Hear and Write Hadith; Etiquette of the Student with His Shaykh, Seeking Knowledge, and Preserving It (Section 49)
Section 50 — On the Etiquette of the Hadith Student: Comprehension, Mastery, and Authorship (Section 50)
The Twenty-Ninth Category: Knowledge of Elevated and Lowered Chains of Transmission (Al-Isnād al-ʿĀlī wa al-Nāzil) (Section 51)
Section 52 — The Thirtieth Category: The Well-Known (Al-Mashhūr) Hadith, and the Thirty-First and Thirty-Second Categories (Section 52)
Section 53 — On the Science of Gharīb al-Ḥadīth (Rare/Obscure Terms in Prophetic Reports) and the Science of Musalsal (Chained/Serialized Reports) (Section 53)
Section 54: On Knowing the Abrogating and Abrogated Hadith, and Related Sciences (Section 54)
Section 55 — Type Thirty-Six: Knowledge of Contradictory Hadith (Mukhtalif al-Hadith) and Its Ruling (Section 55)
Section 56 — Types 37–39: Knowledge of Additions in Connected Chains, Subtle Discontinuities (Mursal), and the Companions (Section 56)
Section 57 — The Thirty-Ninth Category: Knowledge of the Companions (Sahābah), May Allah Be Pleased with Them (Section 57)
Section 58 — On the Knowledge of the Companions (ʿUlamāʾ al-Ṣaḥābah): Their Number, Virtues, and Distinctions (Section 58)
Section 59 — The Fortieth Category: Knowledge of the Followers (Al-Tābiʿūn), May Allah Be Pleased with Them (Section 59)
Section 60: The Forty-First through Forty-Fourth Categories — Knowledge of Major Narrators from Minor Ones, Mudabbaj and Peer Narration, Brothers, and Fathers Narrating from Sons (Section 60)
Section 61 — Types 44–47: Fathers Narrating from Sons; Sons Narrating from Fathers; Disparity in Death Dates of Co-Narrators; and Those from Whom Only One Narrated (Section 61)
Section 62 — Types 47, 48, and 49: Those Reported by Only One Narrator; Those Known by Multiple Names or Attributes; and Isolated Narrations (al-Mufradāt) (Section 62)
Section 63 — On Knowing Names, Epithets (Kunyah), and Honorific Titles (Alqāb): A Chapter on Orthographic Precision in the Names of Narrators (Section 63)
Section 64 — On Knowing the Names (Al-Asmā') and Honorific Appellations (Al-Kunā) (Section 64)
Section 65 — The Eighth and Ninth Categories of Those Known by Kunyah, and Chapter 51: Knowing the Kunyahs of Those Famous by Name (Section 65)
Section 66 — The Fifty-Second Type: Honorific Nicknames (Al-Alqāb) (Section 66)
Section 67 — The Fifty-Third Type: The Homographic and the Heterographic (Al-Mu'talif wa al-Mukhtalif) (Section 67)
Section 68 — On Precision in Names Occurring in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs or in the Muwaṭṭaʾ (Section 68)
Section 69 — On Names with Variant Spellings (al-Muthannāh) and Distinguishing Agreed-Upon from Differentiated Names (al-Muttafiq wa al-Muftariq) (Section 69)
Section 70 — The Fifty-Fourth Category: Knowledge of the Agreeing-in-Form and the Diverging (al-Muttafiq wa al-Muftariq) (Section 70)
Section 71 — The Fifth Category (Part 2): Agreement in Names, Fathers' Names, and Lineages, with Examples (Section 71)
Section 72 — Types Fifty-Five, Fifty-Six, and Fifty-Seven: Compound Names, Similar Names with Distinguished Genealogies, and Those Attributed to Other Than Their Fathers (Section 72)
Section 73 — The Fifty-Seventh Type: Knowledge of Those Attributed to Other Than Their Fathers (Section 73)
Section 74 — Types Fifty-Eight & Fifty-Nine: Knowledge of Attributive Names Contrary to Their Apparent Meaning, and Knowledge of Ambiguous Identities (Al-Mubhamāt) (Section 74)
Section 75 — The Sixtieth Type: Chronologies of Narrators and Death-Dates (Section 75)
Section 76 — The Fifth Class of Hadith Masters, and Chapter 61: Knowledge of the Trustworthy and Weak Narrators (Section 76)
Section 77 — The Sixty-Second Type: Knowledge of Trustworthy Narrators Who Became Confused (Ikhtilāṭ) in Their Later Years (Section 77)
Section 78 — The Sixty-Fourth Category: Knowledge of the Mawālī (Clients/Freed Slaves) Among Narrators and Scholars (Section 78)
Section 79 — On Knowing the Homelands and Countries of Narrators (Maʿrifat Awṭān al-Ruwāt wa Buldānihim) (Section 79)
Section 80 — On the Hadith of Jaththam (The Kneeling) and Its Chain of Damascene Narrators (Section 80)

The Conclusion — The Editor's Afterword on the Completion of the Investigation (Section 82)

# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
# رب لطفك دائما (أ)
# (قال الشيخ الإمام العالم العامل الصدر الكامل التقي الزاهد محي الدين

أبقاه الله محفوظا وبعين عنايته ملحوظا) (ب).
# : الحمد لله ذي الآلاء (¬1) والحكم، المفضل أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

على سائر (¬2) الأمم التي خصصها بعلم الإسناد (¬3)، الذي لم يشركها # فيه أحد من العباد، تشريفا لعبده ورسوله وحبيبه (أ) وخليله محمد سيد

الأنام، عليه منه أفضل الصلوات والبركات والسلام، دائما متزايدا بلا انفصام

(ب) وعلى آله (¬1) وأزواجه و (ذريته) (ج) وأصحابه البررة الكرام والتابعين

لهم بإحسان من الأماثل (د) والأعلام، أما بعد:
# فإن الله (سبحانه) (ه) لما خص هذه الأمة - زادها الله شرفا - بعلم

الإسناد نصب للقيام بحفظه خواص من الحفاظ النقاد وجعلهم ذابين (و) عن سنة

نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في جميع الأوقات والبلاد، باذلين وسعهم في تبيين

الصحة من طرقها، والفساد، خوفا من الانتقاص منها والازدياد، ودحضا (¬2) (ز)

لما اخترعه أهل الأهواء والعناد، وحفظا على الأمة إلى يوم التناد (¬3)،

فبالغوا في ذلك بالجد والاجتهاد ولا يزال على القيام # بذلك بحمد الله ولطفه طوائف من الخواص العباد، إلى انقضاء الدنيا، وإقبال

المعاد، وإن قلوا وقربوا من النفاد.
# واعلم أن علم الحديث من أفضل (أ) العلوم وأولاها بالاعتناء وأحق ما شمر

(¬1) فيه المبرزون ومحققوا العلماء إذ هو أكثر العلوم تولجا (¬2)، في

فنونها، لا سيما الفقه الذي هو إنسان عيونها ولذلك كثر غلط العاطلين (¬3)

منه من مصنفي الفقهاء وظهر الخلل في كلام المخلين (¬4) به من العلماء، ولقد

كان شأن الحديث فيما مضى عظيما وأمره مفخما جسيما. عظيمة جموع (¬5) طلبته،

رفيعة مقادير حفاظه وحملته، فذهب في هذه الأزمان المعظم من ذلك، ولم يبق

إلا آثار مما كان هنالك، والله المستعان وعليه التكلان (¬6).
# وهذا كتاب اختصر فيه إن شاء الله الكريم الرؤوف الرحيم - معرفة علوم

الحديث للشيخ الإمام الحافظ الضابط البارع المتقن المحقق بقية # العلماء المحققين والصلحاء العارفين ذي التصانيف الحميدة والمؤلفات

المفيدة أبي عمرو عثمان بن عبد الرحمان الشافعي المعروف بابن الصلاح رضي

الله عنه وأرضاه وأكرم نزله (¬1) ومثواه (¬2) وجمع بيننا وبينه في دار

كرامته مع من اصطفاه، فإن كتابه رحمه الله وإن كان بليغا في الاختصار فقد

ضعفت عن حفظه همم أهل هذه (أ) الأعصار والهمم مترقية في الكسل والفتور فصار

لما اخترعه أهل الأهواء والعناد، وحفظا على الأمة إلى يوم التناد (¬3)،

فبالغوا في ذلك بالجد والاجتهاد ولا يزال على القيام # بذلك بحمد الله ولطفه طوائف من الخواص العباد، إلى انقضاء الدنيا، وإقبال

المعاد، وإن قلوا وقربوا من النفاد.
# واعلم أن علم الحديث من أفضل (أ) العلوم وأولاها بالاعتناء وأحق ما شمر

(¬1) فيه المبرزون ومحققوا العلماء إذ هو أكثر العلوم تولجا (¬2)، في

فنونها، لا سيما الفقه الذي هو إنسان عيونها ولذلك كثر غلط العاطلين (¬3)

منه من مصنفي الفقهاء وظهر الخلل في كلام المخلين (¬4) به من العلماء، ولقد

كان شأن الحديث فيما مضى عظيما وأمره مفخما جسيما. عظيمة جموع (¬5) طلبته،

رفيعة مقادير حفاظه وحملته، فذهب في هذه الأزمان المعظم من ذلك، ولم يبق

إلا آثار مما كان هنالك، والله المستعان وعليه التكلان (¬6).
# وهذا كتاب اختصر فيه إن شاء الله الكريم الرؤوف الرحيم - معرفة علوم

الحديث للشيخ الإمام الحافظ الضابط البارع المتقن المحقق بقية # العلماء المحققين والصلحاء العارفين ذي التصانيف الحميدة والمؤلفات

المفيدة أبي عمرو عثمان بن عبد الرحمان الشافعي المعروف بابن الصلاح رضي

الله عنه وأرضاه وأكرم نزله (¬1) ومثواه (¬2) وجمع بيننا وبينه في دار

كرامته مع من اصطفاه، فإن كتابه رحمه الله وإن كان بليغا في الاختصار فقد

ضعفت عن حفظه همم أهل هذه (أ) الأعصار والهمم مترقية في الكسل والفتور فصار

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes praise arising from recognition of beneficence; al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh as absolute, all-encompassing praise exclusive to the Divine.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥamd is praise (thnāʾ) predicated upon voluntary beneficence (iḥsān ikhtiyārī), distinguishing it from mere madḥ (praise for any quality).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Aḥmadtu ’Llāha bi-jamīʿi maḥāmīdih" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical (majāz): "Aḥmadtu ’l-arḍa" — I found the land commendable for dwelling.
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
 * Lisan / Ayn: ʿIlm as the indelible mark or trace (aʿlām) by which a thing is known; the faculty of discerning reality.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is apprehension of a thing in its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatih), either of the essence itself or of a judgment predicated upon it.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Mā ʿalimtu bi-khabarika" — I had no awareness of your news. Metaphorical: "Huwa min aʿlām al-dīn al-shāhikhah" — he is among the towering landmarks of the religion.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Ḥadīth as newly-occurring speech; the report of an event (ḥadath).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after non-existence; muḥdath is that which is originated. Applied to speech (ḥadīth) as newly-arrived communication.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" — the vicissitudes of time befell him. Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" — ʿUmar was one whose intuition was inspired, as if he were told (ḥudditha) of hidden matters.
- Root: جمع (J-M-ʿ)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Jamʿ as the gathering and drawing together of dispersed parts into a unity.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Jamʿ is the conjunction of things by approximation of some to others; al-jamʿ al-ḥasīr is the gathering of all creation on the Day of Resurrection.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kuntu fī majmaʿ min al-nās" — I was in a great assembly of people. Metaphorical: "Amruhum jamīʿ" — their affair is a well-kept secret, concealed as a virgin is veiled.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its governed noun when the intervening phrase is syntactically complete, as in the author's periodic constructions where subordinate invocations and blessings intervene between grammatical dependents.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
O Lord, may Your gentleness be perpetual.

The Shaykh, the Imām, the scholar, the worker [of righteousness], the eminent one, the complete one, the God-fearing, the ascetic — Muḥyī al-Dīn — may God preserve him, guarded, and kept in the eye of His care — said:

Praise be to God, Possessor of abundant blessings and [Supreme] judgments, Who favored the community of Muḥammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — above all other communities, [that community] which He singled out with the science of chain transmission (ʿilm al-isnād), in which He gave no created being any share alongside them — as an honor to His servant, His Messenger, His beloved, and His intimate friend (khalīl), Muḥammad, the master of all mankind. Upon him be from Him the most excellent of prayers, blessings, and peace, perpetually increasing without cessation — and upon his family, his wives, his progeny, and his righteous, noble Companions, and those who followed them in excellence from among the distinguished and the luminaries. To proceed:

Indeed, when God — glorified be He — singled out this community — may God increase it in honor — with the science of chain transmission, He appointed for the task of preserving it select individuals from among the critical hadith masters (al-ḥuffāẓ al-nuqqād), and made them defenders of the Sunnah of His Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — in all times and lands, expending their utmost effort in clarifying soundness from its chains and corruption [therein], out of fear of diminishment from it or augmentation [of spurious material], and in refutation of what the people of vain desires and obstinacy had fabricated, and as a protection for the community until the Day of the Great Summons (yawm al-tanād). They strove in this with utmost seriousness and diligence, and there shall not cease — by the praise of God and His gentleness — to be groups of select servants undertaking this until the end of the world and the advent of the Hereafter, even if they be few and near to extinction.

Know that the science of hadith is among the most virtuous of the sciences, the most deserving of attentive care, and the most worthy of that for which the distinguished and the verifying scholars among the learned gird their loins — for it is the science that penetrates most deeply into the various branches of knowledge, especially jurisprudence (fiqh), which is the very eye of those branches. For this reason, the errors of those devoid of it among the jurist-authors have multiplied, and the defect has become manifest in the speech of those deficient in it among the scholars. Indeed, the standing of hadith in times past was great, its matter august and immense: vast were the multitudes of its students, lofty were the ranks of its preservers and bearers. Yet in these times, most of that has vanished, and nothing remains but traces of what once was. God is the One Whose aid is sought, and upon Him is reliance.

This is a book in which — God willing, the Generous, the Clement, the Merciful — I have abridged the knowledge of the sciences of hadith [as set forth in the work] of the Shaykh, the Imām, the preserver (ḥāfiẓ), the precise, the brilliant, the masterful, the verifier, the remnant of the verifying scholars and the righteous knowers of God, possessor of praiseworthy works and beneficial compositions, Abū ʿAmr ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāfiʿī, known as Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may God be pleased with him, and grant him satisfaction, and honor his resting place and his abode, and gather us together with him in the abode of His generosity among those whom He has chosen. For his book — may God have mercy on him — although it is concise and eloquent in its brevity, the aspirations of the people of these times have weakened with respect to memorizing it, and aspirations are ever descending into indolence and languor.

# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
# الحمد لله رب العالمين، اللهم صل على محمد، وعلى آل محمد وسلم، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أما بعد:
# فهده نبذ مهمة في "شرح سنن أبي داود" رحمه الله أقتصر فيها على عيون الكلام، مما يتعلق بلغاته وألفاظه وأسانيده ودقائقه، وضبط ما قد يشكل من ألفاظ المتون والأسماء، والإشارة إلى بعض ما يستنبط من الحديث من الأحكام وغيرها، والتنبيه على صحة الحديث أو حسنه أو ضعفه، وبيان صواب ما تختلف فيه النسخ، وبالله التوفيق.

| 1 -

|

| فصل
#
# روينا عن الإمام أبي داود صاحب الكتاب رحمه الله أنه قال: "ذكرت في كتابي هذا الصحيح وما يشبهه ويقاربه". وفي رواية عنه ما معناه أنه يذكر في كل باب أصح ما عرفه في ذلك الباب (1)، وقال (2): "ما كان في كتابي 
#
# من حديث فيه وهن شديد فقد بينته (1)، وما لم أذكر فيه شيئا فهو صالح (2)، 
#
# وبعضها أصح من بعض" (1). 
#
# فعلى هذا، ما وجدنا في "سنن أبي داود" وليس هو في "الصحيحين" أو أحدهما، لا نص على صحته أو حسنه أحد ممن يعتمد، ولم يضعفه أبو داود، فهو حسن عند أبي داود أو صحيح، فنحكم بالقدر المحقق: وهو أنه حسن (1)، فإن نص على ضعفه من يعتمد، أو رأى العارف في ... 
#
# . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 
#
# . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 
#
# . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 
#
# سنده ما يقتضي الضعف ولا جابر له، حكمنا بضعفه (1). 
#
# وقد قال الحافظ أبو عبد الله بن منده (1): "إن أبا داود يخرج الإسناد 
#
# الضعيف إذا لم يجد في الباب غيره؛ لأنه أقوى عنده من رأي الرجال".
# واعلم أنه وقع في "سنن أبي داود" أحاديث ظاهرة الضعف لم يبينها، مع أنها متفق على ضعفها عند المحدثين: كالمرسل والمنقطع، وروايته عن مجهول: كشيخ ورجل ونحوه. فقد يقال: إن هذا مخالف لقوله: "ما كان فيه وهن شديد بينته"!
# وجوابه: أنه لما كان ضعف هذا النوع ظاهرا، استغنى بظهوره عن التصريح ببيانه (1).

| 2 -

|

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence in form and meaning
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ḥasan: every pleasing and desirable thing, perceived by intellect, desire, or sense"
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visible comeliness; Metaphorical: "Qīmatu al-mar'i mā yuḥsin" — a man's worth is what he does well
- Root: ضعف (ḍ-ʿ-f)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Feebleness, weakness, opposite of strength
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ḍaʿf: the opposite of quwwah (strength)"; al-Khalil: ḍuʿf (with ḍammah) is bodily weakness, ḍaʿf (with fatḥah) is weakness in intellect and judgment
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or material weakness; Metaphorical: "fī aḍʿāf al-kitāb" — in the folds/innermost parts of the book
- Root: وهن (w-h-n)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Feebleness, frailty, slackness
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weakness and infirmity, whether in resolve, body, or circumstance
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily languor; Metaphorical: weakness of proof or chain
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-istiṭrāf (Parenthetical Clarification) — The author interposes explanatory clauses between the main assertion and its qualification, as in "fa-huwa ḥasanun ʿinda Abī Dāwūd aw ṣaḥīḥun, fa-naḥkumu bi-al-qadri al-muḥaqqaq" where the apodosis is deferred until the condition is fully specified.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and grant them peace. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. To proceed:

This is an important treatise on the "Commentary on Sunan Abi Dawud" — may Allah have mercy upon him — in which I confine myself to the choicest of discourse, concerning what relates to its variant readings (lughāt), its expressions (alfāẓ), its chains of transmission (asānīd), and its subtleties (daqāʾiq); and the precise voweling (ḍabṭ) of whatever may be problematic among the expressions of the texts (mutūn) and the names; and indicating some of what is derived from the ḥadīth of legal rulings (aḥkām) and other matters; and drawing attention to the authenticity (ṣiḥḥah) of a ḥadīth, or its goodness (ḥusn), or its weakness (ḍuʿf); and clarifying the correctness of what differs among the manuscript copies. And with Allah is the success.
Section 1

We have related from Imam Abi Dawud — the author of the book, may Allah have mercy upon him — that he said: "I have mentioned in this book of mine the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and what resembles it and approaches it." And in another narration from him, its meaning being that he mentions in every chapter the most authentic (aṣaḥḥ) of what he knew in that chapter. And he said: "Whatever ḥadīth in my book contains severe weakness (wahn shadīd), I have indeed clarified it. And whatever I have not mentioned anything concerning, it is sound (ṣāliḥ) — and some of them are more authentic than others."

So upon this basis: whatever we find in the "Sunan Abi Dawud" that is not in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Ṣaḥīḥayn) or one of them, and no one whose opinion is relied upon has explicitly ruled on its authenticity or goodness, and Abu Dawud has not declared it weak — then it is ḥasan (good) according to Abu Dawud, or ṣaḥīḥ (authentic). So we rule by the certain measure (al-qadr al-muḥaqqaq): namely, that it is ḥasan. For if one whose opinion is relied upon has explicitly declared it weak, or the knowledgeable one sees in its chain (sanad) what necessitates weakness and there is no compensating factor (jābir) for it, we rule by its weakness.

And al-Ḥāfiẓ Abu ʿAbdillāh ibn Mandah has said: "Abu Dawud does transmit the weak chain (al-isnād al-ḍaʿīf) when he finds no other in the chapter, because it is stronger in his view than the opinion of men (raʾy al-rijāl)."

And know that there have occurred in the "Sunan Abi Dawud" ḥadīths of apparent weakness that he did not clarify, despite their being unanimously agreed upon as weak among the muḥaddithūn — such as the mursal (interrupted at the Companion level) and the munqaṭiʿ (broken chain), and his narration from an unknown (majhūl) person: such as "a shaykh" or "a man" and the like. So it may be said: This contradicts his statement: "Whatever contains severe weakness, I have clarified it!"
And its answer is: Since the weakness of this type is apparent, its very appearance sufficed in place of explicit clarification of it.

# وبعد:
# فهذا الكتاب النافع المفيد، كتاب "الأربعين النووية" للإمام النووي رحمه

الله, ومعها زيادات الحافظ ابن رجب رحمه الله, قام بتخريج أحاديثه والحكم

عليها، أخي في الله (الشربيني بن فايق الشربيني) حفظه الله، وبذا استزاد

نفع الكتاب وازدادت الفوائد منه, وقد نظرت في عمل أخي حفظه الله فألفيته

نافعا موفقا، ولله الحمد.
# فالله أسأل أن يزيده توفيقا وسدادا ومواصلة لطلب العلم الشرعي والدعوة

إلى الله.
# وصل اللهم على بينا محمد وسلم
# والحمد لله رب العالمين
# كتبه
# أبوعبد الله مصطفى بن العدوي

| AUTO مقدمة المحقق

# الحمد لله رب العالمين, والصلاة والسلام على رسولنا الأمين، وعلى آله

وصحبه أجمعين.
# أما بعد:
# فإن كتاب الأربعين للإمام النووي رحمه الله كتاب عظيم، نفع الله به

العباد في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها, وقد زاد الكتاب نفعا بما زاده الحافظ ابن

رجب الحنبلي رحمه الله، من تتمة لهذه الأحاديث، وكان من فضل الله عليا أن

يسر لي الاطلاع على هذا الكتاب فوجدت أنه على ما فيه من خير إلا أنه قد حوى

بعضا من الأحاديث الضعيفة، فاستعنت بالله تعالى وشرعت في الحكم على هذه

الأحاديث صحة وضعفا مع ذكر سبب الضعف مختصرا, ثم عرضت هذه الأحاديث على

فضيلة الشيخ مصطفى بن العدوي - حفظه الله - لتتم الفائدة.
# والله أرجو أن ينفع به العباد, وأن يرزقنا الإخلاص والقبول.
# وصل اللهم على نبينا محمد وسلم تسليما كثيرا
# والحمد لله رب العالمين

# وكتبه
# الشربيني بن فايق الشربيني
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

| CHECK [الأربعون النووية]

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of praising with gratitude; the act of commendation for beneficence.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥamd is praise (thanāʾ) for an act of voluntary beneficence (iḥsān ikhtiyārī), distinguished from mere madḥ (praise without necessary gratitude).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "أحمد الله بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical (majāz): "أحمدت الأرض" — found the land commendable for dwelling.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الابتداء بالحمد (Inaugural Praise Construction) — The basmala and ḥamdala serve as fixed formulaic openers (ṣīghāt) preceding the main discourse, functioning as detached nominative sentences (jumal ismiyyah) establishing the authorial frame.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
**Foreword**
All praise is due to Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah.
To proceed:

This is a beneficial and useful book — the book "The Forty Hadith" (al-Arbaʿūn al-Nawawiyyah) of Imam al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy upon him. With it are the additions (ziyādāt) of al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab, may Allah have mercy upon him. The one who undertook the verification of its hadiths (takhrīj) and the ruling upon them is my brother in Allah, al-Shirbīnī ibn Fāʾiq al-Shirbīnī, may Allah preserve him. By this, the benefit of the book increased, and the advantages derived from it multiplied. I have examined the work of my brother — may Allah preserve him — and found it beneficial and successful, and to Allah belongs all praise.
I ask Allah to increase him in success (tawfīq) and right guidance (sadād), and in perseverance in seeking sacred knowledge and calling to Allah.
O Allah, send blessings upon our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.

Written by:
Abū ʿAbdillāh Muṣṭafā ibn al-ʿAdawī
**The Verifier's Introduction**
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our trustworthy Messenger, and upon his family and all his companions.
To proceed:

Indeed, the Book of the Forty (al-Arbaʿūn) of Imam al-Nawawi — may Allah have mercy upon him — is a great book, by which Allah benefited His servants in the easts of the earth and its wests. And the book increased in benefit by what al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī — may Allah have mercy upon him — added to it, as a completion (tatimmah) of these hadiths. It was from Allah's grace upon me that He facilitated my access to this book, and I found that despite the good it contains, it nevertheless included some weak hadiths (aḥādīth ḍaʿīfah). So I sought the aid of Allah the Exalted and commenced ruling upon these hadiths as authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) or weak (ḍaʿīf), while mentioning the cause of weakness in brief. Then I presented these hadiths to his eminence, Shaykh Muṣṭafā ibn al-ʿAdawī — may Allah preserve him — to complete the benefit.
I hope from Allah that He benefits His servants through it, and that He grants us sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and acceptance (qabūl).
O Allah, send blessings upon our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, abundantly. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.

Written by:
al-Shirbīnī ibn Fāʾiq al-Shirbīnī
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
[The Forty Hadith of al-Nawawi] O Allah, send blessings upon our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, abundantly. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.

Written by:
al-Shirbīnī ibn Fāʾiq al-Shirbīnī
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
[The Forty Hadith of al-Nawawi]

paragraphs.text: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and from Him we seek aid.
**The Author's Introduction**

Praise be to God, the Creator of all made things, the Originator of all created beings, the Governor of all existent things, and the Disposer of speaking tongues — He who favored the Arabic language above all other languages, and who sent down His Book and dispatched His Messenger and Beloved, Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — with it, as an exaltation of its standing, and as an introduction to the greatness of its rank and the loftiness of its station. I praise Him with the most complete and perfect praise, with the purest and most comprehensive praise. And I bear witness that there is no god but God — the Subtle, the Generous, the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, His Beloved and His Intimate Friend — may God bless him and grant him peace — and upon all the other Prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous.
To proceed:

Since the Arabic language occupies the most exalted station and the highest rank — for by it is known the Book of the Lord of the Worlds, and the Sunnah of the best of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors, may God's blessings be upon him and upon all the Prophets and those who followed them in excellence until the Day of Judgment — therefore, those possessed of insight, pure souls, and refined exalted aspirations exerted their utmost efforts in attending to it, and in mastering it through the memorization of the poetry of the Arabs, their orations, their prose, and other aspects of their discourse. This attention existed during the era of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, notwithstanding their eloquence in lineage and abode, and their knowledge of the language through memorized proficiency. Rather, they sought to increase their acquisition of the language whose condition was as described.

# المؤلف: الإمام العلامة الفقيه الحافظ أبي زكريا محيي الدين بن شرف النووي
# عنيت بنشره وتصحيحه والتعليق عليه ومقابلة أصوله: شركة العلماء بمساعدة

إدارة الطباعة المنيرية
# يطلب من: دار الكتب العلمية، بيروت - لبنان
# عدد الأجزاء: 4
# [ترقيم الكتاب موافق للمطبوع]
# (تخريج الأحاديث وتخريج أسماء الرجال ل مصطفى عبد القادر عطا، وليست في

المطبوع) 

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وبه نستعين

| AUTO مقدمة المؤلف
# الحمد لله خالق المصنوعات، وبارىء البريات، ومدبر الكائنات، ومصرف الألسن

الناطقات، مفضل لغة العرب على سائر اللغات، المنزل كتابه والمرسل رسوله

وحبيبه محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بها تنويها بشأنها، وتعريفا بعظم

محلها وارتفاع مكانها، أحمده أبلغ الحمد وأكمله، وأزكاه وأشمله، وأشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله اللطيف الكريم، الرءوف الرحيم، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده

ورسوله، وحبيبه وخليله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وعلى سائر النبيين وآل كل

وسائر الصالحين، أما بعد:
# فإن لغة العرب لما كانت بالمحل الأعلى، والمقام الأسنى، وبها يعرف كتاب

رب العالمين، وسنة خير الأولين والآخرين، وأكرم السابقين واللاحقين، صلوات

الله عليه وعلى سائر النبيين والتابعين لهم بإحسان إلى يوم الدين، اجتهد

أولو البصائر والأنفس الزاكيات، والهمم المهذبة العاليات فى الاعتناء بها،

والتمكن من إتقانها بحفظ أشعار العرب وخطبهم ونثرهم، وغير ذلك من أمرهم،

وكان هذا الاعتناء فى زمن الصحابة، رضى الله عنهم، مع فصاحتهم نسبا ودارا،

ومعرفتهم باللغة استظهارا، لكن أرادوا الاستكثار من اللغة التى حالها ما

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise, commendation, and gratitude directed toward one who is worthy by virtue of inherent excellence or beneficence.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ḥamd (praise) is the acknowledgment of divine perfection and beneficence, distinct from mere shukr (thanksgiving) which is specific to favors received.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" (I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes). Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" (I deemed his deed praiseworthy) — extending the root to judgment of actions.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Creation, fashioning, measuring, and originating something with precise proportion and destiny.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes khalaqa (creation ex nihilo and from pre-existing matter) as divine origination (ījād) and estimation (taqdīr).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الله الخلق" (God created creation). Metaphorical: "خلق فلانًا" (He measured/fashioned him) — applied to character formation.
- Root: برأ (b-r-')
 * Lisan / Ayn: To create, originate, and bring forth from nothingness; also to cure and free from ailment.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bara'a specifically denotes creation of souls/living beings (al-nasamah) with soundness and freedom from defect — a nuance of divine origination of animate life.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "برأ الله النسمة" (God originated the soul). Metaphorical: "برأ من المرض" (recovered from illness) — the root's semantic field of purification and release.
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To manage, govern, and administer affairs; to consider the consequences of matters (from dubr, the rear/end).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tadbīr (governance) of God is His wise administration of creation toward its appointed ends, implying forethought and purposeful ordering.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "دبر الأمر" (he managed the affair). Metaphorical: "دبرت الريح" (the wind turned) — the root's extension to cyclical change and consequence.
- Root: صرف (ṣ-r-f)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, divert, change, and dispose; to vary and alternate.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taṣrīf (diversification) of tongues is God's act of making languages distinct and varied — a sign of His power and wisdom.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صرفته عن كذا" (I turned him away from something). Metaphorical: "صرف الدهر" (the vicissitudes of time) — the root's application to divine disposal of affairs.
- Root: فضل (f-ḍ-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, surplus, superiority, and excellence; that which remains beyond necessity.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Faḍl (grace/excellence) of God is His gratuitous bestowal of superiority — here, the pre-eminence of Arabic over all languages as a divine favor.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فضل الشيء" (the thing exceeded). Metaphorical: "فضل الله المؤمن على الكافر" (God favored the believer over the disbeliever) — the root's theological application to divine preference.
- Root: نزل (n-z-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To descend, alight, and settle; the act of coming down from a higher place.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tanzīl (sending down) of the Book is God's revelation of the Qur'an from the heavenly Preserved Tablet to the Prophet — a technical theological term for divine communication.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نزل من الجبل" (he descended from the mountain). Metaphorical: "نزل الله القرآن" (God sent down the Qur'an) — the root's established usage for revelation.
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: To send forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger dispatched with a message.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root's core is "انبعاث على التؤدة" (emission with deliberateness). The Messenger (rasūl) is one sent with a divine message — here, Muhammad as the bearer of God's revelation in Arabic.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" (God sent messengers among the nations). Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" (God loosed punishment upon them) — the root's extension to divine sending of both mercy and wrath.
- Root: محل (m-ḥ-l)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Place, station, rank, and position; that wherein something settles.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maḥall (station) here denotes the exalted rank and standing of the Arabic language — its ontological and epistemological primacy as the vehicle of revelation.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "المحل" (the place of alighting). Metaphorical: "فلان له محل رفيع" (so-and-so has an exalted station) — the root's extension to honorific rank.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure of the author's introduction employs extended prepositional phrases (e.g., "الحمد لله خالق المصنوعات...") where the governed noun is qualified by successive appositional and adjectival clauses, requiring careful parsing of the genitive chain (silsilat al-ijrā') to preserve the rhetorical cadence of the original.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and from Him we seek aid.
**The Author's Introduction**

Praise be to God, the Creator of all made things, the Originator of all created beings, the Governor of all existent things, and the Disposer of speaking tongues — He who favored the Arabic language above all other languages, and who sent down His Book and dispatched His Messenger and Beloved, Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — with it, as an exaltation of its standing, and as an introduction to the greatness of its rank and the loftiness of its station. I praise Him with the most complete and perfect praise, with the purest and most comprehensive praise. And I bear witness that there is no god but God — the Subtle, the Generous, the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, His Beloved and His Intimate Friend — may God bless him and grant him peace — and upon all the other Prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous.
To proceed:

Since the Arabic language occupies the most exalted station and the highest rank — for by it is known the Book of the Lord of the Worlds, and the Sunnah of the best of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors, may God's blessings be upon him and upon all the Prophets and those who followed them in excellence until the Day of Judgment — therefore, those possessed of insight, pure souls, and refined exalted aspirations exerted their utmost efforts in attending to it, and in mastering it through the memorization of the poetry of the Arabs, their orations, their prose, and other aspects of their discourse. This attention existed during the era of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, notwithstanding their eloquence in lineage and abode, and their knowledge of the language through memorized proficiency. Rather, they sought to increase their acquisition of the language whose condition was as described.

paragraphs.text: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
The Author's Introduction

Praise be to God, the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving, the Apportioner of all decrees (muqaddir al-aqdār), the Disposer of all affairs, Who wraps the night over the day — a lesson for those possessed of hearts and eyesights. He it is Who awakened from among His creation whom He chose, and admitted him into the company of the righteous (al-akhyār); and He granted success to whom He selected from among His servants, making him one of the pious (al-abrār); and He gave insight to whom He loved, causing them to renounce this abode, so that they strove earnestly for His good pleasure and made ready for the abode of permanence (dār al-qarār), and avoided what incurs His wrath, and took heed against the punishment of the Fire. They constrained their souls to diligence in His obedience and to constancy in His remembrance (dhikr) at evening and at dawn, and throughout the vicissitudes of circumstances in the hours of night and day — whereupon their hearts were illumined with the flashes of divine lights.

I praise Him with the most complete praise (aḥmaduhu ablagha al-ḥamd) for all His blessings, and I ask Him for increase from His bounty and His generosity. And I bear witness that there is no god but God, the Magnificent, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Ṣamad), the Mighty, the Wise. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, His chosen one, His beloved, and His intimate friend (khalīl) — the most excellent of all created beings, the most noble of all who have preceded and all who will come after. May the blessings of God and His peace be upon him, and upon all the prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous.

To proceed: God the Magnificent, the Mighty, the Wise has said: {«فاذكروني أذكركم»} ("So remember Me; I will remember you") [Al-Baqarah: 152]. And He, exalted be He, has said: {«وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون»} ("And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me") [Al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. By this it is known that among the most virtuous — or rather, the most virtuous — of the servant's states is his remembrance of the Lord of the worlds, and his occupation with the remembrances (adhkār) transmitted from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the master of the messengers.

Now, the scholars — may God be pleased with them — have composed numerous books on the practices of the day and night, on supplications (daʿawāt), and on remembrances (adhkār), well known among the learned. However, these works are lengthy due to their chains of transmission (asānīd) and repetition, and thus the aspirations of seekers have weakened before them. So I resolved to facilitate this matter for those who desire it, and I commenced the compilation of this book, condensing the objectives of what I have mentioned, to bring it near to those who give it their care. I omit the chains of transmission in most of it, for the reason I have stated — namely, my preference for brevity — and because this work is intended for devotees (mutʿabbidīn), who are not inclined toward knowledge of chains of transmission, but rather find them distasteful, however short they may be, save for a very few. And because the purpose of this book is the knowledge of the remembrances and acting upon them, and the clarification of their loci for those who seek guidance.

And I shall mention — God willing, exalted be He — in place of the chains of transmission, what is more important than them and what is generally lacking in such works: namely, the clarification of which hadiths are sound (ṣaḥīḥ), which are good (ḥasan), which are weak (ḍaʿīf), and which are rejected (munkar). For this is something whose knowledge is needed by all people, except for the rare few among hadith specialists. This is the most important matter that must be given care, and which the student verifies through the agency of the precise memorizers (ḥuffāẓ al-mutqinīn) and the trusted, penetrating imams. And I shall append to it — God willing, the Generous — a number of precious gems from the science of hadith, the subtleties of jurisprudence (fiqh), the important principles of the foundational rules (qawāʿid), the disciplines of the soul (riyāḍāt al-nufūs), and the etiquettes (ādāb) whose knowledge is emphatically incumbent upon those traversing the spiritual path (sālikīn).
And I shall present everything I mention in a clarified manner, such that its understanding is made easy for the common people and for those engaged in the study of jurisprudence alike.

paragraphs.text: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God for His abundant blessings, and gratitude to Him for the increase of His favors. And may blessings and peace be upon our Master and Beloved Muḥammad, who said: "My Lord disciplined me, and perfected my discipline." May God be well pleased with the noble Companions, who spared no effort in serving the Qur'an — nay, they expended their full capacity (wusʿahum) in actualizing what they were commanded. They compiled it after its dispersal and transmitted it from breasts (ṣudūr) to lines (suṭūr) — a matter not easily accomplished — so may God reward them on behalf of this Community with the best of rewards.
To proceed: God — exalted be He — has bestowed upon me a third honor (al-karāmah al-thālithah) by commissioning me to serve some of the works of this virtuous scholar [the author].
1. The first: *Bustān al-ʿĀrifīn* (The Garden of the Knowers), which investigates the most precious of treasures — narratives, wisdoms, and legal rulings.
2. The second: *Kitāb al-Fatāwā* (The Book of Legal Opinions), pertaining to the rights of God and the rights of servants — comprising acts of worship (ʿibādāt) and transactions (muʿāmalāt).

EPUB/chap_01.xhtml.title: The Etiquette of Associating with People — Section 1 (Introduction & Table of Contents)

paragraphs.text: In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

Praise be to God, with a praise that pleases Him, and His blessings upon Muḥammad, a prayer that elevates him and encompasses him. I ask God for assistance in devoting myself to it, and in listening attentively to it, and in being alerted to gratitude for it, and in gaining insight into its affair, and in proceeding in obedience to Him, and in excellence of conduct in dealing with Him. And that He make us — by His grace, through His mercy, from His bounty — among those whom He has granted a gift that is everlasting, not a loan that is returned. And that He send blessings upon His chosen Prophet and his family, and that He place us in his company through His mercy.

To proceed: The meaning of "associating with people" (mukhālaṭat al-nās) is: entering into mutual dealings with them, intermingling among them, and transacting with them through approach and mutual assistance. Its benefit: drawing nearer to God through them, and advancing oneself toward them. "The group" (al-zumrah): the congregation; the congregation of the believers in God.

It has reached me what transpired in the presence of the Shaykh — may God prolong his life — concerning the mention of associating with people and shunning them: that those present with him differed — some praising shunning (mujānabah), and some praising association (mukhālaṭah). Then they differed concerning friendship (al-ṣadāqah): whether its meaning has existence [in reality], or whether it is merely a verbal expression without a real referent — as one of the ancients said, when asked about the friend (al-ṣadīq): "It is a name without a meaning, an animal that does not exist." And if its meaning does have existence, is it [attainable]? For people have differed concerning friendship itself: some said it exists, and there are people living among us who could be friends to us. Others said: No, it does not exist in reality; it is merely a word in the language that has not translated into actual practice among people. And this is the second fundamental subject of this treatise.
It has been said that the impossible are three: the ghoul, the phoenix (ʿanqāʾ), and the true friend.
Abū Ḥayyān al-Tawḥīdī (d. 421 AH), a contemporary of al-Rāghib, has cited in his epistle on friendship and the friend a poem that touches upon these very questions:

1. Desired or shunned?
And even so, although people had differed about it before, far off is he who denied the virtue of the friend and did not acknowledge it or its merit.
So I desired to make this a book in which I mention the subtle points of what the learned and the wise have said, and to make it a gift — challenging thereby what al-Mutanabbī said:
"We have no horses to give you, nor wealth — so let speech prosper if fortune does not prosper."

And he — may God grant him success — in accepting that from me, even though it is from him that it is derived and to him that it returns. We have heard the name "friend" and demanded its meaning — so we sought out the friend. Do you think he exists on earth? But we find no path to him. Or do you see their saying "no friend" as a metaphor — you see beneath their words no reality?
And in this epistle of al-Tawḥīdī [it is related] that the one who posed this question was Rawḥ ibn Zinbāʿ.

So whoever [wishes] — let him gather from his garden bundles of sweet basil. And Ibn al-Rūmī has said: "I will surely thank the one who gives us from his speech that from him we derive its beauty and its eloquence." For God, Glorious and Exalted, thanks the doer of such a deed, reciting to him His revelation and His words. May God guard him and take care of him. For what is literature (adab) save through his care, and what is its currency save through his good guardianship? And the jewel, though it be an ornament to garments, is [valued] by the measure of one's desire for it.
The mention of the chapters:

Chapter One: On associating with people and withdrawing from them, and the virtue and blame of each.
Chapter Two: On love (al-maḥabbah), its types, and the causes that necessitate it.
Chapter Three: On the innate affinities (al-mashākil al-gharīziyyah) existing in man and in all other existents.
Chapter Four: On the detailed account of the beloved things, and clarifying which is from which.
Chapter Five: On the quiddity of love, intimate friendship (al-khullah), affection (al-mawaddah), friendship (al-ṣadāqah), and their sisters, and their soundness.
Chapter Six: On God's love for His servants and the servants' love for Him, and the mention of the intimate friendship (al-khullah) between Him and them, and the permissibility of using that [term] concerning Him.
Chapter Seven: On the disagreement of people concerning the acquisition of a friend.
Chapter Eight: On the virtue of acquiring him.
Chapter Nine: On the number of friends one ought to acquire.
Chapter Ten: On the conditions that a person observes in preferring and acquiring a friend.
Chapter Eleven: On the conditions that a person must fulfill for his friend and not demand from him.
Chapter Twelve: On living with the various classes of all people and associating with them.
End of the Table of Contents.

# 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

| مقدمة المؤلف
# الحمد لله الواحد القهار، العزيز الغفار، مقدر الأقدار، مصرف الأمور،

مكور الليل على النهار، تبصرة لذولي القلوب والأبصار، الذي أيقظ من خلقه

ومن اصطفاه فأدخله في جملة الأخيار، ووفق من اجتباه من عبيده فجعله من

الأبرار، وبصر من أحبه فزهدهم في هذه الدار، فاجتهدوا في مرضاته والتأهب

لدار القرار، واجتناب ما يسخطه والحذر من عذاب النار، وأخذوا أنفسهم بالجد

في طاعته وملازمة ذكره بالعشي والإبكار، وعند تغاير الأحوال في آناء الليل

والنهار، فاستنارت قلوبهم بلوامع الأنوار.
# أحمده أبلغ الحمد على جميع نعمه، وأسأله المزيد من فضله وكرمه، وأشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله العظيم، الواحد الصمد العزيز الحكيم، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده

ورسوله، وصفيه وحبيبه وخليله، أفضل المخلوقين، وأكرم السابقين واللاحقين،

صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعلى سائر النبيين، وآل كل وسائر الصالحين.
# أما بعد: فقد قال الله العظيم العزيز الحكيم: (فاذكروني أذكركم) [البقرة:

152] وقال تعالى: (وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعدون) [الذاريات: 56] فعلم

بهذا إن من أفضل - أو أفضل - حال العبد، ذكره لرب العالمين، واشتغاله

بالأذكار الواردة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد المرسلين.
# وقد صنف العلماء رضي الله عنهم في عمل اليوم والليلة والدعوات والأذكار

كتبا كثيرة معلومة عند العارفين، ولكنها مطولة بالأسانيد والتكرير، فضعفت

عنها همم الطالبين، فقصدت تسهيل ذلك على الراغبين، فشرعت في جمع هذا الكتاب

مختصرا مقاصد ما ذكرته تقريبا للمعتنين، وأحذف الأسانيد في معظمه لما ذكرته

من إيثار الاختصار، ولكونه موضوعا للمتعبدين، وليسوا إلى معرفة الأسانيد

(1) متطلعين، بل يكرهونه وإن قصر إلا الأقلين، ولأن المقصود به معرفة

الأذكار والعمل بها، وإيضاح 
# مظانها للمسترشدين، وأذكر إن شاء الله تعالى بدلا من الأسانيد ما هو أهم

منها مما يخل
# به غالبا، وهو بيان صحيح الأحاديث وحسنها وضعيفها ومنكرها (1) ، فإنه مما

يفتقر إلى معرفته جميع الناس إلا النادر من المحدثين، وهذا أهم ما يجب

الاعتناء به، وما يحققه الطالب من جهة الحفاظ المتقنين، والأئمة الحذاق

المعتمدين، وأضم إليه إن شاء الله الكريم جملا من النفائس من علم الحديث،

ودقائق الفقه، ومهمات القواعد، ورياضات النفوس، والآداب التي تتأكد معرفتها

على السالكين.
# وأذكر جميع ما أذكره موضحا بحيث يسهل فهمه على العوام والمتفقهين.

كتبا كثيرة معلومة عند العارفين، ولكنها مطولة بالأسانيد والتكرير، فضعفت

عنها همم الطالبين، فقصدت تسهيل ذلك على الراغبين، فشرعت في جمع هذا الكتاب

مختصرا مقاصد ما ذكرته تقريبا للمعتنين، وأحذف الأسانيد في معظمه لما ذكرته

من إيثار الاختصار، ولكونه موضوعا للمتعبدين، وليسوا إلى معرفة الأسانيد

(1) متطلعين، بل يكرهونه وإن قصر إلا الأقلين، ولأن المقصود به معرفة

الأذكار والعمل بها، وإيضاح 
# مظانها للمسترشدين، وأذكر إن شاء الله تعالى بدلا من الأسانيد ما هو أهم

منها مما يخل
# به غالبا، وهو بيان صحيح الأحاديث وحسنها وضعيفها ومنكرها (1) ، فإنه مما

يفتقر إلى معرفته جميع الناس إلا النادر من المحدثين، وهذا أهم ما يجب

الاعتناء به، وما يحققه الطالب من جهة الحفاظ المتقنين، والأئمة الحذاق

المعتمدين، وأضم إليه إن شاء الله الكريم جملا من النفائس من علم الحديث،

ودقائق الفقه، ومهمات القواعد، ورياضات النفوس، والآداب التي تتأكد معرفتها

على السالكين.
# وأذكر جميع ما أذكره موضحا بحيث يسهل فهمه على العوام والمتفقهين.

- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise, commendation, and gratitude directed toward one who is worthy by virtue of beneficence.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of divine perfection and beneficence, distinct from mere thanks (shukr), which is acknowledgment of a specific favor.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage — "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" (I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes); metaphorical extension — "أحمدت صنيعه" (I commended his deed), indicating praise directed at an act rather than the agent.
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and apportioning with precision.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When attributed to God, "power" (qudrah) signifies the negation of incapacity (ʿajz) from Him — absolute, unrestricted capability; when attributed to humans, it is always qualified and limited.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "الأمور تجري بقدر الله" (affairs run by God's decree); metaphorical — "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride), extending the root to spatial reach.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remembrance, recollection, and mindful invocation — the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance (dhikr) is the presence of a thing in the mind; when directed to God, it is the heart's attentive awareness of Him, and its highest form is the tongue's utterance coupled with heartfelt presence.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — remembrance as mental recall; metaphorical — "صاروا أحاديث" (they became [mere] tales), showing the extension of the root to transmitted speech.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between a preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic structure of the author's opening doxology.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
The Author's Introduction

Praise be to God, the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving, the Apportioner of all decrees (muqaddir al-aqdār), the Disposer of all affairs, Who wraps the night over the day — a lesson for those possessed of hearts and eyesights. He it is Who awakened from among His creation whom He chose, and admitted him into the company of the righteous (al-akhyār); and He granted success to whom He selected from among His servants, making him one of the pious (al-abrār); and He gave insight to whom He loved, causing them to renounce this abode, so that they strove earnestly for His good pleasure and made ready for the abode of permanence (dār al-qarār), and avoided what incurs His wrath, and took heed against the punishment of the Fire. They constrained their souls to diligence in His obedience and to constancy in His remembrance (dhikr) at evening and at dawn, and throughout the vicissitudes of circumstances in the hours of night and day — whereupon their hearts were illumined with the flashes of divine lights.

I praise Him with the most complete praise (aḥmaduhu ablagha al-ḥamd) for all His blessings, and I ask Him for increase from His bounty and His generosity. And I bear witness that there is no god but God, the Magnificent, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Ṣamad), the Mighty, the Wise. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, His chosen one, His beloved, and His intimate friend (khalīl) — the most excellent of all created beings, the most noble of all who have preceded and all who will come after. May the blessings of God and His peace be upon him, and upon all the prophets, and upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous.

To proceed: God the Magnificent, the Mighty, the Wise has said: {«فاذكروني أذكركم»} ("So remember Me; I will remember you") [Al-Baqarah: 152]. And He, exalted be He, has said: {«وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون»} ("And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me") [Al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. By this it is known that among the most virtuous — or rather, the most virtuous — of the servant's states is his remembrance of the Lord of the worlds, and his occupation with the remembrances (adhkār) transmitted from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the master of the messengers.

Now, the scholars — may God be pleased with them — have composed numerous books on the practices of the day and night, on supplications (daʿawāt), and on remembrances (adhkār), well known among the learned. However, these works are lengthy due to their chains of transmission (asānīd) and repetition, and thus the aspirations of seekers have weakened before them. So I resolved to facilitate this matter for those who desire it, and I commenced the compilation of this book, condensing the objectives of what I have mentioned, to bring it near to those who give it their care. I omit the chains of transmission in most of it, for the reason I have stated — namely, my preference for brevity — and because this work is intended for devotees (mutʿabbidīn), who are not inclined toward knowledge of chains of transmission, but rather find them distasteful, however short they may be, save for a very few. And because the purpose of this book is the knowledge of the remembrances and acting upon them, and the clarification of their loci for those who seek guidance.

And I shall mention — God willing, exalted be He — in place of the chains of transmission, what is more important than them and what is generally lacking in such works: namely, the clarification of which hadiths are sound (ṣaḥīḥ), which are good (ḥasan), which are weak (ḍaʿīf), and which are rejected (munkar). For this is something whose knowledge is needed by all people, except for the rare few among hadith specialists. This is the most important matter that must be given care, and which the student verifies through the agency of the precise memorizers (ḥuffāẓ al-mutqinīn) and the trusted, penetrating imams. And I shall append to it — God willing, the Generous — a number of precious gems from the science of hadith, the subtleties of jurisprudence (fiqh), the important principles of the foundational rules (qawāʿid), the disciplines of the soul (riyāḍāt al-nufūs), and the etiquettes (ādāb) whose knowledge is emphatically incumbent upon those traversing the spiritual path (sālikīn).
And I shall present everything I mention in a clarified manner, such that its understanding is made easy for the common people and for those engaged in the study of jurisprudence alike.

paragraphs.text: 5-Pillar Lexicographical Apparatus (AynEngine AI v4.0 Sovereign Edition)

- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to praise, commend, or laud someone for their virtues or beneficence; the opposite of ذم (blame).
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is specifically for beneficence (niʿmah) and virtue, distinguished from mere commendation (madh) which may lack genuine grounds; it is the acknowledgment of divine favor.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical (majāz): "أحمدت صنيعه" — I deemed his deed praiseworthy, extending the root to judgment of acts.
- Root: وسع (w-s-ʿ)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: breadth, capacity, expanse; to be wide or spacious.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Capacity (saʿah) applies to places, states, and acts like power and generosity; "وسع" denotes what exceeds the obligatory minimum, hence "لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها" {«لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا»}.
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial width. Metaphorical: "بذلوا وسعهم" — they exerted their full capacity/effort, a majāz transferring physical expanse to human endeavor.
- Root: صدر (ṣ-d-r)
 * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: the chest; front or beginning of a thing.
 * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Literally the bodily chest; metaphorically (istiʿārah) used for the forefront of anything — "صدر الكتاب" (the beginning of a book), "صدر المجلس" (head of a gathering).
 * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدروا عن الماء" — they returned from water. Metaphorical: "الأمور بصدورها" — matters by their beginnings; "من الصدور إلى السطور" — from breasts (memory) to lines (writing), a striking majāz pairing internal and external transmission.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a prepositional phrase from its governing element, permitting rhetorical fronting for emphasis, as in "حمدا لله" where the verbal noun (maṣdar) is fronted as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) to signal praise as the primary act.
English Scholarly Translation (Verbatim Authorial Voice)
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God for His abundant blessings, and gratitude to Him for the increase of His favors. And may blessings and peace be upon our Master and Beloved Muḥammad, who said: "My Lord disciplined me, and perfected my discipline." May God be well pleased with the noble Companions, who spared no effort in serving the Qur'an — nay, they expended their full capacity (wusʿahum) in actualizing what they were commanded. They compiled it after its dispersal and transmitted it from breasts (ṣudūr) to lines (suṭūr) — a matter not easily accomplished — so may God reward them on behalf of this Community with the best of rewards.
To proceed: God — exalted be He — has bestowed upon me a third honor (al-karāmah al-thālithah) by commissioning me to serve some of the works of this virtuous scholar [the author].
1. The first: *Bustān al-ʿĀrifīn* (The Garden of the Knowers), which investigates the most precious of treasures — narratives, wisdoms, and legal rulings.
2. The second: *Kitāb al-Fatāwā* (The Book of Legal Opinions), pertaining to the rights of God and the rights of servants — comprising acts of worship (ʿibādāt) and transactions (muʿāmalāt).
